Generative agents bring new expressive power to agent-based modeling, enabling simulations of collective social processes like cooperation, polarization, and norm formation. Yet they also introduce complexity through additional architectural choices, such as agent specification, memory representation, interaction protocols, and environment design. Small perturbations that appear minor to researchers can cascade into macro-level outcomes through repeated interaction, creating a "butterfly effect." Consequently, scientific claims drawn from LLM social simulations may reflect implementation artifacts rather than the social mechanisms being modeled. We support this position with two case studies: a repeated Prisoner's Dilemma and a social media echo chamber simulation. Across multiple models, minor perturbations in persona format and game-instruction framing shift cooperation rates by up to 76 percentage points, while network homophily and hub assignment produce significant and consistent shifts in polarization metrics. We also find that sensitivity is unevenly distributed across both architectural choices and model families: the same perturbation that produces the 76 pp shift in one frontier model only shifts another by 1 pp. Robustness is therefore a property that should be measured per claim and per model, not assumed. To address this validation gap, we introduce TRAILS (Taxonomy for Robustness Audits In LLM Simulations), a robustness-audit taxonomy spanning three levels of simulation design: agent (micro-level), interaction (meso-level), and system (macro-level). We call for robustness to become a first-order validation requirement before LLM social simulations are used to explain mechanisms, evaluate interventions, or inform decisions.

items.title: An Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator for coupled surrogate morphodynamic modelling
items.summary: Morphodynamic simulations require repeated coupling between hydrodynamic solvers, sediment transport modules, and bed updating. For long duration, multi-scenario simulations on large unstructured meshes, such coupling is computationally demanding. This study proposes an Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator (AH-GNO) that formulates bed evolution as a graph operator learning problem from recent hydrodynamic and topographic states to predict future bed elevation increments. The model operates directly on the native unstructured meshes. The approach integrates area-weighted graph learning, historical state selection, and forecast horizon estimation, allowing the effective history length (K) and update interval (B) to vary with the evolving flow and bed state. Using Telemac2D/GAIA solutions as supervised numerical references, the framework is evaluated on the official Bump and Yen bend benchmarks and on a field-scale application (Waiho River, New Zealand). Results show that the AH-GNO reproduces the main patterns of bedform migration, bend-scale erosion and deposition, and localized bed adjustment. Across the three cases, the tested CPU-GPU deployment reduced post-training bed-update workflow time from 12~1204 s with GAIA to 0.08~3.34 s with AH-GNO. This improvement corresponds to deployment-specific accelerations of approximately 150~360 times relative to 4-core GAIA CPU configurations, and with 105~186 times gains for 20-core CPU configurations. These results suggest that, while retaining hydrodynamic feedback from TELEMAC-2D, a learned operator for bed updating can provide an efficient acceleration component for morphodynamic scenario analysis and rapid coupled simulation.

items.title: Emergent Entropic Forces Drive Inverse and Reentrant Phase Transitions in Condensates of Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
items.summary: We present a phenomenological, mean-field model for condensates of intrinsically disordered proteins that describes inverse phase transitions and qualitatively predicts reentrant phase behavior as a function of salt concentration. The model is based on a matrix-based formulation of the Flory-Huggins free energy, in which the enthalpic interaction parameter and the protein valence, defined here as the number of effective "sticky patches", are treated as free parameters. Its central insight is that integrating out dynamics of fast-moving molecular species generates an effective entropic force that increases the free-energy barrier to mixing, even within a mean-field description. We account for this by linking Gaussian integration of co-solutes to the Schur complement of the matrix-based Flory-Huggins free energy. This provides a general thermodynamic framework illustrating how enthalpic interactions that increase the number of available microstates necessarily induce effective entropic forces. We demonstrate the expressiveness and predictive power of the model by qualitatively reproducing recent experimental observations on the rabies virus phosphoprotein.

items.title: Tandem jets in crossflow: a one-parameter dilution law for the trajectory and the velocity decay
items.summary: The front jet of a tandem pair in crossflow is not passive. This paper treats the mean-flow phenomenology and its scaling; the mechanism is left to the companion paper. In 40\ kHz time-resolved PIV measurements covering nine spacing--velocity-ratio conditions ($L=2d$, $3d$, $4d$; $r\approx3$, $5$, $7$) and a single-jet baseline, the front-jet $rd$-normalized trajectory lies below the single-jet reference in every condition (near-field segment up to 40\% shorter), while the shielded rear jet rises above the reference in eight of the nine and penetrates $1.4$--$2.0$ times deeper than the front jet. The mean pressure and reverse-flow statistics are inconsistent with the two classical explanations: the inter-jet region is pressurized rather than sub-atmospheric, the lateral pressure difference across the front jet is weakened rather than enhanced (within reconstruction uncertainty), and the reverse-flow region does not follow the ordering of the modification. In natural coordinates the centerline decay re-scales onto the single-jet law at the effective velocity ratio (seven of nine within 18\%), so bending and decay are two readouts of one dilution, which whole-trajectory matching condenses into the one-parameter law $r_{\mathrm{eff}}/r=r/(r+c)$, $c=3.31$, with the velocity ratio as the primary control and the spacing entering through the near-field capacity ($c_h=2.50$--$3.30$). The law has one fitted constant and needs only the single-jet reference family; leave-one-condition-out predictions reproduce each held-out condition within 15\%, so the procedure is portable to any tandem array in which the gap recirculation closes.

items.title: Metasurface engineering of transient photothermal responses for vibrational imaging at living interfaces
items.summary: Chemical transformations at biological interfaces are central to cellular function, yet the weak vibrational signals associated with subtle molecular changes limit their spatially resolved observation. Here, we present metasurface-driven mid-infrared photothermal imaging (MetaMIP), which uses resonantly engineered metasurfaces to amplify molecular temperature modulation while retaining rapid thermal recovery. Visible-light detection converts this response into submicrometre maps of individual nanoparticles and biological cells. In living cells, MetaMIP resolves spatially distinct chemical changes during enzymatic lipid conversion across the cell membrane. These results demonstrate the potential of engineered photothermal interfaces for mapping chemical composition and tracking its evolution during reactions.

items.title: Second-harmonic generation from an optically levitated KTP nanocrystal in vacuum
items.summary: The optically levitated system in vacuum has emerged as a powerful platform for studies of fundamental physics and precision measurements. Although various nanoparticles have been successfully levitated in vacuum, they typically lack the capability to support optical nonlinear processes. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the stable levitation of a potassium titanyl phosphate (KTP) nonlinear nanocrystal in vacuum and investigate its second-harmonic generation (SHG) properties. This levitated system intrinsically provides a pristine dark-background environment with a high signal-to-noise ratio. The trapping laser simultaneously serves as a fundamental light for efficient SHG. Moreover, the polarization of the collected SHG signal is correlated with that of the fundamental laser, providing clear evidence of the optical torque enabling controllable alignment of the nanocrystal with the driving field. Our work establishes a new route, to our knowledge, toward exploring nonlinear optical processes in vacuum levitation systems and designing novel nanodevices with high manipulation agility in a fully contact-free environment.

items.title: Opinion dynamics on switching networks
items.summary: We study opinion dynamics over a two-layer multiplex network with weighted, directed influence and reciprocal links. Within each layer, an agent weighs its neighbors equally, so the influence of a neighbor is inversely proportional to the agent's number of neighbors in that layer. Agents update their opinions over time to coordinate with their neighbors. However, the frequency of agents' interactions with neighbors in different network layers differs: one layer is always active, whereas the other one is active only once every $k$ time steps. Consequently, the multiplex network's adjacency matrices are time-varying. We characterize how the activation frequency of the second layer impacts the convergence of the opinion dynamics process. Without requiring agents to place positive weight on their own opinions, we prove that, for every activation period $k$, the opinions reach a consensus whose value depends on $k$, and that the asymptotic per-step convergence factor equals the $k$th root of the second-largest eigenvalue modulus of the one-period transition matrix. As $k$ grows, this factor generically converges to that of the always-active layer when this layer is connected; when it is disconnected, the time to consensus generically grows linearly in $k$. Numerical experiments on 1,000 random multiplex networks confirm these results.

items.title: Alignment-Free Optical Combining with Scalar-Message Expectation Propagation Detection for Distributed Multi-Aperture Coherent Reception
items.summary: We propose an alignment-free distributed multi-aperture optical receiver with a single coherent front end, in which the differential delays between apertures are large. The branch signals are optically combined without inter-branch delay or phase alignment. Large differential delays produce separated tap clusters, forming a sparse ISI channel with long memory. Scalar-message expectation propagation exploits this sparsity to recover the transmitted symbols. Simulations show lower BER than equal-area single-aperture reception and no clear BER degradation over the tested delay spans. As the maximum differential delay increases from 100.5 to 200.5 symbol periods, the channel span nearly doubles, while the factor-graph edge count increases by only about 1.5\%. The trade-off is higher BER than ideal coherent combining schemes in exchange for fewer coherent front ends than digital combining and no inter-branch delay or phase alignment before optical combining.

items.title: Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation
items.summary: The co-condensation of DNA and proteins plays an important role in genome compaction, including heterochromatin formation and chromosome segregation. Meanwhile, transcription and replication continuously generate DNA supercoiling, yet how the resulting torsional stress affects co-condensation remains poorly understood. Here, by coupling DNA elasticity to a protein concentration field, we show that supercoiling acts as a topological catalyst for co-condensation through a mutually reinforcing interplay with protein wetting. Specifically, protein wetting facilitates twist-to-writhe conversion, generating highly writhed DNA conformations that in turn promote capillary collapse into a protein-rich droplet. In the absence of supercoiling, DNA remains kinetically trapped in metastable extended states within our model, whereas sufficiently strong supercoiling removes the nucleation barrier and enables spontaneous co-condensation. These results establish topology as a distinct control parameter for biomolecular condensation and provide a mechanical framework for how active genomic processes can dynamically regulate large-scale genome organization.

items.title: Quantum theory of molecular orientation
items.summary: We formulate a quantum phase space for rotational and nuclear-spin states of rigid molecules. For each nuclear spin isomer, we re-derive the isomer's admissible angular momentum states from molecular geometry and nuclear-spin data, introduce its angular position states using quantization theory, and develop a generalized Fourier transform converting between the two. We classify molecules into three types -- asymmetric, rotationally symmetric, and perrotationally symmetric -- with the last type having no macroscopic analogue due to nuclear-spin statistics constraints. We discuss two general features in perrotationally symmetric state spaces that are Hamiltonian-independent and induced solely by symmetry and spin statistics. First, we quantify when and how an isomer's state space is completely rotation-spin entangled, meaning that it does not admit any separable states. Second, we identify isomers whose position states house an internal pseudo-spin or "fiber" degree of freedom, and the fiber's Berry phase or matrix after adiabatic changes in position yields naturally robust operations, akin to braiding anyonic quasiparticles or realizing fault-tolerant quantum gates. We outline how the fiber can be used as a quantum error-correcting code and discuss scenarios where these features can be experimentally probed

items.title: Efficient third-harmonic generation in high-Q tantalum pentoxide microcavities
items.summary: Nonlinear harmonic generation in microcavities offers a compelling route toward energy efficient on-chip short-wavelength coherent light sources, enabled by tight optical confinement within compact mode volumes and flexible dispersion engineering. Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) photonic platforms are particularly promising for realizing such nonlinear processes: their broad transparency window (280-8000 nm) supports broadband operation, their large bandgap suppresses two-photon absorption, and their thick-film deposition capability enables dispersion management--features that can collectively enhance the performance of nonlinear light sources. Here, we demonstrate, to the best of our knowledge, the first efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) in high-Q Ta2O5 microcavities. These microcavities feature smooth surfaces and high loaded Q factors up to 2.67X10^6, thereby facilitating nonlinear interactions. Through dispersion engineering, efficient THG is realized in both suspended microdisks and monolithic microrings under telecom-band continuous-wave laser pumping, as confirmed by optical spectra, visible-light microscopy, and the near-cubic pump-power dependence of the conversion efficiency. This work lays a foundation for chip-scale f-3f self-referencing of frequency combs and next-generation integrated nonlinear photonics.

items.title: Deep-Learning Identification and Global Characterization of Energetic O2+ Beams at Mars
items.summary: Martian ionospheric ions can be accelerated away from Mars by the solar wind, contributing substantially to atmospheric ion escape. Here, we develop a U-Net-based image segmentation model to identify a distinct population of escaping planetary ions, energetic O2+ beams, from a decade of Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN (MAVEN) observations and perform an event-based statistical analysis of their global properties and dependence on external conditions. We find that O2+ beams are widely distributed throughout the Martian plasma environment, with a strong preference for the +E hemisphere, where the solar wind convective electric field points away from Mars. This pronounced spatial asymmetry indicates that the convective electric field plays a major role in beam formation. In the solar wind and magnetosheath, these beams are consistent with the plume. Their occurrence-weighted flux agrees with previous long-term plume estimates, whereas the flux during identified beam intervals is substantially higher. This highlights the advantage of our event-based approach in capturing the intrinsic properties of O2+ plumes. In the induced magnetotail, beam formation remains strongly associated with the convective electric field, while the Hall electric field can provide additional energization. The beam properties are primarily controlled by upstream solar wind conditions, with no apparent influence from solar extreme ultraviolet irradiance. These results might improve our understanding of ion escape at Mars. More broadly, we also demonstrate the potential of deep learning for identifying transient plasma populations from spacecraft observations.

items.title: Superheating field of clean superconductors near the type-I--type-II boundary: the low-temperature Meissner stability limit of niobium
items.summary: We calculate the low-temperature superheating field $B_{\rm sh}$ of clean superconductors near the boundary between type-I and type-II superconductivity, with particular emphasis on Nb. Ginzburg--Landau theory is not applicable at low temperatures, while previous microscopic calculations have been limited to either the large-$κ$ regime or the dirty limit. The clean, low-$κ$ regime relevant to Nb has therefore remained unresolved. We solve the self-consistent nonlinear nonlocal Eilenberger problem for the Meissner state and then analyze its stability against small perturbations. For a Nb-like material with $κ_{\rm GL}=0.7$, we obtain $B_{\rm sh}\simeq 290\,{\rm mT}$ at $T/T_c=0.2$, using $B_{c0}\simeq 200\,{\rm mT}$. For a TESLA-shaped Nb accelerator cavity, this corresponds to an intrinsic Meissner-stability limit of about $67\,{\rm MV/m}$.

items.title: Thouless Pumping of One-Dimensional Dark Solitons and Domain Walls
items.summary: We predict that quantized transport of dark solitons and domain walls can be observed in mutually sliding optical lattices in both focusing and defocusing nonlinear materials. Two different classes of underlying periodic backgrounds are considered here -- unstaggered and staggered -- which are accurately represented, respectively, by the in-phase and out-of-phase trains of Wannier functions. The nonlinear excitations formed on top of these backgrounds -- dark solitons and domain walls -- are sustained by defocusing or focusing Kerr nonlinearities of the optical medium. Despite non-zero asymptotics, dark solitons and domain walls can still undergo quantized topological transport in dynamically changing refractive index landscape when they and background on which they are constructed are dynamically stable. The extended intervals of propagation constants (and, correspondingly, of the background amplitude) and lattice depths, where stable quantized transport occurs, are identified for both dark solitons and domain walls. Outside these intervals, the quantized transport regime is found to be unstable. Our results extend the concept of nonlinear topological transport from bright to dark soliton states.

items.title: Global non-equilibrium thermodynamics of stationary states applied to the Rayleigh-Bénard convection
items.summary: Classical thermodynamics describes physical systems in thermodynamic equilibrium, characterized in particular by the absence of macroscopic motion. Global non-equilibrium thermodynamics extends this framework to include physical systems in stationary states (Hołyst et al., EPL 149, 30001 (2025)). Here, we demonstrate that this extended theory captures macroscopic motion in stationary states, thereby providing a unified framework for global thermodynamics and fluid mechanics. We apply the theory to stationary Rayleigh-Bénard convection and show how the second law of global non-equilibrium thermodynamics determines the direction of changes in fluid motion.

items.title: Number Theory of Decaying Turbulence 2: The Energy Spectrum and the Riemann Zeta Zeros
items.summary: The odd Euler ensemble, the locally stable attractor of the momentum-loop dynamics of freely decaying incompressible turbulence, has a self-similar energy spectrum \(E(k,t)=L^{-3/2}H(kL)\), \(L\sim\sqrt{\tildeνt}\), which does not depend on the dimension of space. We compute its scaling function as a Mellin--Barnes integral whose amplitude contains the ratio \(ζ(p+15/2)/ζ(p+17/2)\) of Riemann zeta functions; the odd ensemble differs from the even one by a prime-\(2\) Euler factor. The integral is evaluated by deforming the contour to Lefschetz thimbles. The non-trivial zeros of \(ζ(s)\) generate a vertical wall of complex poles. As \(ξ=\log(k\sqrt{\tildeνt})\) increases, the thimble traps them in a Stokes staircase, first collectively and then a few at a time, and Berry smoothing turns each trapping into an analytic activation of an exponentially small oscillatory term. Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis and simplicity of the zeros, all these poles lie on one wall and their activations accumulate only at infinite time: the spectrum is analytic at every finite time and has an essential singularity at \(t=\infty\). The same analysis gives the second-order structure function, whose index falls continuously from \(2\) to \(0\) without an inertial plateau, and the decay laws, energy \(\propto t^{-5/4}\) and enstrophy \(\propto t^{-9/4}\). The operator representation and the stability of the Euler ensemble are derived in the first paper of this series, and the comparison with simulations and experiments is given in the third.

items.title: Laser with $7\times10^{-18}$ stability
items.summary: We report a laser with record frequency stability, based on a 21 cm cryogenic silicon cavity. For best short-term stability, the cavity operates at 6 K to minimize Brownian thermal noise and achieves a fractional stability of $7\times10^{-18}$ between 2 to 50 s of averaging time and 2.5 mHz linewidth. For best long-term stability the cavity operates at 16 K, where silicon has a zero-crossing of thermal expansion. Slightly increased thermal noise limits the performance to $9\times10^{-18}$, consistent with the expected temperature scaling, but the long-term performance is improved. The laser then has a linewidth of 2.9 mHz and long-term frequency drift less than 4 μHz s$^{-1}$. The laser is used to enhance the performance of a state-of-the-art Sr lattice clock, operating with Rabi and Ramsey interrogation times beyond 10 s.

items.title: First Results of Calculation of the Dayside Magnetopause Reconnection Rate with TRACERS
items.summary: Quantifying the rate of reconnection remains a key challenge in the study of geomagnetic storms. In this study, we present the first results from the new Tandem Reconnection and Cusp Electrodynamics Reconnaissance Satellites (TRACERS) mission to calculate the reconnection rate from dispersed ion populations measured in the cusp, using previously developed methodology. We study ion dispersion events in two storms. During the first storm, which occurred on September 30, 2025, 21 dispersion events were identified in TRACERS 2 ion data as a combined result of geospace dynamics and the spacecraft cusp encounters. Throughout this time when ion dispersion was detected by TRACERS , the reconnection rate is calculated and is shown to track reasonably well with another measure of geomagnetic activity, the Cross Polar Cap Potential (CPCP) as obtained by the Super Dual Auroral Radar Network (SuperDARN). The dispersions are correlated with the smoothed CPCP, and a correlation of $r^2=0.62$ was found using the dispersions from the onset and main phase of the storm. The correlation disappears when including dispersions from the recovery period. The distribution of reconnection rates throughout this storm lies generally between 0.1 - 1.5 mV/m, slightly lower than previous reconnection rates calculated with DMSP, but consistent with in-situ observations made with Polar. In this work, we also apply a previously developed automatic identification algorithm for ion-energy cusp dispersion to TRACERS, with the intent that it may serve as a tool for future statistical analysis as the data volume becomes too large to manually review.

items.title: Concentration-Dependent Speciation in ZnCl2 Electrolyte Solutions: Transferability of Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials and Speciation Sensitivity of EXAFS
items.summary: Predicting speciation in concentrated electrolytes requires accurate ion interactions and adequate sampling of slowly interconverting coordination environments. We combine Zn K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) measurements with long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) using machine-learning interatomic potentials to study aqueous ZnCl2 from dilute conditions to 30 m. We train revPBE-based DeepMD models with D3 corrections included or excluded for Zn-containing pairs and compare them with DPMD-SCAN, classical MD (CMD), and MACE-MATPES-r2SCAN. EXAFS calculations are benchmarked against hydrated and chloride-coordinated Zn reference complexes, then applied to MD ensembles alongside Zn-Cl coordination free-energy analysis. Increasing concentration reduces octahedral coordination, replaces water with chloride, and promotes chloride-bridged association. All three DeepMD models yield similar EXAFS at 3 m, but DPMD-SCAN shows greater transferability across concentrations, reproducing measured spectral trends, key features of mixed ZnCl2/LiCl spectra, and octahedral fractions consistent with other studies. DFT treatment strongly affects coordination free energies and aggregation; excluding Zn-related D3 corrections does not systematically improve EXAFS agreement. CMD shows larger spectral discrepancies and less consistent coordination trends. MACE-MATPES-r2SCAN improves upon CMD and yields spectra comparable to DPMD-SCAN, which provides more consistent agreement and greater computational efficiency. Neighbor-resolved analysis shows that distance disorder and scattering-path interference can produce similar EXAFS signatures for distinct coordination ensembles, highlighting the need for rigorous sampling and ensemble-averaged spectra to distinguish isolated from chloride-bridged Zn species.

items.title: CARS: a centerline-anchored attention surrogate for coronary blood flow on skeleton-generated lumen geometries
items.summary: When the parameter of a PDE surrogate is the flow domain itself, the key/value set of an attention model must encode that domain. We present CARS (Coronary Artery Rapid Surrogate), a learned surrogate for the finite-volume solution map of the steady incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on coronary lumens built from image-derived centerlines. CARS maps a centerline with per-point lumen radius and a scalar inlet flow rate to pressure and velocity at arbitrary query points. The attention focal set is the case's own centerline, so geometry fusion costs $O(N n_f)$ rather than $O(N^2)$ in the number of evaluation points. Trained per territory on $2{,}700$ OpenFOAM solutions with synthetic focal lesions, CARS reaches relative $\ell_2$ errors of $0.120/0.149$ (pressure/velocity) on left-coronary and $0.063/0.119$ on right-coronary test sets, in $87$~ms per case against a solver wall-clock of $572$-$1{,}063$~s. It outperforms four parameter-matched neural operators, and accuracy saturates eightfold below the operating focal count. Fractional flow reserve derived from the predicted pressure matches the CFD label at Pearson $r = 0.941/0.993$ and reproduces the $\mathrm{FFR}\le 0.8$ decision in $97.7\%/96.3\%$ of held-out cases. The predicted velocity does not satisfy continuity closely enough for derived quantities, and the weights are territory-specific.

items.title: Two-Laser Heterodyne Detection System for ALPS II
items.summary: The Any Light Particle Search II employs a highly sensitive heterodyne detection system to measure an ultra-weak electromagnetic field that is reconverted from axions inside a regeneration cavity (RC). The initial design of the heterodyne system utilized a local oscillator laser (LO) that was resonant with the RC to form an interference beatnote with the weak signal field exiting the cavity. A weakness of this design is that it is possible for the out-of-mode field component of the LO to be larger than the in-mode component, allowing its noise to dominate the optical component of the noise budget and reducing the SNR of the experiment. This problem can be addressed by introducing a second, non-resonant laser as the LO. Since the in-mode light of this laser does not couple to the cavity, significantly more of its power is reflected than when the LO is resonant. We present a model for the measurement noise that predicts these design changes increase the SNR by a factor of roughly 35. This model was then confirmed experimentally by injecting a weak signal to the RC and examining the difference in the sensitivity of the detection system in each of these configurations.

items.title: Orientation-selective microwave heating of laser-graphitized diamond at 2.45 GHz
items.summary: Pristine diamond couples negligibly to a 2.45 GHz field. We show that femtosecond-laser inscription of a buried graphitic (sp2) architecture makes a 4 x 4 x 2 mm^3 N-doped (100 ppm) high-pressure high- temperature (HPHT) crystal absorb strongly, and that the absorption is switched by the orientation of the inscribed structure relative to the cavity electric field. With the 1.8 mm depth of a concentric grating along E, stepped power gave a smooth staircase to an indicated ~500C at 80 W followed, at 90 W, by an abrupt excursion to an indicated ~900C with surface roughening and terraced oxidation. Rotating the same sample so that the grating diameter lay along E, and an unmodified crystal in either orientation, gave no signal above the ~40C floor. We account for this by the depolarisation factors L of the sub-wavelength tracks, collapsed into one screening parameter S = Lσ/(ωε0εh), here, σ conductivity, ω - cyclic frequency, εh,0 - permittivity of host and vacuum, respectively. The model turns element length, diameter and writing regime into design variables for microwave absorption in a transparent host.

items.title: Linear and nonlinear stability of rate-and-state faults
items.summary: Models of faults incorporating slip rate- and state-dependent friction have reproduced phenomena from spontaneous slow, aseismic slip to earthquake-generating dynamic rupture. Numerical explorations of model parameter space show sudden transitions in behavior. However these boundaries are poorly constrained analytically, with commonly used scalings derived assuming unrepresentative conditions of uniform sliding on an infinite, homogeneous fault. In this work, we demonstrate that an analysis of linear stability can reflect model conditions. We examine two scenarios that move beyond the classical case: an asperity driven by the steady creep of its surroundings, and a finite fault experiencing a constant rate of shear loading. We identify the critical fault dimension $L_c$ at which point linear stability is lost. Beyond this linear regime, the non-linear nature of the friction law implies the loss of memory of loading conditions as instability progresses and the existence of universal solutions describing this process. We refine prior analyses of this non-linear instability and find the minimum fault size that can support self-sustaining, unstable acceleration towards dynamic rupture. We examine the role of the state evolution law and delineate conditions under which faults may be linearly stable but non-linearly unstable, requiring finitely large perturbations to trigger instability. For both the linear and non-linear analysis, we consider scenarios of two- and three-dimensional deformation. On the basis of numerical solutions, approximate but accurate algebraic expressions for the transition boundaries are presented. These results provide means for careful model design and to delimit plausible regions of parameter space when considering physical observations of stable creep, aseismic (slow slip) or seismic transients.

items.title: Suppression of Grain Boundary Nitrogen Degradation by Boron in Superalloys
items.summary: Superalloys enable the hottest sections of jet engines to operate at high temperatures, but environmentally assisted degradation limits their lifetime. In polycrystalline alloys, nitrogen penetrates beneath the protective surface oxides, to produce embrittling grain boundary nitrides. Boron is added in trace amounts to improve grain boundary strength, yet its role, if any, in oxidation-related degradation remains unclear. Here we show that boron segregates to an internal nitride--matrix interface in a Ni/Co-base $γ$/$γ^{\prime}$ strengthened superalloy. Both B-free and B-containing alloys develop stratified chromia/alumina scales at 800~$^{\circ}$C in \SI{100}{\hour}, but the B-free variant produces larger, deeper and more elongated Ti/Nb-rich subsurface grain boundary nitrides. Correlative 4D S/TEM and atom probe tomography identify the particle as a chemically complex B1 nitride and reveal interfacial boron segregation. This shows that trace alloying as an alloy strategy can control damaging internal reaction product precipitation and growth by core-shell segregation.

items.title: Unified Projection-Domain Material Decomposition for Energy-Integrating and Photon-Counting CT
items.summary: Objective: To develop a unified and efficient method for projection-domain material decomposition in spectral computed tomography (CT) that incorporates an arbitrary number of spectral measurements, independent of the acquisition mechanism, without reducing the measurements to two effective energies. Approach: A nested optimization method was developed for two-material basis decomposition from K>=2 spectral measurements. It extends an existing two-measurement univariate method by replacing its polynomial approximation with profile minimization of the Poisson negative log-likelihood, reducing the inversion to two one-dimensional searches that use all measurements without spectral rebinning. The method was evaluated in simulation for energy-integrating (GE Revolution Apex Elite, Siemens SOMATOM Flash) and photon-counting (Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha) CT. Main results: The method recovered line integrals with noiseless iodine errors below 3e-6 g/cm^2 and noise within 3% of the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB). Virtual monoenergetic images (VMIs) agreed, at 70 keV and above, with reference CT numbers and, on all three systems, with vendor VMIs of physical scans (mean absolute error 6-22 HU). For photon counting, four measurements instead of two reduced the iodine CRLB by 19% and image noise by 8-16% at every VMI energy, and lowered the regression error at 70 keV and above. Iteration and tolerance settings changed CT numbers by less than 0.04 HU, and decomposition took 0.34-0.67 s per million rays on an A100 GPU. Significance: The method provides fast, accurate decomposition for any spectral CT acquisition mechanism and number of measurements, so one method can serve every scanner in a virtual imaging trial.

items.title: Comparing local and global optimization reveals untapped hybrid potentials for machine learning-based inverse planning
items.summary: Machine learning (ML) models for normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) can be embedded directly into inverse treatment planning, but the resulting optimization problems are generally nonconvex, and the choice between global and local optimization involves a trade-off between optimality guarantees and computational cost. Two open-source frameworks for ML-based inverse planning were compared: OptiCL (global mixed-integer optimization via constraint learning) and pyanno4rt (local nonlinear optimization via end-to-end differentiation). Logistic regression, linear support vector machine, and feed-forward neural network NTCP models for grade 2+ xerostomia and grade 2+ radiation pneumonitis were embedded. Plan optimization was performed for eight head-and-neck (HN) photon cases and seven lung proton cases. The plans were compared by target coverage, OAR dose metrics, spatial dose agreement, post-hoc predicted NTCP, and runtime. A projection-based gradient approximation was introduced to embed decision trees. In addition to that, warm-starting, constraint strengthening, and pruning were investigated as hybrid strategies for combining local and global optimization. Comparing OptiCL and pyanno4rt across the HN and lung treatment plans revealed broadly consistent dose distributions. Mean differences (OptiCL}$-$pyanno4rt [95% CI]) were small: for HN cases, -0.16 Gy [-0.37, 0.06] (parotid) and -0.00 Gy [-0.01, 0.00] (PTV); for lung cases, -0.52 Gy [-1.10, 0.06] (total lung) and -0.04 Gy [-0.07, -0.01] (PTV). Mean NTCP differences amounted to -0.08 p.p. [-0.49, 0.33] (HN) and -1.73 p.p. [-2.68, -0.77] (lung). OptiCL tended toward lower OAR doses and predicted NTCP, but required higher wall-clock runtime. Hybridization of the decision tree-based HN plan eliminated 80% of binary decision variables without compromising plan quality.

items.title: Fixed-Dimensional Latent Flow for Generating Variable-Size 3D Molecules
items.summary: Molecular size is intrinsically linked to composition, structure, and properties, but most 3D molecular generators treat size as a predefined input rather than a quantity to be generated. We introduce Equivariant-Free Transformer-Autoencoded Latent Flow Matching, a two-stage framework that samples a fixed-dimensional latent vector using flow matching and employs an autoregressive Transformer to determine molecular size, atom types, coordinates, and chemical attributes. Canonical atom ordering and rigid-pose alignment enable Transformers without equivariant layers, while decoded attributes guide bond reconstruction. On PCQM4Mv2, unconditional generation yields 87.9\% unique and novel molecules passing sanitization and PoseBusters checks, exceeding baselines with lower end-to-end training and sampling time and higher end-to-end throughput. Across ten target HOMO-LUMO gaps, internal ranking retains 30\% of the screened candidates and increases the density functional theory-verified hit rate within 0.1 eV of the target from 25.0\% to 52.4\%, while largely preserving novelty and diversity. These results demonstrate fixed-dimensional latent generation with autoregressive decoding as a practical approach to molecular design without prespecifying size.

items.title: Predicting droplet landing in angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting
items.summary: Nozzle-free droplet generation eliminates the need for a dispensing orifice, but useful printing also requires control over where droplets are deposited. Here we demonstrate predictable droplet deposition using a nozzle-free, angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting platform. Opposing focused interdigital transducers steer droplets from a pendant parent drop toward a collection substrate, with the ejection angle set by the time-integrated acoustic acceleration imbalance. The overall acceleration ratio identifies the operating window for single-droplet ejection and separates it from no-ejection, satellite-droplet, and multiple-droplet regimes. We then connect ejection angle to landing position through a geometric deposition model referenced to a balanced shot in each experiment. At a 5.2 mm parent-drop-to-substrate spacing, 80 steered shots across twenty experiments show strongly anisotropic relative placement scatter: 0.59 mm in the steering direction and 0.06 mm transverse to it. In tests conducted independently over several days, a model calibrated on six earlier collection dates predicted landing positions on two later dates with a root-mean-square error of 0.71 mm; bootstrap resampling placed the 95% confidence range for this error between 0.41 and 1.01 mm. The results establish a practical framework for predicting relative droplet landing in angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting and identify the limits imposed by steering angle, separation distance, and actuation regime from an orifice-free, clog-free droplet ejection method.

items.title: Synthetic Stochastic Time Series from Generative Models
items.summary: Obtaining statistically converged time-series data represents a fundamental challenge in computational chemistry, where sampling is constrained by the prohibitive computational cost of high-fidelity simulations. The accuracy attainable from a finite simulation budget is governed by the standard-error scaling $1/\sqrt{n}$, rendering exhaustive sampling challenging for systems of realistic complexity. Here we show that generative models trained on high-quality stochastic trajectories can reproduce key statistical properties of the underlying process and generate additional synthetic trajectories at substantially lower computational cost, thereby enhancing the sampling accessible from a finite set of simulations. We present a systematic comparison of four generative architectures across two complementary data sources: an analytically tractable Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reference and donor-acceptor energy-gap trajectories from all-atom molecular dynamics simulations. Among the four architectures tested, the denoising diffusion probabilistic model reproduces the target statistics most consistently, across both data sources and across the range of correlation times examined, and generates far faster than the sequential Transformer. Specifically, for the energy-gap trajectories, augmentation from 0.1 ns of training data yields statistical estimates comparable in accuracy to those obtained from 0.25-0.50 ns of direct MD sampling. We further show that the benefit of synthetic augmentation is bounded by the information contained in the training data, producing a quality floor determined by both the training data and the generative model. Our findings establish diffusion-based generative models as an effective route to data-driven augmentation of stochastic time series in computational chemistry.

items.title: Semblance Distance Analysis for Channel Quality Assessment in Distributed Acoustic Sensing
items.summary: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) enables dense, kilometer-scale measurements for seismic and environmental monitoring, but its performance is limited by spatially heterogeneous noise and fiber to ground coupling. Identifying high-quality sensing channels remains a challenge, particularly in nonstationary and complex noise environments where conventional signal to noise ratio (SNR) or correlation based approaches are insufficient. In this work, we introduce a statistical framework for DAS channel quality assessment based on a semblance distance metric, which quantifies the deviation of individual channels from a locally coherent reference signal. Unlike traditional pairwise similarity measures, the proposed method formulates channel selection as a distance estimation problem in a coherence enhanced signal space, enabling identification of incoherent noise and coupling induced distortions without requiring prior knowledge of installation conditions or noise statistics. The method is validated using multiple independent datasets, including recordings of the 2023 Turkish-Syrian earthquakes, a controlled seismic source experiment, and long-term continuous measurements. Across all scenarios, the approach identifies regions of low noise and strong coupling, with results that correlate with independent SNR and root mean square error (RMSE) metrics. Furthermore, the method detects subtle sub-decibel temporal variations in coupling conditions over seasonal timescales, demonstrating its capability for continuous fiber health monitoring. These results establish semblance distance analysis as a physically interpretable tool for DAS channel selection with direct applications in seismic imaging, structural health monitoring, and noise mitigation in high sensitivity systems such as gravitational wave detectors.

items.title: QuDPy-FDGF: A Python-Based Tool for Computing Ultrafast Nonlinear Optical Responses Using Frequency Domain Green's Functions
items.summary: We present QuDPy-FDGF, an open-source Python framework that evaluates Liouville-space pathways as hybrid chains of time propagators and frequency-domain Green's functions. Frequency-resolved intervals are computed directly through shifted linear systems, without time propagation followed by a Fourier transform, while other intervals may remain in the time domain. A model-agnostic block interface separates the physical model from pathway construction, numerical propagation, and detection. The released implementation provides an explicit dense Liouville-space backend for reference calculations and a sector-resolved sparse backend using matrix-free generator actions, Krylov time propagation, and generalized minimal residual (GMRES) resolvent solves. Its observable layer reuses propagated pathway responses to evaluate operator expectation values, action-detected readout interactions, instantaneous jump rates, and integrated mean jump counts. The framework is assessed on an analytically solvable open two-level system and on two examples of increasing complexity: the complete third-order rephasing response, with its eight sequences, of a thermally initialized anisotropic Heisenberg (XXZ) spin chain with unequal excitation sectors, and two coupled dissipative anharmonic modes whose spectra depend on the detected observable, with the fifth-order double-quantum response of their closed limit. The calculations reproduce the analytical two-level response, check the matrix-free sparse evaluation against the dense assembly of the generator, and recover the harmonic-limit cancellation of the fifth-order signal when the required three-excitation manifold is retained. QuDPy-FDGF therefore provides a unified framework for pathway- and observable-resolved nonlinear spectroscopy in finite or truncated Hilbert spaces with unitary or Markovian Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) dynamics.

items.title: Black-Hole Ringdown from Photon-Sphere Modes in an Elastic Analogue
items.summary: Quasinormal modes (QNMs) govern the ringdown of black holes, yet their physical origin and experimental accessibility remain limited. Here we create an elastic analogue of a black hole using a curved metallic shell engineered to emulate a Schwarzschild-like metric, and directly probe its vibrational dynamics in the time domain. Following impulsive excitation, the elastic system exhibits a clear ringdown response, providing a tangible analogue of black-hole ringing. The underlying modes are flexural vibrations localized near the photon sphere. A reduction of the thin-shell elastic equations yields a photon-sphere effective potential and predicts the dependence of the localized-mode frequencies on azimuthal order. Crucially, they persist even when boundary reflections are strongly suppressed, demonstrating that their confinement is governed by a curvature-induced effective potential rather than by cavity boundaries. This platform enables direct access to quasinormal modes through both their temporal decay and spectral signatures, establishing a direct connection between photon-sphere dynamics and ringdown. More broadly, our results identify curvature-induced trapping as a general mechanism for wave localization and dissipation in open systems.

items.title: Foundry-Fabricated Silicon Nitride Grating Arrays with Uniform Power Distribution at Visible Wavelengths
items.summary: Multiplexed optical biosensors are widely deployed to read out many biological targets in parallel. However, their channel count and integration density are limited by the photonic network that delivers light to individual sensing sites. Existing on-chip networks have been largely developed for phased arrays and image projection, where performance is assessed through an aggregate radiation pattern rather than the local intensity at each output. In this Letter, we demonstrate a novel bus-and-tap network architecture for massively parallel multiplexed optical delivery. The network uses cascaded directional couplers with individually designed interaction lengths, allowing for arbitrary, user-defined illumination patterns not possible with conventional binary tree architectures. We experimentally validated our proposed architecture with 46 visible-wavelength grating emitter channels designed for uniform illumination at 40 $μ$m pitch in a commercial 300-mm silicon nitride foundry process, achieving an emitted-intensity coefficient of variation of 9.3% at 530 nm, and 8.8% under band-integrated illumination from 550 nm to 650 nm. These results provide a route to scalable visible-light delivery for sensing, imaging, neural interfaces, and parallel optical addressing in quantum systems.

items.title: Robust PCA Study of TEM Images of Gold Nanospheres: Stable and Dynamic Closed Knot-Like Phase-Space Loops
items.summary: In this study, we apply Robust PCA to transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of gold nanoparticles (GNPs) to decompose their geometrical, topological, and dynamical organization into static and dynamic knot-like phase-space loops. Dynamic loops show higher crossing numbers and longer rope lengths, while static loops show higher mean curvature. Although most Alexander determinants were D(t)=1 with isolated values of D(t)=3 at smaller nanoparticle diameters, implying that geometrical complexity does not require topological complexity. The different writhe signs indicate opposite handedness and distinct phase-space geometries in static and dynamic cases. For both static and dynamic knot-like loops, the graphs show an inverse relationship between mean curvature and mean torsion. Flatter trajectories occur at high curvature, and more torsional twisting occurs at low curvature. The small changes in Moffatt-Ricca helicities (~10^-14<<0) are due to circulation-dependent scaling, yet Moffatt-Ricca helicities still follow the same self-linking trend in both static and dynamic configurations. As nanoparticle diameter increases, the dynamic knot-like loops show stronger Kelvin-like spectral localization and smaller minimum self-approach distances, indicating more concentrated spatial modes and tighter geometric folding. At the same time, the decreasing CTEI suggests reduced global phase-space organization. These contrasting trends indicate that the geometrical organization tends to be less global and coherent, and more localized and mode-specific. These results show that the PCA-reconstructed phase space could serve as a mathematical analog to Kelvin's aether, because all disturbances exhibit similar topological configurations with varying degrees of geometric difference.

items.title: A novel mechanism for spontaneous ExB shear layer formation in scrape-off-layer plasmas
items.summary: We present a novel mechanism for spontaneous shear-flow generation in the scrape-off layer (SOL) of magnetically confined plasmas, arising at abrupt changes in the sheath connection length $L_\parallel$. Such transitions occur naturally in the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator. Applying a critical balance treatment for interchange turbulence, we find that $L_\parallel$ sets the equilibrium pressure gradient and hence the radial electric field away from the transition, producing an $E\times B$ shear around the transition comparable to the turbulence growth rate. High-fidelity simulations are shown to be consistent with the theoretical prediction.

items.title: Evolution of Jeans instability in nonthermal magnetized complex plasmas
items.summary: The classical Jeans instability framework provides a conceptual foundation for understanding self-gravitational collapse and subsequent star formation in interstellar environments. However, cosmic plasmas are inherently magnetized and frequently collisionless, exhibiting significant departures from local thermodynamic equilibrium. While linear theories predict initial instability thresholds, they fail to track the long-term nonlinear runaway dynamics. We present a fluid simulation investigating the nonlinear evolution of the Jeans instability in a magnetized tricomponent complex (dusty) plasma. The constituent nonthermal electrons and ions are governed by the $κ$-distribution law, while the heavier dust grains are treated in a fluid framework, coupled with a uniform ambient magnetic field. The numerical architecture utilizes a fourth-order finite difference method (FDM) for spatial gradients and a second-order leap-frog time-integration scheme. We systematically investigate the complex interplay among the self-gravitational attraction, nonthermal electrostatic screening, and magnetic pressure across a wide range of magnetic field strengths and degrees of nonthermality. It is found that enhanced nonthermality accelerates structural localization, while the magnetic field introduces a critical pressure barrier that suppresses the instability. In highly magnetized environments, thermal and nonthermal systems exhibit identical growth rate characteristics, indicating that magnetic pressure dominates the nonthermal thermostatistics in the strong magnetic regime. This study develops a comprehensive and numerically robust framework to understand early-stage star formation and evolution processes in nonthermal astrophysical media.

items.title: Finite time implosions of the multidimensional compressible Euler equations with a finite far-field cutoff
items.summary: We study the problem of finite time singularities in the isentropic compressible Euler equations in multiple dimensions with radial symmetry. Our initial data consists of the radially symmetric Kidder self-similar implosion with a continuous constant density cutoff. Motivated by our recent work on the one-dimensional problem, we present high-resolution radially symmetric adaptive mesh refinement simulations that when combined with asymptotic similarity solution analysis present a full picture of the ensuing dynamics of the implosion. From the cutoff point in the initial data, an expanding wave emerges. The endpoints of the wave follow the "imploding" and "exploding" characteristic speeds associated with the system of hyperbolic conservation laws. This wave has much more complex structure than the exact non-centered rarefaction wave that emerges in the one-dimensional problem. As in the one-dimensional case, the inner Kidder solution is swallowed up by the expanding wave as time approaches the singularity time. However, unlike the one-dimensional case, a blowup occurs along the point where the `imploding' side of the expanding wave attaches to the Kidder solution. This composite blowup has an asymptotic self-similar form that has an interpretation in terms of the Gurderley-type self-similarity structure. The numerical method for the PDE necessitates a Lagrangian scheme to avoid the numerical diffusion inherent in Eulerian methods. We use a leapfrog method coupled to recursive refinement of the mesh near the blowup, which allows for very high resolution simulations, resolving many orders of magnitude of the self-similar blowup. Consistent with prior rigorous results for these equations, the blowup does not involve mass concentration and exhibits a critical $L^p$ space for the concentration of the density, depending on the dimension of space.

items.title: Shear-induced mechanical yielding controls cluster morphology and dynamics in aggregating non-Brownian suspensions
items.summary: In sheared aggregating suspensions, flow drives both the formation and breakage of particle clusters, whose dynamic evolution influences transport and rheological properties. Understanding these mechanisms remains challenging due to the complex interplay between interparticle forces, hydrodynamic interactions, and shear flow. Using parallelized Accelerated Stokesian Dynamics (PASD) simulations, we investigate cluster microstructure and rotational dynamics, and how their coupling produces suspension stress in sheared, attractive non-Brownian suspensions. When interparticle attraction dominates over separating shear forces, clusters grow until mechanical loading balances maximum interparticle bond strength. We examine how the cluster stresslet depends on cluster size, with both quantities normalized by their mechanical yielding scales. Scaled cluster stresslets collapse onto a master curve exhibiting three distinct regimes: cubic, quadratic, and linear with respect to the scaled radius of gyration $R_g$. In the cubic regime, small, compact clusters behave as rigid bodies, whose hydrodynamic stresslet scales with cluster volume $R_g^3$. As clusters grow into the quadratic regime, low-aspect-ratio clusters preferentially yield under flow, driving a proportional increase in average aspect ratio with size. High-aspect-ratio clusters follow Jeffery rotational dynamics within the flow-gradient plane, spending longer durations aligned with the flow and thereby reducing their time-averaged hydrodynamic stresslet to scale as $R_g^2$. In the linear regime, clusters approach the maximum size sustainable by the interparticle bonds. The internal tension is bounded by the maximum bond strength, limiting the stresslet to an $R_g$ dependence. These findings establish a mechanistic framework connecting microscale cluster morphology and dynamics to macroscale rheology.

items.title: In-Situ Differential-Light-Shift Cancellation for Trapped-Atom Clocks
items.summary: Differential light shifts (DLS) induced by optical trapping fields fundamentally limit the stability and accuracy of trapped-atom microwave clocks. We demonstrate an in-situ method to cancel DLS by simultaneously interrogating multiple spatially separated atomic ensembles at different trap intensities generated from a common light source. By operating the ensembles at set intensity ratios and performing Ramsey spectroscopy, the intensity-dependent frequency shifts are measured within each experimental cycle and extrapolated to the zero-intensity limit. This approach effectively enables shot-to-shot determination of a DLS-free frequency without requiring magic wavelengths or species-specific cancellation schemes. We validate the method for Rb atoms trapped in time-averaged potentials by introducing controlled variations of the total trap power and show that the extrapolated frequency remains insensitive to these fluctuations. The technique is general and can be extended to other systematic shifts, providing a scalable route toward improved stability and accuracy in compact trapped-atom clocks and related quantum sensors relying on optical dipole traps

items.title: Plasma transport by carrier electrons: classical coefficients across ionization and magnetization
items.summary: The classical transport of magnetic field and electron energy in a plasma requires the use of coefficients that depend on plasma ionization $Z$ and magnetization $χ$. This paper explains these scalings through studying the electron velocities responsible for each transport process. Both electron-electron collisions and magnetization affect higher velocity electron populations preferentially, lowering the carrier velocities; transport carried by a high energy electron population is therefore more suppressed by both electron-electron collisions and magnetization than transport carried by lower velocities. Carrier Hall parameters $ψ=χf(Z)$ are defined for each coefficient such that magnetization can be described independent of ionization. An analytic idealized coefficient with a single rigid carrier velocity reproduces many of the characteristics of the coefficients, in particular thermal conductivity, but overestimates plasma magnetization due to magnetization itself lowering the carrier velocity. A single moving carrier model improves agreement, but cannot describe the smoothness of the Righi-Leduc coefficient, which originates from being an average over a range of carrier velocities. This is the first paper in a 3-part series; the subsequent papers will extend the carrier picture to non-local heat-flux (paper 2) and non-local magnetic field evolution (paper 3).

items.title: Automated generation and execution of large-scale semidefinite programs for variational two-electron reduced density matrix theory
items.summary: The variational two-electron reduced density matrix (v2RDM) method provides a wave-function-free approach to the description of strong electron correlation whose computational cost scales polynomially with the number of correlated orbitals. Here, we present an automated pipeline for the generation and execution of semidefinite programs (SDPs) associated with the v2RDM problem. Algebraic constraints encoding ensemble $N$-representability conditions are generated via the p$^\dagger$q second-quantized algebra package, and the p$^\dagger$q-generated expressions are automatically translated into a sparse-matrix representation that can be digested by an appropriate SDP solver. We have implemented a boundary-point SDP (BPSDP) solver in the libsdp package that can execute the v2RDM SDPs on either CPU or GPU hardware. We apply the code in several contexts. First, two-particle conditions are used to describe the 76-orbital model of the iron-molybdenum cofactor (FeMoco) of nitrogenase, the simulation of which requires roughly 25 hours of compute time on a single Nvidia H100 GPU. Second, the performance of high-order (four-particle positivity) conditions is evaluated on a challenging two-dimensional H$_{10}$ cluster problem. Lastly, new classes of positivity constraints for mixed fermion-boson systems are generated and applied within the context of ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics simulations.

items.title: Sequential SBI for Resonance Searches at the LHC
items.summary: Neural simulation-based inference has been shown to extract significantly more information from LHC data than histogram-based analyses. So far, it has mostly been applied to couplings, for which the polynomial structure of the scattering amplitude can be exploited. Masses and widths instead move and deform the signal in phase space, and learning their likelihood requires many event samples covering the continuous theory parameter space. We show how sequential simulation-based inference can address this by iteratively concentrating the simulations where the observed data points. Using a parton-level example with an exact reference likelihood and reconstruction-level analyses of $A\to ZH\to \ell\ell b\bar b$ and $Y\to HH\to (t\bar t)(t\bar t)$, we demonstrate that sequential training produces significantly more accurate and better calibrated likelihoods than single round training with the same amount of training events.

items.title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
items.summary: Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we theoretically show how an optomechanical membrane provides a phonon-assisted optical interface for controlling free-electron recoil and sensing localized forces. Transverse membrane motion scatters cavity light into high-momentum evanescent sidebands that enable phase-matched interaction with electrons traveling in vacuum. Beyond supplying momentum for phase matching, the vibration amplitude controls the electron-light interaction strength and redistributes electron populations among recoil orders. External forces that perturb the vibration are thereby encoded in the electron recoil spectrum. Under the modeled conditions, electron readout of localized stochastic forces can yield a higher signal-to-noise ratio than a Gaussian optical homodyne benchmark at equal detected probe rates. These results provide a theoretical basis for mechanically reconfigurable free-electron optics and mode-selective mechanical sensing.

items.title: Adaptive cut reveals multiscale complexity in networks
items.summary: Hierarchical clustering and community detection are important problems in machine learning and complex network analysis. A common approach to identify clusters is to simply cut dendrograms at some threshold. However, single-level cuts are often suboptimal in terms of capturing underlying structure in the data, especially when the dendrogram is unbalanced. In this paper, we present the adaptive cut, a novel method that leverages the hierarchical structure of dendrograms by employing multi-level cuts to overcome the limitations of single-level approaches. The adaptive cut optimizes an objective function using a Markov chain Monte Carlo with simulated annealing, resulting in better partitions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the adaptive cut through applications to link clustering and modularity optimization, but note that the method is applicable to any clustering task that relies on a dendrogram and an objective function. Beyond the adaptive cut, we introduce the balancedness score, an information-theoretic metric that quantifies how balanced a dendrogram is. Balancedness predicts the potential benefits of using multi-level cuts. For the community detection examples, we evaluate our method on more than 200 real-world networks and multiple synthetic datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in partition density and modularity over traditional single-cut approaches. In addition, we show the generality of the adaptive cut by applying it across various hierarchical clustering techniques and objective functions. Our results indicate that the adaptive cut provides a robust and versatile tool for improving clustering outcomes.

items.title: An Implicit Conservative Finite Volume Scheme with Poisson Brackets for the Steady-State Transport of Galactic Cosmic Rays
items.summary: Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) pose a persistent radiation hazard to astronauts and spacecraft in the heliosphere. Modeling their transport is essential for understanding how the solar wind and heliospheric magnetic field shape their spatial distributions and energy spectra. Timely predictions require solving for the particle distribution function much faster than real time, but explicit numerical schemes are restricted by the stability limit on the time step. In this Letter, we present an implicit conservative finite-volume scheme for kinetic equations formulated with Poisson brackets. This scheme conserves particle number, maintains the total-variation-diminishing property, achieves second-order spatial accuracy, and remains stable for time steps far beyond the explicit limit, while reaching quasi-steady states in less than ~1/100 of the computational time required for the explicit scheme, as demonstrated by numerical tests. We apply this scheme to the Parker transport equation along magnetic field lines in the background solar wind during Carrington rotation 2211, where it reaches steady-state GCR distributions within 10 iterations, about 1000 times faster than the explicit scheme. The GCR proton spectrum averaged over 27 days agrees with AMS-02 measurements to within 10%. The simulation also yields a realistic radial intensity gradient and captures the Forbush decrease features associated with three stream interaction regions observed at Earth.

items.title: Matrix-free phase-field modeling of fracture in micromechanical testing simulations of inelastic materials
items.summary: Resolving steep damage gradients across diffuse cracks in the phase-field modeling of fracture favors the use of high-order finite elements, for which matrix-free methods can provide superior performance and scalability. Here, we implement the Peric & Dettmer constitutive framework for visco-elastoplastic materials in an open source solid mechanics library supporting matrix-free operators for high-order finite elements with p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs. We introduce a rheological fracture element assembled in series with the Peric & Dettmer block, keeping fracture and inelastic material properties mutually independent. We conduct numerical simulations of tensile and compressive quasistatic tests on synthetic particle-matrix microstructures using an El Capitan high-performance computing prototype. The results reproduce representative inelastic responses and fracture patterns, including X-shaped cracking observed in polymer-bonded explosives and cup-and-cone fracture in ductile metals.

items.title: Electrically Pumped Quadratic-Soliton Mode-Locked Laser in Lithium Niobate Nanophotonics
items.summary: Femtosecond mode-locked lasers are the workhorse of modern photonics, enabling optical atomic clocks, frequency combs, precision spectroscopy, and ultrafast signal processing. Bringing them onto nanophotonic chips promises miniaturized ultrafast systems, yet combining femtosecond pulse generation with electrical pumping remains a major challenge, rooted in a trade-off between the speed and energy efficiency of mode-locking mechanisms. Kerr-based mechanisms offer nearly instantaneous response but typically require high intracavity peak powers that are difficult to achieve with nanophotonic-compatible semiconductor gain. Conversely, semiconductor saturable absorbers enable strong nonlinear responses at low energies but are limited by their slow carrier dynamics. Here we break this trade-off by introducing quadratic-soliton mode-locking based on a quadratic nonlinear interferometer (QNLI): an effective saturable absorber built from cascaded second-order nonlinearity in periodically poled lithium niobate nanophotonics, with a measured sub-20 fs response time. Through hybrid integration with an electrically pumped semiconductor gain element, we demonstrate a self-starting quadratic-soliton mode-locked laser with femtojoule pulse energies, operating in single- and multiple-soliton states. Quadratic solitons arise through the QNLI's dissipative and dispersive nonlinear response, which we confirm with a modified complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in agreement with measurements. By combining soliton formation with intracavity electro-optic modulation, we generate 750 fs pulses with flat-top spectra. Our engineerable, ultra-energy-efficient, electrically powered laser provides the critical source for fully integrated ultrafast photonic circuits in lithium niobate nanophotonics that natively offers electro-optic control, quadratic wavelength conversion, pulse compression, and spectral broadening.

items.title: Accelerating Periodic Coupled Cluster and Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Theories With Frozen Natural Orbitals
items.summary: We present a unified frozen natural orbital (FNO) framework for periodic Gaussian-orbital post-Hartree-Fock calculations with explicit k-point sampling. The approach includes conventional ground-state FNOs together with state-specific (SS-FNO) and state-averaged (SA-FNO) variants constructed from perturbative one-particle density matrices. We implement these approximations for periodic Moller-Plesset perturbation theory, algebraic diagrammatic construction, and equation-of-motion coupled cluster methods in the PySCF software package and benchmark them for correlation energies, equations of state, fundamental band gaps, and quasiparticle band structures of semiconductors and insulators. FNO truncation reproduces canonical results with small errors while substantially reducing computational cost. SS-FNO enables accurate large-basis band-gap calculations, including quadruple-zeta results, whereas SA-FNO efficiently compresses the virtual space for multi-state band-structure calculations. Combined with basis-set and thermodynamic-limit extrapolations, the framework provides a practical route to high-accuracy correlated calculations in periodic systems.

items.title: Orientational frustration drives enhanced diffusion of anisotropic particles in a liquid labyrinth
items.summary: Transport of nanoscale objects in complex, structured environments plays a key role in a wide range of processes, from biomolecular dynamics in extracellular spaces to transport in porous materials such as filters and catalysts. While anomalous diffusion is well established, how particle anisotropy governs transport under geometric constraints remains unclear. Here we use 3D single-particle tracking to investigate the diffusion of stiff one-dimensional carbon nanotubes in a continuous soft matter network of interconnected chambers and constrictions. Transport is anomalous and antipersistent, with strong length dependent confinement and trapping, consistent with obstructed diffusion. Unexpectedly, however, escape from confinement is poorly sensitive to nanotube length as opposed to what would be expected of pore mediated transport. Despite a tenfold length increase and significantly enhanced trapping, escape time increased by only ~1.4. Single-particle orientational tracking reveals the origin of this weak scaling. Indeed, long nanotube, i.e. those with length comparable to the chamber dimensions, dynamically align with constrictions enabling efficient, geometry-assisted escape that offsets increased confinement while shorter nanotubes need to screen the volume to find their escape path. These results uncover an alignment-mediated transport mechanism that decouples confinement strength from escape kinetics, distinct from pore-mediated transport mechanisms, establishing a quantitative framework for anisotropic diffusion in complex environments.

items.title: Methane and ethane adsorption on calcite surfaces: effects of surface morphology from molecular dynamics and 3D-RISM
items.summary: Understanding the adsorption of alkanes on mineral surfaces is important for industrial processes such as oil and gas recovery from shale reservoirs. Previous studies have examined the adsorption of functionalized and non-functionalized alkanes on calcite, as well as adsorption under confinement. However, real surfaces commonly exhibit defects that can influence adsorption behavior. In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and the three-dimensional reference interaction site model (3D-RISM) are used to investigate the adsorption of methane and ethane on calcite surfaces with step defects. MD simulations were carried out with and without positional restraints to investigate the effects of carbonate reorientation. 3D-RISM calculations were performed on these structures and on energy-minimized configurations of the relaxed crystal. Both methods show adsorption enhanced at step defects relative to flat regions, with methane exhibiting higher excess adsorption than ethane. Carbonate reorientation at the relaxed step edges reduces the local density peaks at specific step sites in both methods, while the integrated excess adsorption from MD remains comparable to that of the restrained surface. 3D-RISM predicts lower maxima for the highest density peaks and larger excess adsorption than MD, but reproduces the spatial organization and overall adsorption trends at a fraction of the computational cost. These results highlight the importance of surface heterogeneity in fluid-mineral interactions and demonstrate that 3D-RISM is an efficient tool for semi-quantitative screening of adsorption across complex surface geometries

items.title: Stationarity Constraints Improve Both Energies and Densities of Machine-Learned Exchange-Correlation Functionals
items.summary: Empirical exchange-correlation functionals are fitted on fixed orbitals but used self-consistently, so better energies often come with worse densities. We show that the Brillouin residual of a trained functional on the Kohn-Sham orbitals of an accurate density controls, to first order, both the self-consistent density shift and the gap between fitted and self-consistent energies. Penalizing it requires no self-consistent-field solution during training. Trained on 6 energies and 11 CCSD densities, a neural meta-GGA surpasses SCAN in both atomization energies and densities of unseen molecules.

items.title: DiffVortex: A quantum-inspired fast solver for incompressible flows
items.summary: Matrix-product-state (MPS) and quantized tensor-train (QTT) representations offer a promising framework for computational fluid dynamics, with logarithmic run time and memory scaling in mesh size when bond dimensions remain bounded. Existing MPS-based solvers are Eulerian: they compress velocity fields and enforce immersed-body boundary conditions through static masks or body-fitted coordinates. Moving or flexible bodies complicate this approach: deformation requires updating MPS masks every time step, while filamentary vorticity in high-Reynolds-number flows may resist low-rank compression. We propose a complementary approach: compress the Biot--Savart kernel rather than the flow state, evolve vorticity using Lagrangian vortex particles, and represent immersed bodies by bound vortex sheets on Lagrangian surface points. Our main theoretical result is a lifting theorem: QTT rank $r$ of the kernel implies matrix-product-operator (MPO) rank at most $2^d r$ for the corresponding convolution operator in $d$ dimensions, independent of grid resolution. This bound is sharp for our interleaved ordering. With quantics tensor cross interpolation, the moment-to-local stage of a single-level fast multipole method becomes a precomputed tensor-network contraction with quasi-linear complexity, retaining Lagrangian flexibility for immersed bodies. Our PyTorch implementation (\texttt{DiffVortex}) is end-to-end differentiable, runs on GPUs, and handles $6.7\times10^{7}$ particles on a single device. We validate against reference vortex-method results for an impulsively started cylinder and exact and reference solutions for inviscid elliptical vortices. We also demonstrate two-dimensional flows past rigidly moving, multiple, and deforming bodies, including gradients propagated through the full time integration.

items.title: UNWRAP: Single-shot phase analysis of bright squeezed vacuum by Newton-ring interferometry
items.summary: The mean field of pulsed bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) vanishes, but the variance can be large, and is strongly phase-dependent. We employ ultrafast Newton-ring wavefront retrieval and analysis of phase (UNWRAP) to extract the field amplitude and phase profile of each BSV pulse, by Fourier analysis of the interference rings between the BSV and a coherent reference with different phase-front curvature. The concentric ring interference fringes are robust against pointing mismatch and drift, thereby simplifying the analysis. The measured distribution has two phase peaks separated by π radians. The rings sweep the delay between the two pulses, so a single frame can capture the temporal field profile of the BSV, even when it is composed of several temporal modes.

items.title: Tangential and normal partial slip at the liquid-fluid interfaces: An application to a small liquid droplet, gas bubble, and aerosol
items.summary: An analytical solution is obtained for the problem of the slow movement of a small drop of a fluid in another immiscible fluid in an infinitely large reservoir with the boundary condition of the normal slip and(or) tangential partial slip at the liquid-liquid or gas-liquid interface.
