items.title: A Diagnostic for Bias in Linear Mixed Model Estimators Induced by Dependence Between the Random Effects and the Corresponding Model Matrix
items.summary: We explore how violations of the often-overlooked standard assumption that the random effects model matrix in a linear mixed model is fixed (and thus independent of the random effects vector) can lead to bias in estimators of estimable functions of the fixed effects. However, if the random effects of the original mixed model are instead also treated as fixed effects, or if the fixed and random effects model matrices are orthogonal with respect to the inverse of the error covariance matrix (with probability one), or if the random effects and the corresponding model matrix are independent, then these estimators are unbiased. The bias in the general case is quantified, and a diagnostic for its random-effects contribution is compared to a randomized permutation distribution of the predicted random effects, producing an informative summary graphic for each estimator of interest. This is demonstrated through the examination of sporting outcomes used to estimate a home field advantage.

items.title: A Fast Algorithm for Quaternion Tensor Singular Value Decomposition under the T-product
items.summary: Quaternion tensor singular value decomposition (T-SVD) under the T-product provides a framework for analyzing multidimensional quaternion data. However, the T-SVD construction of Pan and Ng (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl., 2024) \cite{PanNg2024} contains a structural gap: an unrestricted quaternion matrix SVD need not preserve the paired Fourier block structure required for tensor factor recovery, potentially leading to loss of T-unitarity and inaccurate reconstruction. To address this issue, we develop a structure-preserving construction that transforms each paired quaternion block into a complex matrix and maps its complex SVD factors back to quaternion factors with the required structure. This construction corrects the proof of \cite[Theorem 4]{PanNg2024} and leads to a corrected version of \cite[Algorithm 2]{PanNg2024}, hereafter referred to as the ``corrected algorithm'', ensuring T-unitary tensor factors and an f-diagonal core for arbitrary third-order quaternion tensors. A numerical counterexample demonstrates the failure of \cite[Algorithm 2]{PanNg2024} and verifies the corrected algorithm at machine precision. Notably, we propose a fast structure-preserving algorithm, Algorithm~\ref{alg:t-fast}, and compare it numerically with the corrected algorithm. The experimental results show that Algorithm~\ref{alg:t-fast} reduces the decomposition time while maintaining near-machine-precision accuracy. Furthermore, its application to color video encryption yields high reconstruction quality, favorable ciphertext statistics, and stability under input perturbations.

items.title: Concentration inequalities for vector-valued martingales
items.summary: In this paper, we establish several deviation inequalities for the norms of vector-valued martingales, achieving bounds of the same quality as those available in the classical one-dimensional setting. Our results extend and refine previous work by Pinelis (1994) and Hayes (2005) in this area.

items.title: Semi-strict 4-categories as enriched categories
items.summary: We introduce several flavours of semi-strict 4-category as enriched categories. We give the axioms for semi-strict 4-categories in elementary terms and describe a wide range of examples. In particular, we answer the question of what exactly Gray-categories and the higher transformations between them form: namely, a left-sharp 4-category G-Cat$^4$. In addition, we describe examples arising from braided monoidal 2-categories, monoidal Gray-categories (herein defined) and Gray-categories with structure. We use the concepts introduced here and the relationships between them to unify various concepts in the literature, such as Crans' 4-teisi. In the second part of the paper, we investigate homotopical aspects. In particular, we classify the equivalence n-cells in the left-sharp 4-category G-Cat$^4$ for each n. Using this, we show that the left-sharp skew monoidal structure on the category of Gray-categories induces a symmetric monoidal closed structure on the homotopy category of Gray-categories.

items.title: Boundary regularity of $k$-Hessian eigenfunctions
items.summary: We prove smoothness up to the boundary for $k$-Hessian eigenfunctions on smooth bounded uniformly convex domains when $2\leq k<n$. This resolves an open problem in the regularity theory of degenerate fully nonlinear elliptic equations and extends the boundary smoothness theorem for Monge--Ampère eigenfunctions. In contrast to the Monge--Ampère case, the linearized $k$-Hessian operator remains uniformly elliptic up to the boundary.

items.title: Conditioned stochastic stability of equilibrium states on uniformly hyperbolic sets
items.summary: We establish the conditioned stochastic stability of equilibrium states for Hölder potentials on uniformly hyperbolic sets. While standard stochastic stability characterises measures on attractors, we analyse the statistics of transient dynamics on non-attracting sets by conditioning small random perturbations of the dynamics to not escape from our regions of interest. We prove that as the noise intensity vanishes, the quasi-ergodic measure of the $e^φ$-weighted process generated by $\e$-small random perturbations of the deterministic dynamics converges to the unique equilibrium state associated with the potential $φ- \log \left|\det \left. D T\right|_{E^u}\right|$. The results are obtained via perturbative spectral analysis of transfer operators acting on anisotropic Banach spaces and topological hyperbolic dynamics arguments. Furthermore, we extend this framework globally to Axiom A diffeomorphisms with multiple basic sets using dynamical filtrations. This work provides a rigorous characterisation of natural measures on uniformly hyperbolic repellers, which are fundamental in the context of transient chaos. Our results have been formalised in Lean~4.

items.title: Local heights for nef toric compactified divisors
items.summary: We present a definition of a local height of nef toric divisors in the sense of Yuan and Zhang by approximating a height for canonical divisors and then using the local energy to extend to other metrics on the same geometric divisor.

items.title: Random Survivor Sets with Moving Holes in Bedford-McMullen Carpets
items.summary: Let $2\le m < n$ be integers, and let $K(\mathcal{A})$ be the Bedford--McMullen carpet generated by $\{(x,y)\mapsto((x+i)/m,(y+j)/n):(i,j)\in\mathcal{A}\}$, where $\mathcal{A}$ is a subset of $\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}\times\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$. Write $\mathcal{B}$ for the set of occupied columns, and assume that $\#\mathcal{B}\ge2$ and each column contains at least two symbols of $\mathcal{A}$. At each vertex of the column tree $\mathcal{B}^*$, we independently choose one forbidden symbol from $\mathcal{A}$ according to a prescribed distribution. Let $\mathbb{P}$ denote the resulting product measure on $\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. This gives a random survivor set $K_ω(\mathcal{A})$ with $ω\in\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. We show that, for $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $ω$, \begin{equation*} \dim_H K_ω(\mathcal{A})=\frac{1}{\log m}\log\left(\int \sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}}\ell_b(ω)^{\frac{\log m}{\log n}} d\mathbb{P}(ω)\right), \end{equation*} where $\ell_b(ω)$ is the number of surviving symbols in column $b$ at the root.

items.title: Facets of nondegeneracy: central type factor groups, Heisenberg representations and Hadamard matrices
items.summary: Given a pair of complementary subgroups $P$ and $N$ of a finite group $G$, we first discuss how the same type of functions $\mathbb E\colon P\times N\to \mathbb T$, which we call bi-$1$-cocycles, appear naturally in the study of projective representations of $G$ of Heisenberg type and second cohomology of $G$ and of its dual quantum group $\widehat G$. We show then that such representations are irreducible and the corresponding ordinary and dual $2$-cocycles are nondegenerate if and only if the matrix $(\mathbb E(p,n))_{p,n}$ is invertible, if and only if it is Hadamard. We illustrate the result with examples arising from symplectic nilpotent Lie algebras over finite fields with two complementary Lagrangian subalgebras.

items.title: A special Hardy estimate in the axisymmetric swirl problem
items.summary: We examine the proof of Dongyi Wei's logarithmic circulation criterion. A trace estimate specific to $\nabla(u_r/r)$ replaces a generic squared-swirl form bound by one with one logarithm rather than two. Repeating the coupled $J$--$Ω$ energy and comparison argument then gives a proposed threshold of order $(\log D)^{-5/4}$. Under the hypotheses stated below, the proof is intended to establish regularity when $|r u_θ|\le C|\log r|^{-α}$ uniformly near the axis with $α>5/4$, and at $α=5/4$ with an absolute sufficiently small coefficient. Every analytic step, including the cutoff core and exterior terms, is included for independent checking.

items.title: Dimension-free regimes for unadjusted Langevin in ridge-separable models: A subspace robust Wasserstein analysis
items.summary: The Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (ULA) is widely used for high-dimensional Bayesian inference. Classical analyses in Wasserstein-2 distance predict an asymptotic bias and a mixing time that grow with dimension, but this metric is stronger than necessary for many statistical tasks. We instead analyze the bias in subspace robust Wasserstein distance, which controls the mean and arbitrary low-dimensional marginals and is therefore well suited to observables typically estimated in practice. For ridge-separable potentials formed with i.i.d. data, we prove high-probability bounds showing a bell-shaped mixing profile as the number of data points $N$ varies relative to the dimension $d$. In the overparameterized regime, the effective dimension is the rank $N$ of the data-dependent perturbation, leading to complexity depending on $N$ rather than $d$. In the large-sample regime, Gaussian-perturbation estimates yield dimension-free complexity once $N$ is sufficiently large. In contrast, near the proportional regime $\asymp d$, we prove that dimension-free guarantees are impossible in general.

items.title: A hybrid finite-volume scheme with learned rational reconstructions and exact nonlocal fluxes for the space-fractional Burgers equation
items.summary: On coarse grids, fronts of fractional conservation laws can be narrower than one cell, while the flux through each face depends on the whole domain. For the forced space-fractional Burgers equation, we write the finite-volume defect exactly, with the Riesz flux acting as a nonlocal interface flux. Our proposed closure, NRC, is decoder-only, since the encoder is the exact cell-average projection and a small network only maps cell averages to a sub-cell reconstruction. The decoder adds rational atoms with learned complex poles to a trigonometric histopolant, preserves every cell average, and has closed-form advective and Riesz fluxes. We prove that the scheme conserves mass for every value of the weights and that the learned sub-grid flux has a dipole tail. On 64 cells, NRC reaches a median test error of 0.0308% over three seeds, against 0.431% for WENO5-Z and 0.153% for a black-box flux correction. Ablations show that the exact global operator, the projection and the sub-grid Riesz flux carry most of this gain, and most sub-cell fronts carry a deep learned pole within a quarter cell. NRC keeps its advantage over WENO5-Z under shifts of the order and the forcing and, when trained on several diffusivities, under the tested diffusivity shifts by factors from 0.6 to 2.5 in the median over seeds. From 32 to 128 cells, NRC stays an order of magnitude more accurate than WENO5-Z on the same grid. This gain lies in accuracy per degree of freedom and in an interpretable closure.

items.title: A Resource Allocation Tournament
items.summary: We introduce and analyze a round-robin simultaneous resource allocation contest, motivated by sports leagues and other competitive environments where agents must distribute limited resources across multiple encounters. Players allocate resources in advance to matches against all opponents, and match outcomes are determined by relative allocations. We study two payoff schemes: total points, where players accumulate rewards for each win, and winner-takes-all, where only the tournament winner is rewarded. For three players, we provide complete equilibrium characterizations under both schemes. For four or more players, we show that the total points payoff admits Blotto-type equilibria, while the winner-takes-all payoff requires numerical and algorithmic analysis. To address this, we develop a best-response dynamics algorithm with stochastic inertia and use it to approximate equilibria in games with four and five players.

items.title: On weighted extremal Kähler metrics
items.summary: The notion of weighted extremal Kähler metrics extends the classical notion of Calabi's extremal Kähler metrics, but includes many well-studied objects in Kähler geometry such as Kähler-Ricci solitons and Sasaki-Einstein metrics. In this paper, after explaining how this notion grew out, we will try to survey recent works concerning the YTD conjecture on weighted extremal Kähler metrics.

items.title: No braiding for quantum sl2 reps - A short proof
items.summary: We give a short and self-contained proof that the category of all finite dimensional representations of quantum sl2 is not braided.

items.title: The center is the formal internal automorphism group
items.summary: We prove that the deformation functor associated to an algebra over a sufficiently nice Koszul operad can be lifted to an operadic formal moduli problem over the Koszul dual operad. We further show that this operadic formal moduli problem corresponds to the derived center of the algebra under the operadic Lurie-Pridham correspondence. As an application, we prove that the classical Gerstenhaber algebra structure on polyvector fields of a commutative algebra agrees with the derived center of the algebra as an abelian Poisson algebra.

items.title: The symmetric skew monoidal structure of Gray-categories
items.summary: In a previous paper, we constructed a closed skew monoidal structure on the category of Gray-categories and Gray-functors whose internal hom Psd(A, B) captures pseudomaps and pseudo-transformations. In the present paper we give a symmetric description of the Gray-category Psd(A,B) and use this to prove that the skew monoidal structure is symmetric skew monoidal.

items.title: String attractors and bi-infinite words
items.summary: String attractors are a combinatorial tool coming from the field of data compression. It is a set of positions within a word which captures an occurrence of every factor. While one-sided infinite words admitting a finite string attractor are eventually periodic, the situation is different for two-sided infinite words. In this article, we characterise the bi-infinite words admitting a finite string attractor as the eventually periodic words, the characteristic Sturmian words and their morphic images. For words that do not admit finite string attractors, we study the structure and properties of their infinite string attractors.

items.title: Concavity of the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck torsion function on centered ellipses and its failure on convex domains
items.summary: Let $u$ be the torsion function of a bounded domain $Ω$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator, that is, the solution of $-Δu + x\cdot\nabla u = 1$ in $Ω$ with $u=0$ on the boundary. We prove that for every $n\ge2$ there are bounded, centrally symmetric domains whose torsion function is not concave. These domains have boundary with a flat piece and can be smoothed so that the boundary is $C^\infty$, strictly convex with principal curvatures bounded below by a positive constant, while keeping the torsion function not concave. In contrast, the torsion function for every ellipse centered at the origin is concave, and for every ball centered at the origin we prove the sharp bound $D^2u\leq-\frac{1}{n}I$. The ellipse result follows by deformation from the disk, using a boundary flux estimate and third-order boundary identities to exclude a first zero eigenvalue of the Hessian.

items.title: Benign cubic and quartic forms on the sphere
items.summary: One considers the NP-hard problem of minimizing real cubic and quartic forms on the Euclidean unit sphere. One first extends the Hessian spectral characterization of local minima by the author. In particular one provides a gap-depth characterization of negative global and spurious minima, and proves that the minimum value of an odd degree-d form is recovered (up to the factor d(d -1)) by minimizing the smallest eigenvalue of its ambient Hessian over the sphere (and equivalently the unit ball). Next, one exhibits several classes of benign families of cubic and quartic forms (i.e. with no spurious local minima on the sphere) and prove that some are robust to small coefficient perturbation (i.e. the resulting form remains benign even if it leaves the initial family). Therefore the class of benign cubic and quartic forms is full-dimensional (in the ambient space of coefficients), for n $\ge$ 2. Also for every odd degree d, the class of benign degree-d forms increases with the dimension (however it does not imply that such forms become more frequent when the dimension increases).

items.title: Landau-Siegel zeros over a base field and effective Brauer-Siegel
items.summary: Let k be a number field. We prove that for every quadratic extension F/k, every real zero beta of L(s, chi_{F/k}) satisfies (1 - beta) log d_F >= c(k) with an effective constant c(k) > 0, and we deduce (through a reduction of Stark) that the Brauer-Siegel theorem holds effectively and uniformly over all Galois extensions K of k, in the form h_K R_K >= c(k) d_K^{1/2} / ((2 pi)^{[K:Q]} log d_K). Stark's effective cases of the Brauer-Siegel theorem were the fields without quadratic subfields, since the quadratic subfields carried the ineffectivity of Siegel's theorem; over a base field k, the first result removes it. Both rely on a uniform bound for Chebotarev sums. Let K/k be a Galois extension with group G, and suppose S is a subset of G containing the identity. For any prime p of k, let delta_p be the proportion of the primes of K above p whose Frobenius lies in S. Then the sum over Np <= X of delta_p log Np / Np is at most (|S|/|G| + epsilon) log X + O(1), uniformly in K, as soon as X >= d_K^C with C depending only on epsilon and the degree [K:Q]. The proof is Kerr's form of the OpenAI argument, simple vanishing at the points (iota theta)_{iota in S}, with theta in a box in O_K, and Masser's zero estimate. The field enters only through Masser's invariant of the lattice of points, which we compute to be [K:Q]/|S| by averaging over the Galois group of the normal closure. Over Q, the determinant method of Green, Barreto, and Kominers gives sharper Chebotarev bounds, and we explain the comparison.

items.title: Convergence of the Birkhoff spectrum for nonintegrable observables
items.summary: We consider interval maps with countably many full branches and observables with polynomial tails. We show that the Birkhoff spectrum is real analytic and that its convergence to the Hausdorff dimension of the repeller is governed by the polynomial tail exponent. This result extends previous work by Arima on more regular observables and demonstrates how the tail behaviour influences the structure of the Birkhoff spectrum. Our proof relies on techniques from thermodynamic formalism and tail estimates for the observable and our applications are to natural observations on Gauss maps, Lüroth transformations as well as to a the first return time for a class of induced Manneville-Pomeau maps.

items.title: An asymptotic $Γ$-BMT inequality
items.summary: We refine a bound of Cheng-Feyzbakhsh to prove an asymptotic $Γ$-Bayer-Macrì-Toda ($Γ$-BMT) inequality on every smooth polarized complex threefold. The proof relies on a reduction to small tilt stability parameters. Using this inequality we verify Feyzbakhsh-Thomas's condition $(wBG)$ whenever $K_{X}$ is numerically proportional to the polarization. For polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds, this yields a reduction of positive rank generalized Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants to those counting sheaves pure in codimension one. We further express these invariants in terms of rank one generalized DT invariants. Thus, the rank reductions of Feyzbakhsh-Thomas hold without assuming the BMT conjecture.

items.title: Control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems
items.summary: This monograph presents a selection of the author's recent works on the control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems. After a detailed introduction to topics related to time-delay systems covered in the monograph, its main contents are presented in a series of mostly independent chapters.

items.title: $δ$-Superderivations of semisimple finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras
items.summary: In the paper, a complete description of the $δ$-derivations and the $δ$-superderivations of semisimple finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\neq2$ is given. In particular, new examples of nontrivial $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and odd $\frac{1}{2}$-superderivations are given that are not operators of right multiplication by an element of the superalgebra.

items.title: Local-Cohen-Macaulay DG-rings with unequal finitistic projective dimensions
items.summary: For every pair of integers $d,n\geq1$, we construct a commutative noetherian local-Cohen-Macaulay DG-ring $A$ such that $\dim H^0(A)=d$, $\mathrm{amp}(A)=n$, $\mathrm{fpd}(A)=d-n$, and $\mathrm{FPD}(A)=d$. This gives a negative answer to the implication from local-Cohen-Macaulayness to equality of the two finitistic projective dimensions in a question of Bird, Shaul, Sridhar, and Williamson.

items.title: Bridging persistence of discrete and continuous 1D maps: Total variation, permutation equivalence, and diagonal affine transformations
items.summary: Fundamental to the field of topological signal processing (TSP) is the \textit{persistence diagram} (PD), or barcode, of a signal, which gives noise-resistant measures of topologically significant features as distinct from noise. Existing literature proves that the total persistence computed from these diagrams is equal to the total variation, for certain continuous signals on compact domains. We provide a closed formula for this shared quantity, and generalize to all continuous and discrete functions on bounded domains, and to certain functions on non-compact 1D manifolds. Extending the identification of continuous and discrete persistence, we investigate the similarities of functions with the same PDs, and prove that, for any $n$, the persistence diagram can be calculated as a function of the sequence of critical values; we compute these formulas for $n \leq 6$. Finally, we examine which function transformations cause predictable changes in the PD of the transformed function, characterizing affine and linear transformations.

items.title: Stability of Fourier Restriction for a Class of Finite Type Surfaces in $\mathbb R^3$
items.summary: We establish the stability of the optimal non-endpoint Fourier restriction range under smooth flat perturbations of curved-root surfaces in $\mathbb R^3$. Specifically, we consider graphs of $$φ(x_1,x_2)=(x_2-x_1^m)^n+R(x_1,x_2),$$ where $m,n\ge2$ are integers and $R$ is smooth and flat at the origin. On a sufficiently small neighborhood depending on the perturbation, we prove the local $L^p(\mathbb R^3)\to L^2(S,dσ)$ restriction estimate for $1\le p<p_c$, where $$p_c=\frac{q_c}{q_c-1}, \qquad q_c=\max\left\{2+\frac{2mn}{m+1},2n\right\}.$$ If the nonnegative localizing density is positive at the origin, an adapted-box example shows that the estimate fails for $p>p_c$. Thus arbitrary smooth flat perturbations preserve the optimal restriction range away from the critical endpoint. For $n\ge3$, the main local estimate combines planar curve decoupling with a one-dimensional finite-type extension estimate, whose principal scale factors cancel exactly. For $n=2$, we prove a uniform $C^4$ perturbation estimate using a weighted convolution bound and an anisotropic Whitney decomposition. Anisotropic rescaling and summation complete the proof.

items.title: Lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions for a class of curvilinear polygons
items.summary: Steklov eigenfunctions, $\{φ_{σ_j}\}_{j=0}^\infty$, are the eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet to Neumann map on a bounded domain with eigenvalue $σ_j$. This paper considers Steklov eigenfunctions and eigenvalues on a family of curvilinear polygons, $Ω_α$ whose boundaries are smooth away from a single corner of angle $α$. We (i) prove optimal lower bounds on the decay of the harmonic extension, $u_{σ_j}$, of $φ_{σ_j}$ away from the boundary of $Ω_α$ and (ii) give optimal lower bounds on the degree to which the high energy Steklov spectrum of $Ω_α\setminus H_1$ may differ from that of $Ω_α\setminus H_0$ when $H_1$ and $H_0$ are isometric. This shows that the corresponding estimates in recent work by the authors together with Malagutti are optimal. The proof in this paper was obtained through an interaction with ChatGPT 6 Astra: While writing the work with Malagutti, the authors became curious about optimal error bounds for the difference between the Steklov spectra on a curvilinear polygon, $P$, and the spectrum of any operator which knows only local information about $\partial P$. The authors suggested to ChatGPT to remove two isometric, smooth domains from a curvilinear polygon. ChatGPT suggested the ideas for a proof based on a regularized trace and the singularity in the kernel of the DtN map near a corner. The authors then suggested a simpler, conformal approach, the method for handling small angles, and the idea to obtain lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions. The paper is entirely written by the authors and the argument has been significantly modified, clarified, and simplified from the ChatGPT ideas.

items.title: Convex Equilibrium Potentials for Monge--Ampère: Curvature Bounds and A Posteriori Evaluation
items.summary: Equilibrium neural networks define their hidden state as the fixed point of a contraction, so their effective depth is set at evaluation time rather than by the architecture. Using them for fully nonlinear PDEs raises two issues that explicit networks avoid: second derivatives may grow with the effective depth, and the potential is only ever evaluated approximately. We study nonnegative softplus equilibrium networks with contraction factor $q<1$, a convex class suited to the Monge--Ampère equation. A positivity cancellation in the resolvent shows that the Hessian grows at most like $(1-q)^{-2}$, rather than the $(1-q)^{-3}$ of a direct estimate, and an explicit one-neuron family shows that this exponent is sharp; third derivatives satisfy a sharp $(1-q)^{-3}$ bound. Residual-based a posteriori estimates then control the state, its input derivatives and, in two dimensions, the Hessian determinant at an approximate equilibrium. Combined with interval arithmetic on complete covers of the domain, they yield rigorous uniform bounds on the Monge--Ampère residual and, through a comparison argument, on the solution error of a fixed trained network. On two manufactured Dirichlet problems on the unit disk, all six trained models are certified with residual below $0.25$ and boundary error below $0.01$. Adaptive stopping halves float64 evaluation time at best, whereas certified adaptive evaluation remains costlier than fixed depth.

items.title: Bounded symbols and one-component geometry
items.summary: We prove that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on a Hardy model space admits a bounded symbol if and only if its defining inner function is one-component, meaning that it has a connected sublevel set at some level in $(0,1)$. This resolves the bounded symbol conjecture of Baranov, Chalendar, Fricain, Mashreghi and Timotin and, through known equivalences, the embedding and weak factorization conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin. A uniform bound $R$ for the ratio of least bounded symbol norm to operator norm on the rank-one family associated with point evaluation in the disk already forces this geometry. The corresponding bound for all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators is at most $CR\log(e+R)$, where $C$ is absolute, and the logarithmic factor is optimal. In a nonzero de Branges space, the same geometric condition characterizes when every sufficiently small equivalent change of norm preserving the de Branges structure is represented exactly by reweighting the original integral with a positive density bounded above and away from zero. This characterization remains valid when the norm changes are restricted to discrete sampling norms. Outside the one-component class, every model space admits self-adjoint trace class truncated Toeplitz operators without bounded symbols, with arbitrarily small norm and singular values satisfying any prescribed positive upper bounds.

items.title: On conservative algebras of 2-dimensional Algebras
items.summary: In 1990 Kantor introduced the conservative algebra $\mathcal{W}(n)$ of all algebras (i.e. bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. In case $n >1$ the algebra $\mathcal{W}(n)$ does not belong to well known classes of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, Leibniz algebras). We describe $\frac{1}{2}$derivations, local (resp. $2$-local) $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and biderivations of $\mathcal{W}(2)$. We also study similar problems for the algebra $\mathcal{W}_2$ of all commutative algebras on the two-dimensional vector space and the algebra $\mathcal{S}_2$ of all commutative algebras with trace zero multiplication on the two-dimensional space.

items.title: The Penrose Correspondence over a Non-Archimedean Field
items.summary: Let $K$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and let $V$ be a four-dimensional symplectic $K$-vector space. We study the Penrose incidence correspondence $\mathbb{P}(V) \leftarrow \mathrm{Flag}(1,2;V) \rightarrow \mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ after Berkovich analytification. The Klein quadric $\mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ decomposes into the open orbit $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ and the Lagrangian quadric, which parametrize respectively the projective lines transverse and tangent to the standard contact distribution on $\mathbb{P}(V)$. We construct explicit free discrete subgroups $Γ\subset\mathrm{PSp}(V)$ and analytic domains, cut out by Drinfeld upper half-spaces, in all three members of the incidence diagram. Both incidence projections are surjective on these domains, the three $Γ$-actions are free and properly discontinuous, and the Penrose double correspondence descends to the analytic quotients. The quotient of the twistor domain is a contact analytic threefold, and the Grassmannian domain is contained in the analytification of the $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ open orbit.

items.title: Adaptive Local Proper Orthogonal Decomposition via Graph Partitioning and Provable Error-Bounded Lossy Compression for Parametric Series in Finite-Dimensional Function Spaces
items.summary: We introduce a spatially adaptive proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method for error-bounded lossy compression of snapshot data in finite-dimensional function spaces. The method combines hierarchical graph partitioning with independent low-rank approximations on spatial subdomains, allowing the local approximation ranks to adapt to the spatial distribution of information in the data. For partitions that are orthogonal in the discrete inner product, we establish an exact decomposition of the global squared reconstruction error into local contributions and characterize the optimality of the resulting local POD approximations for fixed partitions and ranks. These results provide a rigorous mechanism for allocating a prescribed global error tolerance among subdomains and selecting the smallest admissible local ranks. We further develop a sufficient error bound for the coefficient-space normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE). A greedy hierarchical refinement algorithm accepts a spatial subdivision only when it reduces the storage required by the local low-rank factors while preserving the prescribed reconstruction-error bound. The method is assessed using synthetic data and snapshot sequences from two- and three-dimensional compressible-flow simulations. The numerical results illustrate how spatially adaptive ranks and partitioning can improve compression relative to global POD and fixed spatial partitions, particularly when the data exhibit spatially heterogeneous dynamics.

items.title: Diffusive Stochastic Master Equation (SME) with dispersive qubit/cavity coupling
items.summary: We provide a detailed analysis of the quantum diffusive Stochastic Master Equation~(SME) for qubit/cavity systems with dispersive coupling, incorporating classical input signals and output signals (measurement outcomes via homodyne/heterodyne detection). We show that the dynamics of the qubit/cavity density operator converges exponentially towards a slow invariant manifold. This manifold is parameterized by the density operator of a \emph{fictitious} qubit governed by a quantum SME that incorporates the classical input/output signals while preserving complete positivity and trace. The reduced cavity (resp.\ qubit) operator, obtained by partial trace over the qubit (resp.\ cavity), is then expressed as a time-varying deterministic quantum channel acting on the fictitious-qubit density operator. This formulation avoids the non-Markovian descriptions---with temporarily negative dephasing rates or detection efficiencies exceeding one---that appear in several publications. Extensions are considered in which the qubit is replaced by a qudit dispersively coupled to an arbitrary set of cavity modes driven by collective classical input/output signals.

items.title: Discorrelation of the Möbius function with linear phases in short intervals
items.summary: We introduce a new approach to studying correlations between arithmetic functions and linear phases with respect to highly irrational frequencies over short intervals. As an application, we prove that \[ \Big|\sum_{x<n \leq x+H}μ(n) e(nα)\Big| \ll H(\log x)^{-1/3+\varepsilon } \] whenever $x^{0.58+\varepsilon }\leq H\leq x$. In the same range of $H$ we also show that \[ \Big|\sum_{x<n \leq x+H} Λ(n) e(nα)\Big| \ll H(\log x)^{-A} \] for arbitrarily large $A>0$ unless there exists an integer $1\leq q\ll (\log x)^{O_A(1)}$ such that $\|qα\| \ll x (\log x)^{O_A(1)}/H^2$. This breaks the $3/5$ barrier in Theorem 1.5 of arXiv:1911.09076v2 and Theorem 2 of [T. Zhan, "On the representation of large odd integer as a sum of three almost equal primes," Acta Mathematica Sinica 7.3 (1991), 259-272]. Moreover, by our method, any improvement in large value estimates for character-twisted Dirichlet polynomials on the critical range would lead to a corresponding improvement in the lower bound for $H$.

items.title: Sharp stability for the Talenti inequality
items.summary: We prove a sharp quantitative version of the Talenti rearrangement inequality. Specifically, we show that, for any $p\in [1;+\infty]$, for any $f\in L^\infty(Ω),\, f\geq 0,\, f\not\equiv 0$, for any open set $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with finite volume, the solution $u_{f,Ω}$ to $-Δu_{f,Ω}=f,\, u_{f,Ω} \in W^{1,2}_0(Ω)$, satisfies, in dimension $d\geq 1$, $\Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)^2+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}\mathscr A(f,z)^2$ and, in dimension 1, $ \Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}}\mathscr A(f,z)^2$ where $α(Ω)$ denotes the Fraenkel asymmetry of $Ω$, $\mathscr A(f,z)$ a weighted asymmetry of $f$ with respect to some center $z$ and $Ω^\sharp$ (resp. $f^\sharp$) is the Schwarz rearrangement of $Ω$ (resp. of $f$). In dimension $d\geq 2$, this estimate implies $ \Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)^2+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}\Vert f-f^\sharp(\cdot-z)\Vert_{L^1}^2.$ Our result sharpens and extends recent quantitative versions, and does not rely on shape differentiation arguments, but on a generalisation of the quantitative Saint-Venant inequality.

items.title: Integral representations of high-order derivatives of Bessel functions with respect to the order
items.summary: We derive integral representations for the $n$-th derivative with respect to the order of Bessel functions of the first, second and third kinds, as well as the modified Bessel function and the Macdonald function. Based on these integral representations, we have developed a highly-efficient algorithm for the numerical evaluation of these derivatives with respect to the order, applicable to any complex argument and any real order.

items.title: A new lower bound for the sixth Schur number: $S(6)\ge 537$
items.summary: We give an explicit partition of $\{1,\ldots,537\}$ into six sum-free sets, establishing $S(6)\ge 537$. This improves the lower bound 536 of Fredricksen and Sweet (2000). Known recursive constructions then give the improved lower bounds $S(8)\ge 5\,372$, $S(11)\ge 204\,208$, $S(13)\ge 2\,042\,082$, and $R_6(3)\ge 539$. We also report 131 pairwise inequivalent partitions found by the search. We describe their structure and provide the complete partitions in the supplementary material. These partitions provide starting points for future searches and structural studies of Schur partitions.

items.title: Gradient Discrete Schrodinger Bridge Matching for Peptide Generation
items.summary: The optimal control of a discrete Schrödinger bridge is a discrete gradient, a difference of vertex potentials, but recent models such as MadSBM instead learn a free control on the edges by cross-entropy. We prove that this leaves the action uncontrolled: cross-entropy identifies the control only up to a state-dependent shift (a gauge), and the action is $\operatorname{KL}(r\|p)$ plus a gauge term the loss never constrains. We propose GDSBM, which writes the control as a difference of vertex potentials and adds the action to the loss; pinning the gauge costs no expressiveness and makes the action a property of the model, so the penalty acts on the model and not on the gauge. On peptide generation our MadSBM reimplementation has a free-gauge action of order $10^{8}$ for a gauge-fixed value of $6.5$, against $1.5$ for GDSBM, with no quality loss that three seeds can detect. The gradient form also fits guidance, which becomes the addition of a potential: guided toward a net charge of $+3$ at pH~7, GDSBM is closer than MadSBM, over three seeds, to its exact tempered target in total variation at every guidance strength (at $β=1$, $81\%$ of samples in the target window against $74\%$, for a target of $97\%$); we claim no statistical significance.

items.title: Prime Density, Kolmogorov Quotients and Homeomorphisms between Macías Spaces of Integral Domains
items.summary: For an integral domain $R$ that is not a field, the Macías space $M(R)$ is the set $R^0=R\setminus\{0\}$ endowed with the topology generated by the subsets $σ_k^0=\{x\in R^0:\langle x\rangle+\langle k\rangle=R\}$ for $k\in R^0$. We show that the unit group is open in $M(R)$ precisely when $R$ is not semiprimitive, and characterize semiprimitive Dedekind domains and unique factorization domains (UFDs) by means of the density of their irreducible and prime elements, respectively. We describe the Kolmogorov quotient of $M(R)$ in terms of the maximal ideals of $R$, and reduce the homeomorphism problem to these quotients and the cardinalities of the fibers of the quotient maps. Consequently, two local domains have homeomorphic Macías spaces if and only if they have the same cardinality. We characterize the pairs of Dedekind domains with homeomorphic Macías spaces in terms of the cardinalities of their unit groups and the relations among the ideal classes of their maximal ideals; in particular, two Dedekind domains with torsion class groups, such as principal ideal domains (PIDs), have homeomorphic Macías spaces if and only if their unit groups have the same cardinality and so do their sets of maximal ideals. This characterization addresses, for countably infinite semiprimitive PIDs, the homeomorphism problem raised by Macías in 2024. Under an additional hypothesis, UFDs admit an analogous characterization in terms of comaximality with prime elements. Finally, for a class of domains of characteristic zero, we characterize additive homeomorphisms between Macías spaces in terms of isomorphisms of the underlying rings, partially answering a problem raised by Macías and Ortiz in 2024.

items.title: Primes are Complete for a Class of Cantor Spectral Pair
items.summary: We study the complete number problem for a class of self-similar spectral measures on the real line. We say that a real number $t$ is complete for a spectral pair $(μ,Λ)$ if $(μ,tΛ)$ is also a spectral pair. In this paper we consider the partial homogeneous Cantor measure $μ_{N^r,\mathcal D}$ and its canonical spectrum. Our main result fully characterizes all prime powers $p^n$ that are complete for $p>N$. In particular, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for an arbitrary prime $p$ to be complete. {We further establish a connection between the problem and certain Diophantine equations}, including the Nagell--Ljunggren equation, and obtain complete number results for a class of related models. As applications, known solutions of the Nagell--Ljunggren equation provide complete and incomplete prime-power examples.

items.title: Sum-rank analogues of Reed--Muller codes over Abelian Galois extensions
items.summary: Let $\mathbb L/\mathbb K$ be a finite Abelian Galois extension with a fixed decomposition $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb L/\mathbb K)=\langleσ_1\rangle\times\cdots\times\langleσ_m\rangle$. We show that the quotient of the multivariate skew polynomial ring $\mathbb L[x_1,\ldots,x_m;σ_1,\ldots,σ_m]$ by suitable central polynomials $H_1(x_1),\ldots,H_m(x_m)$ is isomorphic to a product of $t$ copies of $\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb K}(\mathbb L)$, so that one skew polynomial represents all blocks of a sum-rank metric space. The sum-rank weight of an element equals the rank of an associated Dickson matrix and of a generalized Moore matrix. Using this, we define sum-rank Reed--Muller-type codes and show that their dimension and minimum distance are given by the formulas for affine Cartesian codes with side lengths $\mathrm{deg}\,H_1,\ldots,\mathrm{deg}\,H_m$; the same holds for codes supported on lower sets. The family contains as special cases linearized Reed--Solomon codes, Gabidulin codes, rank-metric Reed--Muller codes, and affine Cartesian codes. Over finite fields, every linearized Reed--Muller code of Berardini and Caruso is, after a monomial change of variables, a monomial code in our framework. This gives the dimension of all these codes, and their exact minimum distance in every degree whenever the support is a lower set.

items.title: Cluster scattering diagrams of acyclic affine type
items.summary: We give an explicit construction of the cluster scattering diagram for any acyclic exchange matrix of affine type. We show that the corresponding cluster scattering fan coincides both with the mutation fan and with a fan constructed in the almost-positive roots model.

items.title: Endpoint weighted Fourier estimate with vanishing spherical trace
items.summary: We establish an endpoint weighted Fourier estimate under a vanishing restriction condition on the unit sphere. Let $n \geq 2$ and $p_c = 2(n+1)/(n+3)$. We prove that every $f \in L^{p_c}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with zero spherical Fourier restriction satisfies $$ \left\| \bigl|1-|ξ|^2\bigr|^{-1/2}\widehat{f}(ξ) \right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)} \leq C_n \|f\|_{L^{p_c}(\mathbb{R}^n)}, $$ where the restriction condition is understood through the continuous Tomas--Stein restriction operator. This result gives a negative answer to Goldberg's counterexample-existence question and supplies a missing endpoint.

items.title: The smallest singular value for rectangular random matrices with Lévy entries
items.summary: Let $X=(x_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ be a rectangular random matrix with i.i.d. entries (we assume $N/n\to\mathbf{a}>1$), and denote by $σ_{min}(X)$ its smallest singular value. When entries have mean zero and unit second moment, the celebrated work of Bai-Yin and Tikhomirov show that $n^{-\frac{1}{2}}σ_{min}(X)$ converges almost surely to $\sqrt{\mathbf{a}}-1.$ However, little is known when the second moment is infinite. In this work we consider symmetric entry distributions satisfying $\mathbb{P}(|x_{ij}|>t)\asymp t^{-α}$ for some $α\in(0,2)$, and prove that $σ_{min}(X)$ can be determined up to a log factor with high probability: for any $D>0$, with probability at least $1-n^{-D}$ we have $$C_1n^{\frac{1}α}(\log n)^\frac{2(α-2)}α\leq σ_{min}(X)\leq C_2n^{\frac{1}α}(\log n)^\frac{α-2}{2α}$$ for some constants $C_1,C_2>0$. The upper bound was derived in a recent work of Bao, Lee and Xu \cite{bao2024phase2} but the lower bound is new and answers a problem posed in that paper in a weaker form. This appears to be the first determination of $σ_{min}(X)$ in the $α$-stable case with a correct leading order of $n$, as previous anti-concentration arguments only yield lower bound $n^\frac{1}{2}$. The same lower bound holds for $σ_{min}(X+B)$ for any fixed rectangular matrix $B$ with no assumption on its operator norm. The case of diverging aspect ratio is also computed.

items.title: A declarative approach to specifying Paxos using three-valued modal fixpoint logic
items.summary: We present Three-valued Fixpoint Quorum Logic, or 3muQL for short; a three-valued modal fixed-point logic designed for declaratively specifying and reasoning about distributed algorithms, such as the Paxos consensus algorithm. Our methodology represents a distributed algorithm as a logical theory, enabling correctness properties to be derived directly within the framework -- or revealing logical errors in the algorithm's design when they exist. 3muQL adopts a declarative approach, specifying the overall logic of computation without prescribing control flow. Notably, message-passing and state-transitions are not explicitly modelled, and notions of 'quorum' are abstracted from concrete thresholds to abstract modal operators. This distinguishes our framework from approaches like TLA+. The logical abstraction emphasises the essence of distributed algorithms, offering a novel perspective on their specification and reasoning. We define the syntax and semantics of 3muQL, explore its theoretical properties, and demonstrate its applicability through a detailed treatment of the Paxos consensus algorithm. By presenting Paxos as a logical theory and deriving its standard correctness properties, we showcase the framework's capacity to handle non-trivial distributed systems. We envision 3muQL as a versatile tool for specifying and reasoning about distributed algorithms. The Paxos example highlights the framework's ability to capture intricate details, offering a new lens through which distributed algorithms can be specified, studied, and checked. The ideas we present are easily implemented, and to demonstrate this we have implemented a freely-available proof-of- concept 3muQL model-checker, as an effective prototyping tool.

items.title: The shifted symplectic geometry of derived higher groupoids
items.summary: The main goal of this work is to introduce derived Lie n-groupoids and their shifted symplectic structures. We further define shifted lagrangian structures and prove that their composition is well defined under suitable conditions. As an application, we show that our framework incorporates several reduction procedures at critical values, including: classical Hamiltonian reduction, group valued moment maps, Poisson Lie group valued moment maps and Mikami-Weinstein for proper symplectic groupoids.

items.title: Regulator Constants and Cohomology
items.summary: We show how regulator constants of a finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module can be related to $G$-cohomology, where $G$ is a finite group. We then derive consequences of such relation for modules naturally arising in number theory, such as ring of integers and units of number fields, $K$-theory groups of ring of integers and Mordell-Weil groups of elliptic curves.

items.title: A sharp diameter-mass inequality on Einstein manifolds and ADM mass
items.summary: Let $(M^n,g), n\geq 4$ be a close Einstein manifold with positive scalar curvature and $G$ be the Green function of the conformal Laplacian. The ADM mass of the asymptotically flat metric $\hat g:=G^{4/(n-2)} g$ is an important geometric invariant. When either $n=5$ or $n\geq 6$ with Weyl vanishing condition, we prove a mass formula, generalizing Gursky-Malchiodi's formula in dimension $4$. An important step is an extension of Viaclovsky's Green function expansion in higher dimensions. Next we prove a sharp diameter-mass inequality on Einstein manifolds. Finally we present two applications. First, we prove a mass gap theorem for Einstein manifolds. Second, for Collins-Székelyhidi's family of Sasaki-Einstein metrics $g_i$ on $\mathbb{S}^5$ with volume going to zero, the sequence of the masses $m(\hat{g_i})$ blows up uniformly as $i\to\infty$.

items.title: Lawlor's curvature criterion and topologically trivial area-minimizing hypercones of Hsiang type
items.summary: For a closed embedded minimal hypersurface in a unit sphere, we show that the existence of a uniform vanishing angle in Lawlor's criterion suffices for its cone to minimize area. The normal-wedge condition follows from Howard's rolling theorem. We derive explicit curvature bounds and apply them to the reported Hsiang-Sterling curvature estimates for topologically trivial cones. The resulting area-minimizing cones give an affirmative answer to the existence question raised by Ilmanen and White (Camb. J. Math., 2015).

items.title: What the submission does not show: Complexifying cognitive offloading in students' mathematical work with LLMs
items.summary: A common concern is that using large language models (LLMs) lets students offload mathematical work that tasks are designed to elicit. Yet such claims often rest on outcomes (e.g., submitted solutions), rather than on evidence of students' work with LLMs. We followed 23 first-year linear algebra students as they solved three differently designed homework tasks with LLMs. Drawing on self-regulated learning and choice-affluent environments, we interpreted each of 429 prompts as a trace of a regulatory event and compared 59 chatlogs with the problem solutions the students submitted. Prompts formed five structures, casting the LLM mainly as a solver, explainer, or validator. The mix of structures shifted across the tasks, and ten of the 15 students who completed all three tasks changed their dominant structure. Most final submissions stayed close to LLM output, including those that followed exchanges in which students had explained, conjectured, and checked their own ideas. We conclude that an LLM-aided submission is not a trustworthy marker of students' offloading of the mathematical work, and that offloading needs to be examined in each regulatory space and part by part rather than as a whole.

items.title: Fragility-aware Classification for Risk Characterization and Robust Learning
items.summary: Classification models play a central role in data-driven decision-making applications such as medical diagnosis, recommendation systems, and risk assessment. Traditional performance metrics, such as accuracy and AUC, quantify classification errors and pairwise ranking performance but do not account for the magnitude of errors, i.e., the risk of confident misjudgments. This limitation is particularly consequential in safety-critical and cost-sensitive settings, where overconfident errors can lead to severe outcomes. To address this issue, we propose the Fragility Index (FI), a novel performance metric that evaluates classifiers from a risk-averse perspective by capturing the tail risk of confident misjudgments. We formulate FI within a robust satisficing (RS) framework to quantify classifier sensitivity under distributional uncertainty. Building on this, we develop a tractable surrogate-based training framework and establish provable bounds connecting training fragility to ranking-error FI. We further derive tractable reformulations for a broad class of loss functions, including cross-entropy, hinge-type, and Lipschitz losses, and identify specific conditions under which these reformulations are exact. We also introduce an FI-induced regularizer for deep neural networks. Empirical results on real-world medical diagnosis tasks demonstrate that FI complements existing metrics by revealing error tail risk not reflected in accuracy or AUC. FI-based models achieve competitive predictive performance while generally attaining lower FI. In the simulated human--AI diagnostic workflow, they also achieve lower average operational costs than empirical risk minimization.

items.title: Sketching Outside the Hilbert Space for the Infinite-Dimensional Randomised SVD
items.summary: In randomised numerical linear algebra, common choices for distributions of sketch vectors $ω\in \mathbb R^n$ are isotropic, so that $\mathbb E[ωω^T]=I_n$. Unfortunately, the natural extension of an isotropic vector in $(\mathbb R^n, \|\cdot \|_{2})$ to an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ may not exist as an element of the space, posing an obstacle for any attempt to lift the randomised SVD to infinite-dimensional target operators $A$. Current workarounds either forego isotropy and take $ω$ to be a continuous Gaussian process with trace-class covariance operators, or leave $ω$ implicit by instead sampling $Aω$ as if $ω$ were isotropic Gaussian. We unify their approaches by introducing "sketch functionals", an example of cylindrical random variables (Vakhania--Tarieladze--Chobanyan 1987) which allow us to treat general, non-Gaussian distributions with bounded covariance operators. To demonstrate the utility of the new theory, we apply it to develop novel bounds for the infinite-dimensional randomised SVD with a general class of sub-Gaussian sketch distributions.

items.title: Convex-like Submanifolds, Caps and a Volume Comparison Theorem
items.summary: Convex-like submanifolds in the Lorentz-Minkowski spaces are introduced in this paper as a natural and broad generalization of convex surfaces in the Euclidean space. Associated with such a convex-like submanifold in a Minkowski space, we define roofs (which resembles the supporting planes), caps (which are generated by the light rays in the normal bundle), and towers (which revives the notion of interior for such high codimensional objects). As a touchstone of this theory, a volume comparison theorem is proved, which is a non-trivial generalization of the obvious fact that among two nested convex surfaces, the outer one has larger volume. Finally we provide two important applications of this theorem.

items.title: Dissipation Bounds and Hardness in Globally Asymptotically Stable Quadratic Systems
items.summary: Approximating the maximum retained energy fraction in globally asymptotically stable quadratic systems of growing dimension is NP-hard at every fixed positive additive error below $1/2$, even when strict quartic Lyapunov functions and strictness proofs are constructed in polynomial time and included in the input. Polynomial-factor approximation is also NP-hard for the least dissipated fraction, energy-halving time and structured coefficient distance to loss of asymptotic stability. For a partially damped family, minimum unit-sphere coupling norm equals that distance, with two-sided inverse-square halving-time bounds at distances in $(0,1/2]$ and explicit coefficient factors. Additive hardness persists under structured coefficient perturbations and direct damping, even with global exponential stability, a strict quadratic Lyapunov function and a Hurwitz Jacobian.

items.title: Deep Learning for Random Objects in Metric Spaces: Beyond Manifold Assumptions
items.summary: Deep learning (DL) methods have substantially improved predictive performance across a wide range of downstream prediction tasks, enabling new discoveries in multiple domains. However, principled DL methods for non-Euclidean random objects remain relatively scarce, despite the growing importance of modern biomedical outcomes taking the form of probability distributions, random graphs, functions, and other random objects in metric spaces. Motivated by a new generation of digital and clinical biomarkers, we propose a deep learning framework for regression with random objects in metric spaces. Our approach operates directly on the metric structure of the response space, avoiding restrictive manifold or Euclidean embedding assumptions imposed by many existing methods. At the same time, it retains modern statistical guarantees under the stated statistical assumptions. We establish statistical consistency and convergence rates for the proposed estimator, and characterize conditions under which it can mitigate the curse of dimensionality for hierarchically compositional regression functions. Extensive simulation studies demonstrate competitive predictive performance, with gains over several competing approaches in multiple Euclidean and non-Euclidean configurations. Finally, we demonstrate the practical utility of the proposed framework in two digital health case studies with distribution-valued outcomes in Wasserstein spaces, using high-resolution accelerometry and continuous glucose monitoring data. Embedding-based deep-learning methods may be less suitable when no informative low-dimensional representation exists or when the learned embedding does not adequately preserve the intrinsic geometry of the response space.

items.title: Typical periodic optimization and freezing phase transition: Dini potentials and beyond
items.summary: We investigate the Typical Periodic Optimization (TPO) Conjecture and freezing phase transitions for Dini potentials and beyond. We show that the TPO conjecture fails already at Dini regularity. We identify a sharp regularity threshold for freezing phase transitions, which we call weak log-log Dini. Both results reveal the stability of aperiodic ground states. Moreover, we identify Dini regularity as the sharp threshold for a quantitatitve analog of the freezing phase transition.

items.title: A partial result towards the Chowla--Milnor conjecture
items.summary: The Chowla--Milnor conjecture predicts the linear independence of certain Hurwitz zeta values. In this paper, we prove that for any fixed integer $k \geqslant 2$, the dimension of the $\mathbb{Q}$-linear span of $ζ(k,a/q)-(-1)^{k}ζ(k,1-a/q)$ ($1 \leqslant a < q/2$, $\gcd(a,q)=1$) is at least $(c -o(1)) \cdot \log q$ as the positive integer $q \to +\infty$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. It is well known that $ζ(k,a/q)+(-1)^{k}ζ(k,1-a/q) \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}π^k$, but much less is known previously for $ζ(k,a/q)-(-1)^{k}ζ(k,1-a/q)$. Our proof is similar to those of Ball--Rivoal (2001) and Zudilin (2002) concerning the linear independence of Riemann zeta values. However, we use a new type of rational functions to construct linear forms.

items.title: On the pro-Kummer étale cohomology of $\mathbb B_{\operatorname{dR}}$
items.summary: We investigate $p$-adic cohomologies of log rigid analytic varieties over a $p$-adic field. For a log rigid analytic variety $X$ defined over a discretely valued field, we compute the Kummer pro-étale cohomology of $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$ and $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}$. When $X$ is defined over $\mathbb{C}_p$, we introduce a logarithmic ${B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-cohomology theory, serving as a deformation of log de Rham cohomology. Additionally, we establish the log de Rham-étale comparison in this setting and prove the degeneration of both the Hodge-Tate and Hodge-log de Rham spectral sequences when $X$ is proper and log smooth.

items.title: Multiple SLEs and Dyson Brownian motion: transition density and Green's function
items.summary: We consider multiple chordal Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) with $κ\in (0,4]$. Under common-time parameterization, we show that the transition density of the driving function of multiple chordal SLEs can be given by the transition density of Dyson Brownian motion and Green's function. This is a companion paper of [FWY24].

items.title: The Limits of Arithmetical Pluralism: Incompleteness, Large Cardinals, and Graded Non-Pluralism
items.summary: Gödelian incompleteness yields arithmetical sentences \(A\) such that \(\mathsf{PA}+A\) and \(\mathsf{PA}+\neg A\) are both consistent. Are such extensions equally legitimate? I propose graded epistemic arithmetical non-pluralism: justification for choosing between them varies with the set-theoretic strength of \(A\). I defend \(\mathsf{PA}+\mathsf{Con}(\mathsf{PA})\) and show that Friedman's concrete incompleteness results pose a serious challenge to non-pluralism about first-order arithmetic. Resolving the selection problem for such sentences turns on justifying large cardinals. Defending graded non-pluralism thus engages Gödel's programme and the justification of very large cardinals.

items.title: Segre determinants and MHV gravity amplitudes
items.summary: We describe a Segre-Veronese construction of polynomial solutions to the interpolation conditions of the numerators of tree-level MHV gravity amplitudes given by Hodges' formula. The five- and six-point Hodges numerators arise from Segre determinants, while for every $n\geq7$ suitable Segre determinants lead to solutions linearly independent of the Hodges numerator. The existence of such independent elements for $n=7,8$ was recently established by Mai and Zhang.

items.title: Central limit theorem in Rényi divergence for lattice random variables
items.summary: Let $\{X_i\}_{i=1}^n$ be independent, identically distributed lattice random variables with zero mean, unit variance, and maximal span $h>0$. Let $S_n=(X_1+\cdots+X_n)/\sqrt n$. Let $Z_n$ denote the quantization of a standard Gaussian random variable on the support lattice of $S_n$. We show that the Rényi divergence $D_α(S_n\|Z_n)$ of order $1<α<\infty$ tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$ if and only if $D_α(S_{n_0}\| Z_{n_0})<\infty$ for some integer $n_0$ and a sub-Gaussian condition holds. Furthermore, we derive an Edgeworth-type asymptotic expansion of the divergence to arbitrary order. We also show that the Rényi divergence $D_\infty(S_n\|Z_n)$ of infinite order tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$ if and only if a sub-Gaussian condition, a curvature condition, and a uniform separation condition hold. These results constitute lattice counterparts of Rényi entropic central limit theorems for continuous random variables obtained by Bobkov, Chistyakov and Götze (\emph{Ann. Probab.} \textbf{47} (2019), 270--323) and Bobkov and Götze (\emph{Ann. Probab.} \textbf{53} (2025), 453--477). Uniform separation is an additional assumption beyond the sub-Gaussian and curvature conditions used in the continuous setting. The failure of uniform separation may cause an exponentially tilted version of $X_1$ to concentrate on a sublattice of max span $kh$ for some integer $k>1$, which yields the lower bound $D_\infty(S_n\|Z_n)\ge\log k$, and hence a failure of the entropic central limit theorem.

items.title: Atomic limits of empirical measures of interacting particle systems with self-duality
items.summary: We study the fixed-particle limit of empirical measures for a unified self-dual family of conservative particle systems on $\mathbb{Z}^d$: independent random walkers, the symmetric exclusion process, and the symmetric inclusion process. For a fixed number of particles $k$, under diffusive space-time scaling parametrised by $n$, we prove that as $n\to\infty$ the normalised empirical measure converges in $D([0,T],\mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R}^d))$ to an atomic empirical measure carried by $k$ independent diffusions, with constant covariance determined by the microscopic jump kernel. Equivalently, the limit is the unique atomic solution of the Dean-Kawasaki martingale problem with mass quantisation $1/k$. In particular, exclusion and inclusion have the same fixed-$k$ atomic limit as independent walkers: the interaction contributes only through microscopic near-collisions, whose rescaled occupation time vanishes. The proof combines self-duality, consistency-based reduction to two particles, and Green-function estimates for finite perturbations of symmetric random walks.

items.title: An improvement of the large sieve for square moduli under Hooley's hypothesis $R^*$ for short Salié sums
items.summary: Let $S(Q,M,N,(a_n))=\sum_{q\le Q}\sum_{a\bmod q^2,(a,q)=1}|\sum_{M<n\le M+N}a_ne(an/q^2)|^2$ be Zhao's large sieve sum with square moduli. Zhao conjectured that $S\ll(QN)^ε(Q^3+N)\sum|a_n|^2$. The bound of Baier and Zhao (2008) exceeds this conjecture by a factor which reaches $Q^{1/2}$ at the critical point $N=Q^3$, and there the exponent $1/2$ has not been lowered since. We prove that, under Hooley's Hypothesis $R^*$ for short Salié sums, $S\ll(QN)^ε(Q^3+N+Q^{4/3}N^{2/3})\sum|a_n|^2$. This replaces the excess over Zhao's conjecture by its $2/3$-th power throughout the range $Q^{5/2}<N<Q^4$; at $N=Q^3$ it gives $S\ll Q^{1/2-1/6+ε}N\sum|a_n|^2$. The proof is short. Following Zhao's original treatment, we approximate the point under consideration by fractions $b/r$ with denominators up to $Q^{2/3}N^{1/3}$, which for $N<Q^4$ is beyond the customary $\sqrt{N}$. If the approximation is poor, an elementary count suffices. If it is good, the analytic part of the problem disappears: after Poisson summation in both variables the count is expressed through quadratic Gauss sums, and their exact evaluation at every modulus turns the sum over the dual variable into short Kloosterman and Salié sums, to which Hypothesis $R^*$ applies and gives the square root of the elementary count. At odd moduli the hypothesis is needed only in the form of Conjecture (C*) of Friedlander and Iwaniec. The Gauss-sum evaluations, including even moduli and coefficients sharing a factor with the modulus, are proved in full. This version supersedes earlier versions, which obtained the exponent $1/2-1/28$ at $N=Q^3$ by a much longer route through sums of modular square roots. The paper was prepared in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic).

items.title: Exponential decay of fractional moments in the $H^{2|2}$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$
items.summary: For the $H^{2|2}$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$, we show that, at energy zero, the fractional moments of Green functions, $\mathbb E[ G(x,y)^s]$ decay exponentially in the distance between $x$ and $y$, for every constant edge weight $W>0$ and every $0<s<1/2$. Here $ G$ is the infinite-volume Green function of the associated random Schrödinger operator. The main ingredient is a quantitative lower bound on the derivative of the mean effective conductance with respect to the edge weights.

items.title: Mathematical AI Predicts 40% and 57% Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Against H1N1 and H3N2, Respectively, for the 2026--2027 U.S. Season
items.summary: Background: Clinical influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) has often been low over the past two decades, highlighting the need for preseason VE forecasting. Timely forecasts could help health authorities plan prevention strategies and allocate healthcare resources. However, preseason forecasting of clinical influenza VE remains relatively uncommon. Methods: We obtained hemagglutinin (HA) sequences from GISAID for U.S. specimens collected in August--September before each influenza season from 2010--2011 through 2024--2025. After quality screening, we compared each virus with the corresponding vaccine target strain for the same season and subtype or lineage using two mathematical distances based on amino acid patterns in the HA protein. We calculated mean distances for each season and subtype or lineage and paired them with published clinical VE estimates, yielding 26 observations across 13 seasons. Using a mathematical AI approach, we fitted linear regression models of VE against each distance and evaluated their predictive performance by forecasting later seasons using data from earlier seasons, with the historical mean VE for each subtype or lineage as a reference. We then applied the same approach to 87 HA sequences collected in August--September 2026 to forecast VE for the 2026--2027 season. Results: We generated component-specific forecasts of influenza VE for the upcoming 2026--2027 U.S. season. Both mathematical distances were negatively associated with historical VE, indicating that greater differences between circulating viruses and vaccine strains were associated with lower VE. The topological model forecast VE of 40.3%, 56.9%, and 47.1% against A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria, respectively, whereas the geometric model forecast corresponding VE values of 34.0%, 56.8%, and 51.1%.

items.title: Strong Duality Thresholds and Minimum Curvature for the Nearest Rectangular Symplectic Matrix Problem
items.summary: We study the nearest rectangular symplectic matrix problem in the squared Frobenius norm for arbitrary targets $T\in\mathbb R^{2n\times2k}$, with $n\ge k$. We prove that its semidefinite relaxation is exact for every target if and only if $n\ge2k-1$. Under this condition, the primal problem, the relaxation, and both Lagrangian dual problems attain the same optimal value. In this range, we derive the exact minimum Rayleigh quotient of the Riemannian Hessian at every feasible point under the Euclidean induced metric, and prove that all second-order stationary points are global minimizers. We also obtain global objective error bounds. We extend the strong-duality and minimum-curvature results to Hermitian positive definite row weights, proving that strong duality holds for every target if and only if the lowest eigenvalue of the weight has complex multiplicity at least $2k-1$. The dual formulation leads to a method whose main iterations use matrices of order $2k$, with $O(k^2)$ iterative storage apart from the full input and output. Across six tested sizes, mean-time speedups are $2.55$--$12.60$ over a Riemannian first-order method and $4.61$--$43.93$ over Jensen--Zimmermann R--TR2; batching gives a further factor of $3.45$--$23.53$ over sequential calls. The theoretical results complete the critical dimensions not covered by Gram convexification and quadratic matrix programming.

items.title: Model Predictive Control of Wind Turbines: A Model-Oriented Review of Prediction Models, Control Objectives, and Nonlinear Aerodynamic Formulations
items.summary: Model predictive control (MPC) has been applied to wind-turbine regulation with markedly different internal prediction models, ranging from linearized low-order turbine models to nonlinear, aeroelastic, floating, and data-driven predictors. This review organizes the literature primarily by the model propagated by the controller and treats model order, predictor representation, MPC formulation, control objective, and validation plant as separate descriptors. Primary studies show that low-order linear or piecewise-affine predictors are attractive for constrained power and speed regulation, whereas flexible drivetrain, structural, and floating models are needed when drivetrain twist, tower motion, blade loads, or platform dynamics are explicit control quantities. Nonlinear and economic MPC studies further demonstrate coordinated pitch/torque control across broad operating regions, while preview, repetitive, and data-driven formulations address wind prediction, periodic loads, and model mismatch. Particular attention is given to aerodynamic pitch dependence: variable-pitch turbine dynamics can be non-affine with respect to applied pitch, and the term NMPC alone does not prove that the original nonlinear pitch map is retained inside the optimizer. The review therefore adopts a conservative, equation-based classification for direct nonlinear applied-pitch propagation. Here, direct nonlinear applied-pitch propagation means that the applied pitch at each prediction step is evaluated inside the original nonlinear aerodynamic map, rather than replacing that dependence by a linearized, scheduled, piecewise-affine, or learned surrogate. The literature supports a remaining integration challenge at the intersection of flexible drivetrain prediction, nonlinear aerodynamic pitch treatment, explicit constraints and load objectives, and validated adaptive or learned model correction.

items.title: Cohomology of integral structure sheaves for open varieties
items.summary: We study the cohomology of integral structure sheaves for two types of open rigid analytic varieties: complements of divisors in quasi-compact varieties, and partially proper spaces. As applications, we prove a strengthened form of the Hebbarkeitssatz (Riemann's extension theorem), involving the almost vanishing of $R^1\lim$, and study pro-étale $G$-torsors on open varieties.

items.title: Three-orbifolds, positive scalar curvature and fundamental group
items.summary: We show that closed Riemannian 3-orbifolds with positive scalar curvature have virtually free fundamental group. We also build a family of closed 3-orbifolds with free fundamental group of rank 2 which do not admit Riemannian metrics of positive scalar curvature.

items.title: Optimal weighted sampling of positive and normal operator orbits
items.summary: We study weighted sampling of operator orbit frames in infinite dimensional separable Hilbert spaces \(H\), keeping the operator and generating vectors fixed. Let $N_μ(R)$ count the sampling times in $[0,R]$. For a single orbit of a positive operator, let $m_A(R)$ count the eigenvalues in $(0,e^{-1/R}]$. Every real sampling design that preserves the frame property must satisfy the lower bound $N_μ(R)\ge m_A(R)-O_μ(1)$. Conversely, for every $η>0$, we construct an integer sampling design that preserves the frame property and satisfies $N_μ(R)\le(1+η)m_A(R)+O_η(1)$. Thus the coefficient $1$ is optimal. Under additional spectral conditions, we attain $N_μ(R)=m_A(R)+O(1)$ and characterize the weights that preserve the frame property on the constructed sets. For finitely or countably many orbits of a positive operator, let $P_j$, $j\ge1$, be the spectral projection corresponding to $2^{-j-1}<-\logλ\le2^{-j}$ and define $K_A(R)=\#\{j\ge1:2^j\le R,\ P_j\ne0\}$. Every real sampling design that preserves the frame property satisfies $N_μ(R)\ge c_μK_A(R)-C_μ$ for $R\ge2$, with constants $c_μ>0$ and $C_μ\ge0$. Conversely, we construct an integer sampling design that preserves the frame property and satisfies $N_μ(R)\le L K_A(R)+L$ for $R\ge2$, where $L$ depends only on the bounds of the given orbit frame. For normal operators of norm one, we prove that the smallest frame condition number is attained among integer sampling designs that preserve the frame property and satisfy a prescribed counting bound, whenever this class is nonempty. Finally, we construct one normal operator with two families of generating vectors for which the optimal growth orders of $N_μ(R)$ are $\log R$ and $R$, respectively, for both real and integer sampling.

items.title: Numerical reconstruction of polygonal obstacles by diffracted waves
items.summary: We present a numerical method for recovering rigid polygonal obstacles in two dimensions, based on the diffraction-based inverse scattering theory of Bao, Chen, Lu, and Xiong. A single pulse is emitted from a point source, and the resulting wave field is measured on a receiver curve. After isolating the diffracted signals, we recover the visible vertices from arrival times and the corner orientations and opening angles from amplitudes. The use of amplitude information permits local reconstruction in the reflection shadow, where reflected waves do not reach the receiver. The amplitudes also determine the direction of a shadowed edge adjacent to a visible vertex, enabling local non-line-of-sight imaging. Numerical experiments for a convex corner, a concave corner, a triangle, a pentagon and a star-shaped obstacle confirm that the visible portion of the boundary can be recovered stably from diffracted signals. A further convex-corner test with additive noise at level $0.2\%$ on the single arc $L_1$ confirms that the tip and opening remain recoverable.

items.title: Continuation and convergence for the higher dimensional conformal Chern--Calabi flow
items.summary: We study the volume-normalized gradient flow of the squared Chern scalar curvature on compact Hermitian manifolds of complex dimension $n\ge3$. The flow extends smoothly past a finite time if the spatial supremum of Chern scalar curvature belongs to $L^2$ in time. A uniform curvature bound in the evolving $L^p$ norm, for one fixed $p>n$, gives global existence and smooth convergence of the whole trajectory to a constrained critical metric. On Chern scalar-flat backgrounds, small initial $L^p$ curvature gives exponential convergence to the background. A corresponding condition on the trace-free first Chern--Ricci form gives exponential convergence on Chern--Ricci-flat Hermitian and positive Kähler--Einstein backgrounds. The smallness thresholds are independent of the initial higher derivatives. We also construct constant Chern scalar curvature backgrounds of either sign with arbitrarily small smooth perturbations whose solutions, if global, cannot converge back to the background.

items.title: Simultaneous Matrix Multiplication by Tensor Contraction Aggregation
items.summary: We present an interpretation of the fast matrix multiplication algorithms of Coppersmith and Winograd as aggregations of tensor contractions. This point of view provides a direct connection to older constructions by Pan and to more recent work on bilinear algorithms for symmetric tensor contraction. Further, we provide a simple explicit approach for exact aggregation of tensor contractions, each one yielding an independent matrix-matrix product. These constructions and border rank adaptations thereof do not come close to improving the best known bounds on $ω$ (the matrix multiplication exponent), but provide explicit moderate-size fast matrix multiplication algorithms that achieve a better exponent than Strassen's algorithm and have potential practical value. These finite constructions improve the multiplication-count bounds of the reference algorithms compared here for selected numbers and dimensions of independent square matrix products.
