In particular, using $\langle m,m,m\rangle$ to denote the matrix multiplication tensor for matrices of dimension $m$, we obtain constructions that give bounds such as the border rank bound \[ \underline R\!\left(\langle n^2,n^2,n^2\rangle^{\oplus9}\right) \le (n+1)^6+6(n+1)^5, \] and the exact rank bound \[ R\!\left(\langle n^3,n^3,n^3\rangle^{\oplus14}\right)\le (n+1)^9. \] We quantify the accuracy of such constructions in finite precision, and provide border-rank constructions that reduce cost with limiting retained fractions of accuracy at least $1/2$, $1/3$, or $1/4$ relative to the classical matrix-multiplication approach under the stated error model.

items.title: Unipotent representations and the categorical trace of Frobenius
items.summary: We give a new proof of the classification of unipotent representations for split finite groups of Lie type. To do this, we first construct an (infinity, 2)-categorification of Lusztig's map from the Hecke algebra to the asymptotic algebra. Then we use the theory of weights to show that it induces an isomorphism after applying trace of Frobenius.

items.title: Locked Polyomino Tilings
items.summary: A locked $t$-omino tiling is a grid tiling by $t$-ominoes such that, if you remove any pair of tiles, the only way to fill in the remaining $2t$ grid cells with $t$-ominoes is to use the same two tiles in the exact same configuration as before. We exclude degenerate cases where there is only one tiling overall due to small dimensions. It is a classic (and straightforward) result that finite grids do not admit locked 2-omino tilings. In this paper, we construct explicit locked $t$-omino tilings for $t\geq3$ on square and rectangular grids of various dimensions. We show that locked 3- and 4-omino tilings exist on finite square grids of arbitrarily large size. The result for 4-omino tilings in particular is remarkable because they are so rare and difficult to construct: Only a single tiling is known to exist on any grid up to size $40\times40$. We also find locked 5- and 6-omino tilings, and provide a computer-assisted proof that locked 7-omino tilings do not exist on any rectangular grid. In a weighted version of the problem where vertices of the grid may have weights from the set $\{1,2\}$ that count toward the total tile size, we demonstrate the existence of locked tilings on arbitrarily large square weighted grids with only 6 tiles. Finally, we construct locked $t$-omino tilings of the infinite grid for arbitrarily large $t$. Locked $t$-omino tilings arise as obstructions to widely used political redistricting algorithms in a model of redistricting where the underlying census geography is a grid graph. Most prominent is the ReCom Markov chain, which takes a random walk on the space of redistricting plans by iteratively merging and splitting pairs of districts (tiles) at a time. Locked $t$-omino tilings are isolated states in the state space of ReCom. The constructions in this paper are counterexamples to the meta-conjecture that ReCom is irreducible on graphs of practical interest.

items.title: Radial $Φ^4$ models in supercritical regimes
items.summary: We consider the $Φ^4_d$ measure under radial symmetry on the unit ball, formally given by $$dρ(u) = \frac 1 Z \exp\Big( - \frac 14 \int_{B_1} |u|^4 dx - \frac 12 \int_{B_1} |\nabla u|^2 dx\Big) d u, $$ where $u$ is restricted to radially symmetric functions with 0 boundary conditions. We prove that for every dimension $d$, there exists such a measure, which is concentrated on $L^p(B_1)$ for every $p < \frac{2d}{d-2}$ (for every $p < \infty$ if $d \le 2$). Furthermore, we show that these measures are not Gaussian, and when $d \ge 4$, they are singular with respect to the underlying Gaussian measure. We achieve this result by first defining the measure $ρ^+_δ[λ]$ on the shell $\{δ\le |x| \le 1\}$, $0 < δ< 1$, with a boundary condition on the sphere of radius $δ$ of the form $u|_{\{|x| = δ\}} = λ$. Then we prove that this measure satisfies a variational formula, and use it to show moment bounds which are uniform in the boundary value $λ$. A crucial ingredient in this argument is the fact that every solution of the elliptic equation $-Δu + u^3 = 0$ on the annulus $\{ δ\le |x| \le 1 \}$ satisfies uniform bounds inside the domain, independently of the boundary conditions.

items.title: Log blow-ups and global resolutions in rigid geometry
items.summary: In this article, we study log blow-ups in the setting of log adic spaces. As in the theory of log schemes, we prove the existence of global resolutions of toric singularities for fs log adic spaces log smooth over a $p$-adic field, and the acyclicity of certain sheaves under log blow-ups. One new feature of (log) rigid analytic varieties is their integral structure sheaf: we prove that it is also almost acyclic under log blow-ups in the Kummer étale topology. We also supply some foundational results on log adic spaces.

items.title: Deep ReLU Networks Can Fail the Best Approximation Property for Continuous Target Functions
items.summary: We construct a continuous function on $[-1,1]^2$ for which the infimum of the $L^2$-approximation error over the class of ReLU networks with two hidden layers and architecture $(2,2,1,1)$ is not attained. This counterexample shows that deep ReLU networks do not satisfy the best approximation property in general, even for continuous target functions. Our findings contrast with existing results for shallow neural networks, where ReLU is one of the few activation functions that guarantee the existence of global minima in typical regression tasks. The proof is based on the fact that the breaklines for neurons in the second hidden layer can bend, which breaks the symmetry arguments used in the one-hidden-layer case.

items.title: A New Minimax Theorem for a Class of $C^1$-Functionals
items.summary: We establish a new abstract minimax theorem for obtaining ground-state critical points of a class of \(C^{1}\)-functionals. The central feature of this class is that the associated Nehari set is not necessarily a differentiable manifold, but is homeomorphic to a (possibly non-complete) submanifold of the unit sphere. This occurs for functionals whose fibering maps \(t \mapsto I(tu)\) possess a unique global maximum point only when \(u\) belongs to an open cone in the underlying Banach space. A lower semicontinuous boundary barrier, which may be finite, controls minimizing sequences near the boundary of the spherical cone. As a consequence, we provide a general minimax characterization of the ground-state energy level. Elliptic applications complement existing results and include superlinear and quasilinear problems with finite barriers, including thresholds depending on the profile of a first eigenfunction and its gradient.

items.title: On orbits of the automorphism group of toroidal spherical varieties
items.summary: In this paper we study the orbits of the automorphism group on a toroidal spherical variety. In the affine case, we prove that two points lie in the same orbit of the identity component if and only if the kernels of the homomorphisms from the divisor class group to their local divisor class groups coincide. These kernels are described in terms of $B$-stable prime divisors. For a smooth complete toroidal spherical variety, we obtain a similar criterion using the monoids generated by the classes of $B$-stable prime divisors that do not contain a given $G$-orbit.

items.title: Chaos of Caputo derivative
items.summary: We study bounded realizations of Caputo differentiation on coefficient Banach spaces of fractional power series. The main contribution is an explicit quantitative analysis of local approximation and periodic reconstruction. We determine the least possible simultaneous error in the initial displacement and the prescribed target. The optimal value is attained, and a minimizing perturbation is given explicitly. We also solve the exact-arrival problem and establish uniqueness of its least-norm solution. These formulas provide computable approximation times and identify the sharp threshold for hypercyclicity, mixing and Devaney chaos. Every periodic point is described by a finite block whose geometric repetition yields exact norm formulas. The resulting approximations attain any prescribed sufficiently large minimal period near any given vector. For distinct positive powers, a simultaneous block construction gives quantitative error estimates and the same sharp threshold for disjoint mixing. Compact embeddings relate the Banach realizations to the Mittag-Leffler-Caputo Fréchet space. They also exhibit dense stable invariant subspaces inside chaotic realizations. The local approximation condition is a norm formulation of classical transitivity. Its quantitative evaluation, together with explicit periodic and simultaneous reconstruction, provides the central results of the study.

items.title: The achromatic number of Paley graphs, Peisert graphs, and related Cayley graphs
items.summary: The achromatic number of a graph $G$, denoted $χ_a (G)$, is the maximum number of colors in a proper vertex coloring of $G$. Generalizing a result of Maistrelli and Penman, we prove that for sufficiently large $q$, the achromatic number of the $k$-th power Paley graph is at least $\frac{q-1}{k} + 1$. This lower bound gives the correct order of magnitude in $q$, but determining the correct dependence on $k$ remains open for all $k \geq 3$. The achromatic number of Peisert graphs is shown to be $\frac{q+1}{2}$. These bounds are consequences of a general theorem involving Cayley graphs whose generating set is a union of cyclotomic classes. Using character sums and Weil's bound, we prove an upper bound that improves the standard trivial bound $\binom{ χ_a (G) }{2} \leq e(G)$. Finally, we consider random Cayley-sum graphs on an abelian group $Γ$ of order $n$, where elements are included in the generating set independently with probability $\frac{1}{2}$. We prove that the achromatic and pseudochromatic number of such a graph are both at most $\frac{(\sqrt{3}+o(1))n}{\sqrt{\log_2 n}}$ with high probability.

items.title: Remarks on Derivations on Maximal Triangular Operator Algebras
items.summary: This note concerns bounded derivations on maximal triangular operator algebras on a Hilbert space. Given any bounded derivation $δ$ on a maximal triangular algebra whose invariant lattice is continuous at 1, an operator which is shown to implement $δ$ is constructed explicitly. For a general reducible maximal triangular algebra the same construction yields an operator which is shown to implement any $δ$, if and only if $δ$ obeys an additional triple product rule. This work is based on unpublished parts of the author's dissertation [19] and describes a variant of the proof of a more general result in [21] and is thus in effect a footnote to that work. To the best of the author's knowledge the constructive proof and triple product rule have not appeared elsewhere. The work here is not set in the context of the large body of subsequent research, and no claims are made regarding its relationship to later developments.

items.title: The Recursive Behavior of the Number of Irreducible Factors of Certain Rational Transformations over Finite Fields
items.summary: Constructing irreducible polynomials over finite fields via rational transformations is an active field of study. In this paper, we show that the method can be used for more than that. By considering normalized rational functions $Q$ that generate an invariant subfield $\mathbb{F}_q(x)^G$ of $\mathbb{F}_q(x)$, for a subgroup $G\le Aut(\mathbb{F}_q(x)/\mathbb{F}_q)$, and exploiting the factorization pattern of their rational transformations, we are able to prove that the sets arising from considering whether the rational transformation $f^Q$ has exactly $deg(Q)$ irreducible factors of the same degree as $f$, or an irreducible factor of higher degree, admit a recursive behavior, i.e. their numbers satisfy a recursive equation. These sets occasionally can be described in terms of arithmetical properties the roots of the irreducible polynomials satisfy, e.g. their roots satisfy certain trace or power/non-power conditions. These can often be translated to properties of their minimal polynomials. With that, we prove a new theorem about the number of certain irreducible factors of a class of linearized polynomials, which gives a new context to a recent paper by Granger.

items.title: Three-dimensional noncommutative Fano minifolds
items.summary: We give a construction of the previously announced family of three-dimensional noncommutative Fano minifolds of Euler degree $72$. We prove that their defining $\mathbb{Z}$-algebras are Koszul and Artin--Schelter regular, and compute the Hilbert series of their section algebras.

items.title: Sparse power spectrum for passive scalars under Pierrehumbert flow
items.summary: We study the long-time Fourier distribution of driven passive scalars transported by an incompressible alternating shear flow (the Pierrehumbert flow) subjected to IID random phase shifts, in the regime of strong shear-strength. With a novel and self-contained proof, we establish (i) a quantitative version of the cumulative Batchelor's law; (ii) quantitative negative regularity mixing estimates; and (iii) a strong form of `sparsity' -- unevenness in the distribution of Fourier mass in radial sectors in frequency space. Our method uses the strong shear-strength assumption to handle a purely deterministic scalar driving term.

items.title: On The Motivic Leray-Hirsch Theorem For Pure Tate Fibre Bundles
items.summary: We prove a Leray-Hirsch theorem for a smooth proper morphism over a smooth integral base whose generic fibre has a pure Tate motive. We further explore and highlight some key applications of this theorem.

items.title: The Game-Theoretic Katětov Order and Idealised Effective Subtoposes
items.summary: This paper addresses the longstanding problem of determining the structure of the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order in the Effective Topos, known to effectively embed the Turing degrees. In a surprising discovery, we show that the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order is in fact tightly controlled by the combinatorics of filters on $ω$, raising deep questions about how combinatorial and computable complexity interact, both within this order and beyond it. To make the connection precise, we introduce a game-theoretic (''gamified'') variant of the Katětov order on filters over $ω$, which turns out to exhibit a striking mix of coarseness and subtlety. For one, it is strictly coarser than the classical Rudin-Keisler order and, when viewed dually on ideals, collapses all MAD families to a single equivalence class. On the other hand, the order also supports a rich internal structure, including an infinite strictly ascending chain of ideal classes, which we identify by way of a new separation technique. From the computability-theoretic perspective, we show that a computable (and extended) variant of the gamified Katětov order is isomorphic to the original $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order. Moreover, our work brings into focus a new degree-spectrum invariant for filters $\mathcal{F}$, $$\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F}):=\{\,[f\colonω\toω] \mid f\leq_{\mathrm{LT}} \mathcal{F} \},$$ which is shown to always determine a proper initial segment of the Turing degrees. Extending this, given any non-principal $Δ^1_1$ filter $\mathcal{F}$, we show that $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F})$ is precisely the class of hyperarithmetic degrees. This significantly generalises previous results obtained by van Oosten \cite{vO14} and Kihara \cite{Kih23}. The proofs draw on ideas from general topology, descriptive set theory, and computability theory.

items.title: Positivity of supercritical LYZ pairs
items.summary: We introduce the roots of supercritical Leung--Yau--Zaslow pairs and prove pointwise strong positivity of the associated Schur forms. The resulting LYZ cones contain the pliant cone on smooth projective threefolds, with strict inclusion on a Fujino--Sato threefold. We also establish Hard Lefschetz and Hodge--Riemann relations for the associated Chern classes on compact Kähler manifolds in bidegrees $1\le p+q\le\dim X$ with $\min\{p,q\}\le1$.

items.title: Exact controllability and rapid stabilization of linear difference delay equations and one-dimensional hyperbolic systems
items.summary: This paper addresses exact controllability and rapid stabilization issues for linear difference delay systems with finitely many pointwise delays. We first establish a criterion for exact controllability in $L^r$, $r \in [1, +\infty)$, characterized by a necessary and sufficient Hautus-type frequency-domain condition. The sufficiency of this condition in $L^r$ was already known [https://hal.science/hal-04830757/], whereas its necessity had previously been established only in $L^1$ [arXiv:2210.13590]. We answer [arXiv:2210.13590, Conjecture 3.8] by proving that this condition is also necessary for $r \in (1, +\infty)$. The analysis is based on rewriting the system as an evolution equation in a suitable Banach space, which allows one to apply duality arguments in the spirit of [https://doi.org/10.1137/S036301299119795X]. Building on this controllability analysis and the abstract stabilization framework developed in [https://doi.org/10.1137/S0363012996301609, arXiv:1301.5744], we prove that our exact controllability criterion in $L^r$ is also a sufficient condition for rapid stabilization in $L^2$, i.e., that the system of interest can be stabilized by a family of state feedback control laws ensuring that the closed-loop system is exponentially stable in $L^2$ with an arbitrarily large decay rate. As an application, we extend our results to linear one-dimensional hyperbolic partial differential equations, which can be reduced to linear difference delay systems via the method of characteristics, obtaining also a necessary and sufficient frequency-domain criterion for exact controllability in $L^r$, $r\in [1, +\infty)$, which, as before, is a sufficient condition for rapid stabilization in $L^2$.

items.title: On The Rational Realization of Even-dimensional Spheres and Products of Eilenberg--MacLane Spaces as Classifying Spaces
items.summary: In this paper, we study the rational realization problem for the classifying space $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)$. We prove that if $S^{2n}$ is realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for a simply-connected space $X$, then $X$ is $π$-infinite and has vanishing rational Gottlieb elements above degree $2n-1$. In particular, even-dimensional spheres cannot be realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for any simply-connected $π$-finite space $X$. We also prove that, for all $n\geq 2$ and $s,t\geq 1$, the product of Eilenberg--MacLane spaces $K(\mathbb{Q}^s,n)\times K(\mathbb{Q}^t,n+1)$ cannot be realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for any simply-connected $π$-finite space $X$. Moreover, we prove that if $r\geq 2$, $n\geq 3$ and $K(\mathbb{Q}^r,n)$ is realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for a simply-connected $π$-finite space $X$, then $X$ has the rational homotopy type of $K(\mathbb{Q}^r,n-1)$. The proofs are based on two structural results for Gottlieb elements in the derivation Lie algebra of a Sullivan minimal model, which provide a uniform method for these realization problems.

items.title: Capillary John ellipsoid theorem with applications to capillary curvature problems
items.summary: In this paper, we apply a capillary John ellipsoid theorem for capillary convex bodies in the Euclidean half-space $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_{+}}$. This theorem yields a non-collapsing estimate for capillary hypersurfaces, which provides a new approach to obtaining $C^{0}$ estimates for solutions to some capillary curvature problems (including the capillary $L_{p}$ Christoffel-Minkowski problem and the capillary $L_{p}$ curvature problem), based on the corresponding gradient estimates. As an application, we study the capillary $L_{p}$ dual Minkowski problem. A gradient estimate, together with the non-collapsing estimate and a $C^2$ estimate, yields existence for every $1<p<q<\infty$ with positive smooth even data and an acute contact angle. The same estimates also yield the eigenvalue problem for $p=q>1$, with uniqueness up to dilation. We further obtain existence and uniqueness for $p>q$ without an upper restriction on $q$.

items.title: Stable topology and stable compactness
items.summary: To solve a large class of noncompact problems ubiquitous in random functional analysis and its applications, most of compactness-based fundamental theorems established for normed spaces or locally convex spaces are required to be extended for random normed modules and random locally convex modules in an appropriate way of weakening compactness. To achieve this goal, in this paper we first develop stable set theory by introducing some new set-theoretic tools, then propose a class of topological spaces with a stable structure, called stable topological spaces, and in particular propose and systematically develop the theory of stably compact spaces, which is a natural generalization of that of compact spaces. The resulting theory is of independent interest from the perspective of general topology since its investigation requires an analysis of stratification structures coordinated with partitions of unity in a complete Boolean algebra. Finally, we show the power of the theory of stable compactness by establishing random Banach-Alaoglu, random James and random Banach-Bourbaki-Kakutani-Šmulian theorems.

items.title: Sharp quantitative stability of the Ashbaugh--Benguria inequality
items.summary: We establish sharp quantitative stability of the Ashbaugh--Benguria inequality on bounded convex domains in $\mathbb R^n$. After volume and centroid normalization, the eigenvalue-ratio deficit controls the squared $H^{-1/2}(\mathbb S^{n-1})$ norm of the radial displacement from the unit sphere. This yields the optimal exponent $5/2$ for the Fraenkel asymmetry and, for small deficits, the optimal exponent $(n+4)/2$ for the normalized Hausdorff distance. All three exponents are sharp even among smooth strictly convex domains whose principal curvatures lie in $[1/2,2]$. In particular, the quadratic Fraenkel-asymmetry estimate proposed by Brasco and De Philippis (2017, Open Problem 7.65) fails. We also determine the optimal stability exponents under higher-order radial regularity bounds.

items.title: The Maximal Robust Positively Invariant Set for Linear Difference Inclusions
items.summary: This article develops a systematic characterization and exact computational framework for the maximal robust positively invariant set of linear difference inclusions. The maximal set is characterized as the greatest fixed point of the robust predecessor operator, leading to three equivalent set iterations for its computation. Under uniform exponential stability and bounded disturbances, the Kuratowski upper limit of the disturbance-reachable sets yields a necessary and sufficient condition for the maximal set to be nonempty under closed state constraints. Sufficient conditions for its finite determination are also established, together with an explicit bound on the determination index. For polyhedral state constraints, bounded disturbances, and finite or polytopic matrix families, exact half-space implementations of the three iterations are derived. Although these algorithms generate the same set sequence, complexity analysis and numerical experiments reveal substantial differences in their computational performance.

items.title: A Chern-Weil theory for Lie groupoids with Cartan connections
items.summary: We extend Chern-Weil theory to Lie groupoids carrying a Cartan connection. For a principal $(Σ, ω)$-bundle $(P, θ)$ over $X$ we construct a map of differential graded algebras from an $ω$-basic subcomplex of the Weil algebra of the Lie algebroid of $Σ$ to $Ω^\bullet(X)$, whose map in cohomology does not depend on $θ$. It recovers the classical Chern-Weil map for Lie groups, the Cartan model for action groupoids, and the characteristic classes of Cartan geometries for gauge groupoids.

items.title: A complete classification of the rational realization of gap-two products of Eilenberg--MacLane spaces as classifying spaces
items.summary: In this paper, we study the rational realization of the gap-two product $K(\mathbb{Q},n)\times K(\mathbb{Q},n+2)$ as the classifying space $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)$ for a simply-connected $π$-finite space $X$ with rational homology of finite type. We prove that $K(\mathbb{Q},n)\times K(\mathbb{Q},n+2)$ can be realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)$ up to rational homotopy equivalence if and only if $n=3,4$ or $4m+2$ for $m\geq 1$. Moreover, we determine all their minimal Sullivan models up to isomorphism. The rational homotopy type of such $X$ is unique for $n=3$ or $4m+2$ for $m\geq 1$; there exist infinitely many rational homotopy types of such $X$ for $n=4$.

items.title: A general paracontrolled ansatz for singular SPDEs
items.summary: We provide a general ansatz for the paracontrolled approach introduced by Gubinelli, Imkeller, Perkowski for treating singular SPDEs. The ansatz proposed covers a large class of equations. It is described via decorated trees that encode its coefficients and its stochastic data. The main novelty is the recursive definition of the paracontrolled stochastic iterated integrals that involve a well-chosen combinatorial set of words. The paralinearisation is performed via a lift of iterated paraproducts to modelled distributions. The main idea is to integrate localised iterated paraproducts in order to get a global object with a good regularity. We also provide a fixed point argument and the renormalised equation with this ansatz when one uses the preparation map formalism that encompasses the BPHZ renormalisation. The last main result is the convergence of the renormalised stochastic data via the BPHZ renormalisation using an adaptation of the spectral gap approach. One obtains in the end a general solution theory for parabolic singular SPDEs via the paracontrolled approach.

items.title: Hadamard states for linearized gravity on asymptotically flat spacetimes
items.summary: We consider the quantization of linearized Einstein equations on 4-dimensional asymptotically flat spacetimes. We prove the existence of fully gauge invariant Hadamard states in the harmonic gauge for any Einstein metric asymptotic to the Minkowski metric in a conic neighborhood of spatial infinity.

items.title: Exact value functions and sensitivities for energy storage by fast Legendre transforms
items.summary: Long chains of decisions coupled only through a bounded cumulative state, such as the operation of an energy-storage device, form convex programs that generic solvers treat as arbitrary sparse models. We present an exact solver for this class that propagates the complete convex cost-to-reach function through restrictions and infimal convolutions, each evaluated by fast Legendre-Fenchel conjugation as an ordered merge of slopes: no state grid, no value approximation, and a function rather than a single primal-dual pair as output. Price-taking storage instances of 5,000 to 15,000 hourly steps solve 35-93 times faster than Gurobi. The value function is what pays: exact capacity marginals in one differentiated pass, recourse assembled rather than sampled on scenario trees, and a certified sizing loop whose cut count does not grow with the number of weather years. We then widen the carried state. Two storages at one node can be eliminated rather than coordinated by carrying the value function of the pair, and we prove that this object is combinatorially rigid: every breakline the recursion realizes is vertical, horizontal, or borne by a line through the origin, with no genericity assumption. For d co-located stores sharing one charge-discharge coefficient, every realized wall is a position hyperplane or an indifference hyperplane {s_i = s_j}. A catalogue law maps where speed holds: one-dimensional chains beat the frontal solve by 15-30x and growing, while the planar block loses by 13.5-107x on rich network curves. Those curves are themselves exact, traced by a parametric dual simplex. The open-source package FLToptim, every benchmark driver and all data accompany the paper.

items.title: An algebraic proof of 1-extension
items.summary: We give a new proof that 1-extension preserves generic local rigidity of bar-joint frameworks in all dimensions. The proof does not use a special position argument, which makes the approach potentially useful for X-replacement in 3-space. Instead, the balancing conditions recently introduced by the first author use directed paths in the line graph, and by modifying the end of these paths, we transfer a self-stress on the 1-extended graph back to the original. Treating the new vertex as variable allows us to extract the balancing condition of the smaller graph as one coefficient of a homogeneous quadratic. A Lean 4 formalization of the main results accompanies the paper.

items.title: A Recognizable Substitution for the Anti-Penrose Tiling
items.summary: We present a substitution on six marked rhombs, called Seabed, with inflation factor $\varphi^3$. We prove that its tiling space is mutually locally derivable with the unmarked Anti-Penrose pentagrid hull. Eleven vertex patches of depth at most four recognize the parent vertices: their acceptance domains coincide with the five internally contracted windows. Matching the fine tiles around each parent rhomb to a replacement patch recovers their markings uniquely. The inverse local maps have a uniform finite radius and extend to all singular limit tilings in the hull. The construction also gives a recognizable parent hierarchy.

items.title: Functional Inference for the Mean Curve of Intraday Spot Correlation
items.summary: In this paper, we propose estimators for the mean of the daily spot-correlation curves, which are robust to the presence of finite-variation jumps in the price processes. The related feasible functional central limit theorems for the proposed estimators have been established under a joint infill and long-span setting. Based on the asymptotic theory, we develop a test procedure for flatness of the curves. Monte Carlo simulations confirm the strong finite-sample performance of the estimators. In an empirical application to 30 U.S. stocks from 2010 to 2019, we find a pronounced end-of-day surge in the mean of correlation curves across diverse stock groupings, alongside substantial calendar-time non-flatness in the curves.

items.title: The Schützenberger involution and colored lattice models
items.summary: Colored lattice models can be used to describe many different types of special functions of interest in both algebraic combinatorics and representation theory, for example Schur polynomials, nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials, and characters and Whittaker functions for representations of p-adic groups. A notable example is the metaplectic ice model of which there are actually two different variants: a Gamma and a Delta variant. These variants differ in key aspects but surprisingly produce equal partition functions, which are weighted sums over admissible configurations, and this equality is called the Gamma-Delta duality. The duality was used to prove the analytic continuation of certain multiple Dirichlet series and is highly non-trivial, especially since the number of configurations on each side of the equality can differ. In this paper we generalize the Gamma-Delta duality by constructing a new family of solvable, colored lattice models and prove that they are dual to existing lattice models in the literature. Besides the above metaplectic case we also get a new lattice model and Gamma-Delta type duality for (non-metaplectic) Iwahori Whittaker functions together with a crystal limit for Demazure atoms for Cartan type A. The equality of partition functions is shown using Yang-Baxter equations involving both variants of lattice models simultaneously. For the crystal lattice model we show that the duality refines to a weight-respecting bijection of states given by the Schützenberger involution on the associated Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns or semistandard Young tableaux. We also show how the individual steps exchanging two rows in the proof of the duality for the partition functions refines to Berenstein-Kirillov or, equivalently, Bender-Knuth involutions.

items.title: An efficient mixed-integer linear programming formulation for solving influence diagrams
items.summary: Influence diagrams represent decision-making problems with interdependencies between random events, decisions, and consequences. Traditionally, they have been solved using tailored algorithms that determine the expected utility-maximizing decision strategy. Towards this end, most recent state-of-the-art solution approaches convert them into mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) models that can be solved using off-the-shelf MILP solvers. Computationally, these approaches are most efficient for influence diagrams that represent periodic (or sequential) decision processes, which can be cast as partially observable Markov Decision Processes. However, they are inefficient for problems that lack this periodic structure or whose influence diagrams have large state spaces. The efficient MILP formulation presented in this paper is specifically designed for influence diagrams that are challenging for earlier MILP formulations. Additionally, this formulation can be adapted to optimize conditional value-at-risk and to incorporate chance and logical constraints, thereby retaining the modeling flexibility of MILP-based methods. Finally, computational experiments on a range of problems from the literature are reported to show that the proposed formulation is much more efficient than earlier MILP formulations, particularly in problems which cannot be modeled as partially observable Markov decision processes and which lead to influence diagrams whose decision or chance nodes may have large state spaces.

items.title: Poly-Bernoulli numbers from shifted log-sine integrals
items.summary: In 1999, Arakawa and Kaneko introduced a zeta function connecting multiple zeta values with poly-Bernoulli numbers through its special values. Log-sine integrals are also known to be related to zeta values at positive integers. In this article, we study the values of a shifted log-sine integral at negative integers and establish a connection with anti-diagonal sums of poly-Bernoulli numbers. This gives a refinement of Stephan's observation on the central binomial series.

items.title: Logarithmic edge-length ratios for planar drawings of 2-trees
items.summary: For a planar graph $G$ with at least one edge, let $ρ(G)$ be the infimum of the ratio of the longest to the shortest edge length over all planar straight-line drawings of $G$. We prove that every $n$-vertex $2$-tree $G$ satisfies $ρ(G)\le4+5\lfloor\log_2(2n-3)\rfloor$. This improves the known $O(\sqrt n)$ upper bound and, together with the lower bound of Blažej, Fiala and Liotta, shows that the maximum of $ρ(G)$ over $n$-vertex $2$-trees is $Θ(\log n)$. The proof adapts Biedl's recursive bar construction using nonintegral heights and applies a height-preserving straightening theorem.

items.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
items.summary: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.

items.title: Coanalytic subfields and bases of prescribed dimension
items.summary: Assuming $V=L$, we construct proper coanalytic subfields of $\mathbb{R}$ and coanalytic Hamel and transcendence bases of every possible Hausdorff dimension, uniformly in the relevant parameters. There is a single lightface $Π^1_1$ set $G\subseteq[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$ whose sections $A_α$ are proper subfields with $\dim_{\mathrm H}A_α=α$, form a strictly increasing chain, and satisfy $A_α=\bigcup_{β<α}A_β$ for $α>0$. For every $n\ge1$, every countable subfield $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ and every $s\in[0,n]$, we construct a coanalytic Hamel basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$ over $K$ of Hausdorff dimension $s$. Likewise, for every countable subfield $K\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ and every $s\in[0,2]$, we construct a coanalytic transcendence basis of $\mathbb{C}$ over $K$ of Hausdorff dimension $s$. In each case, the bases are sections of a single lightface $Π^1_1$ relation, uniformly in codes for the coefficient field and in the prescribed dimension, as well as in $n$ for Hamel bases. More generally, we prove a uniform theorem for suitably coded families of pregeometries on Euclidean spaces. The constructions combine Cantor sets of controlled dimension with hyperarithmetic coding and coanalytic transfinite recursion. The complexity is optimal: proper subfields of $\mathbb{R}$ of positive Hausdorff dimension and bases of the stated kinds cannot be analytic.

items.title: Degenerations of Jordan algebras
items.summary: We describe all degenerations of complex $4$-dimensional Jordan algebras and of complex $5$-dimensional nilpotent Jordan algebras. The proofs do not use other papers on degenerations, and all degenerations and non-degenerations were formally verified in the proof assistant Lean~4. The graph of primary degenerations of $4$-dimensional Jordan algebras has $73$ vertices and $160$ edges. The variety of $5$-dimensional nilpotent Jordan algebras is stratified into $63$ normal forms, five of which are one- or two-parameter families; together with two special members of a family this gives $65$ objects, and the graph of primary degenerations has $154$ edges. In particular, we describe all irreducible components of the corresponding varieties: the variety of $4$-dimensional Jordan algebras has $10$ irreducible components, and the variety of $5$-dimensional nilpotent Jordan algebras has dimension $22$ and $5$ irreducible components.

items.title: Explicit twists of the Carlitz module and of its tensor powers with unbounded analytic rank
items.summary: Grishkov and Logachev have asked (Problem 1.4 of their recent survey) whether, for a fixed finite field F_q, the analytic ranks of the twists of the Carlitz module are bounded. We answer this in the negative for every q >= 3. For q = p^s and n >= 1 put P_{q,n} = (theta^{q^n} - theta)^{q-2}. We show that the directed graph of the matrix M(P_{q,n},1,k) of Grishkov-Logachev has a completely explicit set of circuits: they are pairwise disjoint, none of them meets an entry involving t, and they are in bijection with the orbits of E^n under cyclic rotation, where E = {l in [0,q-2] : p does not divide l+1}. Consequently L(C_{P_{q,n}},t,T) does not depend on t, factors as a product of one term 1 - wt(nu) T^{per(nu)} per orbit, and the analytic rank equals the sum of p^{v_p(per(nu))} over the orbits of weight 1. When n is a power of p this equals (q/p)^n (p-1)^{n-1}, which is unbounded. The argument also answers questions 3.6.1-3.6.4 of the survey for this family. We then compute the L-function for arbitrary nonzero coefficients on supports of the same shape: taking all coefficients equal to -1 multiplies the rank by p-1, and the full support gives twists of degree (q-2)q^n and analytic rank (q-1)^n, the largest rank attainable on such supports. The same method applies to the tensor powers of the Carlitz module: for 1 <= e <= q-2 we obtain twists of the e-th tensor power of analytic rank (q-e)^n, and by a formula of Grishkov and Logachev the same holds for every exponent e = c q^j with 1 <= c <= q-2, with rank (q-c)^n; in particular these analytic ranks are unbounded as well.

items.title: An elementary proof of rational injectivity in equivariant KK-theory
items.summary: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis proved that, for every countable discrete group $Γ$, the canonical map $EΓ\to\underline{E}Γ$ induces a split injection in equivariant $KK$-theory with real coefficients. In this paper, we give a more elementary proof of the corresponding rational injectivity result in ordinary equivariant $KK$-theory without using $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.

items.title: On the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula for orthogonal Shimura varieties over a general totally real field
items.summary: Let $\mathrm{F}/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension with $p\ne 2$, and let $V$ be a quadratic space over $\mathrm{F}$ of dimension at least two admitting a self-dual lattice. We prove the local arithmetic Siegel-Weil formula for GSpin Rapoport-Zink spaces formulated by Li and Zhang. We use the global-to-local strategy of Mihatsch and Zhang and its application by Luo. Using a generalization of the prismatic realization functor of Imai, Kato, and Youcis, we construct and study derived special cycles on integral models of SO Shimura varieties and their Rapoport-Zink uniformizations. We derive the local intersection formula from the modularity of special cycles on the generic fiber. As a first application, we prove the corresponding semi-global arithmetic Siegel-Weil identity for orthogonal Shimura varieties over a totally real field $F\ne\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: Optimal Hardy weights for the fractional discrete Dirichlet Laplacian on the half-line
items.summary:
For positive powers of the discrete Dirichlet Laplacian $(-Δ_{\mathrm{D}})^σ$, non-trivial Hardy weights exist if and only if $0<σ<3/2$. For $0<σ\leq 1$, an explicit optimal Hardy weight for $(-Δ_{\mathrm{D}})^σ$ was obtained by Das and de la Fuente-Fernández. Their ground state argument does not apply when $1<σ<3/2$, because the off-diagonal matrix entries of $(-Δ_{\mathrm{D}})^σ$ are no longer all non-positive. Nevertheless, we show that their result is true for the entire subcriticality range $0<σ<3/2$. For $1<σ<3/2$, our argument combines the factorisation $$(-Δ_{\mathrm{D}})^σ=
abla_{\mathrm{D}}^{*}(-Δ_{\mathrm{N}})^{σ-1}
abla_{\mathrm{D}},$$ where $
abla_{\mathrm{D}}$ and $-Δ_{\mathrm{N}}$ are the discrete Dirichlet gradient and the discrete Neumann Laplacian, respectively, with a suitable two-term ground state representation. In addition, we use these arguments to derive another explicit family of optimal Hardy weights for any $σ\in(0,3/2)$.

items.title: Integral representations of quantum Rényi divergences on von Neumann algebras
items.summary: We prove an integral representation of the $α$-$z$ Rényi divergences for normal states on arbitrary von Neumann algebras. Along each ray $z=cα$, the divergence is a positive average of relative entropies evaluated in a canonical family of escort states. For orders $α$ above one, we require the divergence to be finite, whereas for orders below one support inclusion suffices. An explicit boundary correction removes the lower-order support assumption. The proof uses a compatible weighted Haagerup $L^p$ scale and applies outside the data-processing region. For faithful density matrices, we express the derivative of the escort relative entropy with respect to the Rényi order in terms of a nonnegative fluctuation quantity. Differences of order-one derivatives of the divergence give quantum Fisher information and Wigner-Yanase skew information. For faithful bipartite density matrices, we also express optimized conditional $α$-$z$ entropies at orders above one as averages of ordinary conditional entropies. Further applications concern coherent-state divergences in quantum field theory and the optimizing order for the strong converse exponent in hypothesis-testing.

items.title: Liouville Theorems and Sharp Homogeneity Defects for Weighted Potential Systems
items.summary: In this paper, we consider \[ \begin{cases} u=K*(|x|^αa_0(x)v^p)&\quad\hbox{in }\mathbb R^n,\\ v=K*(|x|^βb_0(x)u^q)&\quad\hbox{in }\mathbb R^n, \end{cases} \] where $n\ge2$, $0<ρ<n$, $p,q>0$, and $α,β>-ρ$. The radial kernel is nonincreasing and satisfies $K(r)\asymp r^{ρ-n}$. The coefficients satisfy $0<c_0\le a_0(x),b_0(x)\le C_0$ and $|x|(|\nabla\log a_0(x)|+|\nabla\log b_0(x)|)\le L$. We prove nonexistence if \[ \frac{n+α-\varepsilon_a}{p+1} +\frac{n+β-\varepsilon_b}{q+1}>n-ρ+\varepsilon_K, \] where the defects bound the radial logarithmic derivatives. No symmetry, finite-energy condition, or prescribed decay is assumed. The proof combines a localized virial identity with a source-layer pressure estimate whose constants are uniform under centered dilations, including the low-order range $0<ρ\le1$. We also identify the necessary scaling range for existence. For radial weighted Newton systems with unequal powers, we prove that the combined coefficient defect has a sharp, unattained infimum equal to the subcritical gap. A fixed bound on the coefficient ratios forces a strictly larger defect, whereas suitable coefficient--solution pairs approach the threshold with excess at most $C/\log M$. In the scalar Newton case, the threshold is explicit and the approximating family converges, after normalization, to an explicit critical weighted profile. The sharpness results concern the Newton kernel; no corresponding construction is asserted for general fractional kernels.

items.title: A local-to-global principle for $f$-divergence homogenization
items.summary: We study the effect of replacing a family of independent statistical experiments by independent repetitions of their average. We give a simple, complete characterization of the $f$-divergences for which this operation increases divergence by at most a constant depending only on the generator, uniformly in the number of observations and the underlying measurable space. The characterization is governed by a local-to-global principle: a comparison restricted to two observations on a binary alphabet already determines the validity of the general inequality. It admits an explicit scalar formulation, which simplifies further for symmetric divergences. The result applies to arbitrary convex generators and requires no differentiability or symmetry assumptions. It recovers the homogenization inequality for total variation and identifies exactly the admissible members of the power-divergence family. In particular, whenever uniform homogenization fails, the obstruction is already present in a family of binary experiments with two observations. Moreover, the global comparison constant is controlled uniformly over generators with a common bound in the local inequality.

items.title: On Automorphism Groups of (1,2)-Surfaces
items.summary: Let $S$ be a minimal surface of general type with $K_S^2=1$ and $p_g(S)=2$, called a $(1,2)$-surface. We give a geometric recovery and refinement of D. Wen's bound $|\mathrm{Aut}(S)|\leq 200$ using the canonical genus-two fibration and the double-cover model over the Hirzebruch surface $Σ_2$. Computing $\mathrm{Aut}(Σ_2)$ from its Cox ring separates the action on the base $\mathbb{P}^1$ from the vertical kernel. If $\overline K_0$ denotes the vertical image on $Σ_2$, then $\overline K_0$ is cyclic of order $5$, $4$, $2$, or $1$, and we prove the respective sharp bounds $|\mathrm{Aut}(S)|\leq 200, 192, 48, 80$. The proof combines singularity indices of genus-two fibrations with invariant divisors arising from the branch equation. We also construct admissible branch divisors attaining all four bounds and show that their full automorphism groups are, respectively, $(C_{10}\times C_{10})\rtimes C_2$, $(BO_{48}\times C_8)/\langle(-I,J^4)\rangle$, $(BT_{24}\times C_4)/\langle(-I,J^2)\rangle$, and $C_{40}\times C_2$. Here $BO_{48}$ and $BT_{24}$ denote the binary octahedral and binary tetrahedral groups, respectively, and $J$ denotes a generator of the corresponding cyclic factor.

items.title: Integer Cantor Sets: Arithmetic Combinatorial Properties
items.summary: Cantor sets of integers have a rich set of arithmetic combinatorial properties. We consider classical Cantor sets, with a base and a fixed set of allowed digits. For such sets, we (a) give examples of such sets that satisfy the intersective property with power savings (b) characterize uniform distribution, (c) establish polynomial mean ergodic theorems and (d) study metric pair correlation of Cantor sets.

items.title: Minimality and stability of the ball for the charge-qubit energy
items.summary: We study the shape optimization problem introduced by Mazzoleni, Muratov, and Ruffini as a model for a superconducting charge qubit, in which the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of a set of prescribed volume competes with the Coulomb self-energy of the ground state. We prove that, for sufficiently small charge, the ball is the unique minimizer, and that the energy deficit of a volume-preserving and centered perturbation of the ball is comparable to the squared $H^{1/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, with constants independent of the charge. We also obtain the corresponding results for the quadratic Hartree--Ohta--Kawasaki model.

items.title: Geometry of Unimodular Random Hyperbolic Polyhedra
items.summary: We develop a geometric and probabilistic theory of unimodular random infinite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra in $\mathbb{H}^3$, allowing ordinary, ideal, and hyperideal vertices. Our results relate local dihedral geometry to global conformal type and random-walk behavior. A central role is played by a geometric characteristic $L_f(P)$, determined by the dihedral angles incident to a face $f$. We establish the unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity $$ \mathbb E[L_f(P)]=2π-\fracπ{3}\mathbb E[deg(f)]. $$ Together with circle-pattern uniformization, this yields a sharp parabolic-hyperbolic dichotomy governed by the expected geometric characteristic. We also introduce polyhedral soficity and prove that admissible Benjamini-Schramm limits of finite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra are parabolic. We further establish a quantitative Ring Lemma for regular circle patterns, providing degree-sensitive geometric control without assuming bounded degrees. Combined with unimodular probability methods, this estimate enables us to identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Our results extend the geometric-characteristic theory beyond ideal polyhedra, connecting three-dimensional geometry, unimodular Gauss-Bonnet theory, and stochastic boundary behavior.

items.title: Gamma conjectures for Milnor hypersurfaces
items.summary: We prove Gamma conjectures I and II of Galkin, Golyshev and Iritani for Milnor hypersurfaces, the smooth hypersurfaces of bidegree $(1,1)$ in the product of two projective spaces. We provide a criterion for Gamma conjecture II for general Fano manifolds, generalizing the criterion by Hu and Ke. Using the mirror symmetry technique of Galkin and Iritani, we establish global Gamma-I for Milnor hypersurfaces, thereby proving Gamma conjecture I as a special case. Using it, together with the Galois action and our criterion, we verify Gamma conjecture II for Milnor hypersurfaces.

items.title: On the Realizability of Edge-Girth Sequences
items.summary: The edge-girth of an edge $e$ in a simple connected graph is the length of a shortest cycle containing $e$, with $g_e = \infty$ if no such cycle exists, and the edge-girth sequence of a graph is the nondecreasing sequence of the edge-girths of its edges. We characterize the sequences that are realizable as the edge-girth sequence of a simple connected graph. A constant sequence $(g^{(m)})$ with $g$ finite and $m \geq 1$ is realizable if and only if $m = g$ or $m \geq \lceil 3g/2 \rceil$. Otherwise, writing $S = S_0 \uplus (g^{(m)})$, where $g$ is the maximum value of $S$ and $m$ its multiplicity, we prove that $S$ is realizable if and only if $S_0$ is realizable and $m$ lies in an explicit set determined by $g$ and by the maximum diameters of the graphs realizing $S_0$, alone or extended by fewer than $g$ edges of edge-girth $g$. The proof rests on a chaining lemma, which turns a shortest cycle of a realization into a lower bound on the maximum diameter of the realizations of a shorter sequence.

items.title: The Weyl-orbit embedding and a representation-theoretic characterization of the Clifford hierarchy
items.summary: Bu, Gu, and Jaffe introduced the quantum uniformity measures to analytically characterize the Clifford hierarchy. We prove that the quantum uniformity measures are the pullbacks of the matrix-valued uniformity functionals of Gowers and Hatami under the map $U\mapsto(a\mapsto W_aUW_a^*)$, which we call the Weyl-orbit embedding. We study the structure of the Weyl-orbit embedding, and among other results, establish a canonical decomposition of the ambient matrix-valued uniformity space into uniformity preserving twisted copies of the quantum uniformity space. The Weyl-orbit embedding identifies the Clifford hierarchy with Leibman polynomial maps. This identification yields a representation theoretic characterization of the Clifford hierarchy in terms of unitary representations of the universal polynomial groups introduced by the first author and Thom.

items.title: Ultra-hard-edge universality under deterministic preconditioning
items.summary: Let $A_n$ be an $n\times n$ real matrix with iid entries distributed as a fixed centered, variance-one, symmetric subgaussian random variable. For deterministic invertible $M_n$, set $h_n=\|M_n^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}$ and $B_n=M_n^{-1}/h_n$. We prove $\mathbb{P}(s_{\min}(M_nA_n)\le\varepsilon/h_n) =(1+o(1))\varepsilonΘ_n(B_n)$ as $n\to\infty$, uniformly over $M_n$ and $e^{-cn}\le\varepsilon\le n^{-C}$. Here $Θ_n(B)=\mathbb{E}\sqrt{nU^\top BB^\top U}$, where $U$ is uniform on $S^{n-1}$. The constants $c>0$ and $C>1$ depend only on the entry law. No condition-number bound or effective-rank assumption is required. The coefficient tends to one for diffuse inverse profiles. For convergent concentrated or spiked profiles, its limit is an explicit Gaussian expectation. The proof combines the submicroscopic comparison of Sah, Sahasrabudhe, and Sawhney with signed-permutation averaging and a weighted comparison for random hyperplane normals. Applications include inverse amplification, square sample covariance matrices with arbitrary deterministic positive-definite population matrices, and independent random environments.

items.title: Cut elimination for the alternation-free modal mu-calculus
items.summary: We present a syntactic cut-elimination procedure for the alternation-free fragment of the modal mu-calculus. Cut reduction is carried out within a cyclic proof system, where proofs are finitely branching but may be non-wellfounded. The structure of such proofs is exploited to directly transform a cyclic proof with cuts into a cut-free one, without detouring through other logics or relying on intermediate machinery for regularisation. Novel ingredients include the use of multicuts and results from the theory of well-quasi-orders, the later used in the termination argument.

items.title: Zero Forcing on Maximal Outerplanar Graphs: Capacities and Phase Repair
items.summary: We determine the zero-forcing number of maximal biconnected outerplanar graphs. When the weak dual is a path, the zero-forcing number and the induced path-covering number are both two. Otherwise, the branching faces determine a canonical core and a family of terminal strips. We prove that an optimal forcing process can be chosen in a normal form governed by explicit vertex and face capacities on the core. After fixing forests on the terminal strips, the zero-forcing number is expressed through an optimization over core-edge selections and the minimum number of root connections that must be removed to obtain an executable orientation. The path-covering number is obtained from the same capacity optimization without the repair cost. We characterize executable orientations by blocking-circuit equations and identify the two-path obstruction with a first cohomology class of a signed contact multigraph. Local replacements and a finite comparison of boundary recurrences establish the normal form for graphs of arbitrary size. A fifty-six-state recurrence constructs a minimum zero-forcing set and a complete forcing chronology in linear time from indexed triangle adjacency. We also obtain exact replacement results for rooted blocks and construct infinite families in which the zero-forcing number exceeds the path-covering number.

items.title: Grushin spherical harmonics in non-degenerate dimension one
items.summary: The Grushin Laplacian $Δ_α= Δ_x +|x|^{2α}Δ_y $ is a degenerate elliptic operator in $\mathbb{R}^{h+k}$ that degenerates on $\{0\} \times \mathbb{R}^k$. We explicitly compute the Grushin spherical harmonics on the gauge sphere $\{(x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^{h+k} : |x|^{2(α+1)}+(α+1)^2|y|^2=1\}$ and the corresponding spectrum when the non-degenerate dimension $h=1$, a case not covered by the existing literature. The eigenfunctions consist of homogeneous Grushin-harmonic polynomials of degrees $n \equiv 0,1 \pmod{α+1}$, even and odd in the $x$-variable respectively, which can be described in terms of Jacobi polynomials.

items.title: Random Burnside Groups
items.summary: Fix integers $m\ge2$ and $k\ge1$. For every sufficiently large fixed odd exponent $M$, choose $k$ independent elements uniformly from the sphere of radius $\ell$ in the free Burnside group $B_m(M)$. We prove that the quotient by their normal closure is infinite with probability at least $1-e^{-c\ell}$. More precisely, the quotient map has no nontrivial kernel element of length at most $κ\ell$, for constants $c,κ>0$. We also consider the analogue of the Gromov positive density model for the Burnside variety.

items.title: Dynamics of Interfaces in the Two-Dimensional Wave-Pinning Model
items.summary: We study the mass-conserved reaction-diffusion system known as the wave-pinning model, which serves as a minimal framework for describing cell polarity. In this model, the interplay between reaction kinetics and slow diffusion forms a sharp interface that partitions the domain into high- and low-concentration regions. We perform a detailed asymptotic analysis and derive higher-order approximation equations governing the motion of this interface. Our results show that on a fast timescale, the interface evolves via propagating front dynamics, whereas on a slow timescale, it evolves as an area-preserving mean curvature flow. Furthermore, using the derived free boundary problem, we demonstrate that on a significantly slower timescale, an interface whose endpoints lie on the domain boundary drifts along the boundary toward regions of higher curvature. In summary, our analysis reveals that the interface dynamics in the wave-pinning model exhibit a hierarchy of three distinct timescales: wave propagation on a fast timescale, curvature-driven area-preserving evolution on a slow timescale, and motion along the boundary on a significantly slower timescale.

items.title: Well-posedness of a stress-augmented Moore-Gibson-Thompson-type model for thermoviscoelastic evolution in a standard linear solid
items.summary: This manuscript studies a coupled system of nonlinear parabolic and hyperbolic equations that models thermoviscoelastic materials with explicit internal stress relaxation, $$\begin{cases} τu_{ttt} + u_{tt} = (D(Θ)u_{xt})_x + (C(Θ)u_x)_x, \\ Θ_t = Θ_{xx} + |E(Θ)u_{xt} + F(Θ)g_t|^2, \\ τg_t + g = D(Θ)u_{xt} + C(Θ)u_x. \end{cases}$$ The system arises from a stress-strain constitutive relation of Zener type, where the internal variable $g$ encodes mechanical memory effects. A key feature is the explicit coupling of stress relaxation to the heat equation through the dissipation term, which differs from standard approaches that eliminate $g$ via algebraic substitution. Under the assumptions that $τ>0$ and that $D,C\in C^2([0,\infty))$ are positive and $E,F\in C^1([0,\infty))$, and for suitably regular initial data, we establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. Under additionally strengthened regularity requirements on the initial data and on $D,C$, this solution is moreover shown to be classical. These results extend a corresponding local strong and classical solvability theory developed for the underlying system without the stress variable $g$ to the present, stress-augmented setting.

items.title: Turán densities of hypergraph augmentations
items.summary: For a $t$-graph $F$ and an integer $r\ge t$, the \emph{$r$-augmentation} $F(r)$ is the $r$-graph obtained by adding the same set of $r-t$ new vertices to every edge of $F$. We investigate the behaviour of the \emph{Turán density $π(F(r))$}, which is the asymptotically maximum edge density of a large $F(r)$-free $r$-graph, as a function of $r\to\infty$. Let $H_k^r$ be the $r$-augmentation of the complete $(k-1)$-graph on $k$ vertices; equivalently, $H_k^r$ is the (unique up to isomorphism) $r$-graph with $r+1$ vertices and $k$ edges. This paper determines the Turán density of each $r$-graph $H_k^r$ within a constant factor and estimates the lower bounds on $π(H_k^r)$ coming from the circular construction of Sidorenko. In particular, it is shown that if $k/\log r\to\infty$ then $π(H_k^r)=(1+o(1))k/r$. Also, we consider augmentations of graphs (that is, the case $t=2$) and prove that $π(F(r))\ge(\log r)^{-1-o(1)}/r$ for every 3-chromatic graph $F$, which comes close to the known upper bound $1/r$. Note that, for all other graphs $F$, the function $π(F(r))$ is known to be either identically 0 or uniformly bounded away from 0.

items.title: The Hardy-Littlewood-type equivalence problem and its applications
items.summary: The main purpose of this paper is to resolve the Hardy-Littlewood-type equivalence problem. In particular, we show that a Hardy-Littlewood-type theorem holds for arbitrary majorants in the case \(p\in(1,\infty)\), and that the equivalence holds in the case \(p=1\). For the proof, we employ new functional analytic approaches based on Fourier series, the Hilbert transform, and the uniform boundedness principle. Those proof methods are completely different from those of Dyakonov [Acta Math., 178 (1997), 143-167] and Pavlović [Acta Math., 183 (1999), 141-143]. In addition, we present several representative applications that improve a series of known results.

items.title: Open dynamics with a moving hole: inhomogeneous IFS and exponential separation condition
items.summary: Let $\mathcal F=\{f_i(x)=r_i x+t_i\}_{i=0}^{b-1}$ be a self-similar iterated function system (IFS) on $\mathbb R$ with $b\ge 3$, and let $K_{\mathcal F}$ be the associated self-similar set. Given $m\in\mathbb N$, for any sequence $ω=ω^0ω^1\ldots$ with each $ω^i\in \{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^m$ a block of length $m$, let \[ K_{\mathcal F}^ω:=π_{\mathcal F}\left(\{(d_i)\in \{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^{\mathbb N}: d_{k+1}d_{k+2}\ldots d_{k+m}\neω^k\quad\forall k\ge 0\}\right), \] where $π_{\mathcal F}$ is the natural coding map from $\{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^{\mathbb N}$ to $K_{\mathcal F}$. The set $K_{\mathcal F}^ω$ is called the survivor set of an open dynamical system with a moving hole related to $ω$. When $\mathcal F$ is a homogeneous IFS satisfying the open set condition (OSC), the dimensions of $K_{\mathcal F}^ω$ were determined by the first author, Sun and Wang (Adv. Math., 2026). In this paper we generalize these results to inhomogeneous IFSs. When $\mathcal F$ satisfies the OSC, we give explicit formulae for the dimensions of $K_{\mathcal F}^ω$. In particular, we show that the packing dimension and upper box-counting dimension of $K_{\mathcal F}^ω$ always coincide, while the Hausdorff dimension and lower box-counting dimension of $K_{\mathcal F}^ω$ are not necessarily equal, which is different from the homogeneous case. Furthermore, when $\mathcal F$ satisfies the exponential separation condition and the similarity dimension $s_{\mathcal F}\le 1$, we are able to determine the Hausdorff dimension of $K_{\mathcal F}^ω$. Finally, we apply our results to badly approximable numbers and non-recurrence points in the setting of inhomogeneous IFS satisfying the OSC.

items.title: Quantitative positivity properties of the temperature in multi-dimensional thermoviscoelastic systems
items.summary:
We consider the classical model for small-strain thermoviscoelastic evolution in isotropic Kelvin-Voigt materials with inertia, as given by $$ egin{cases} u_{tt} = μΔu_t + (λ+μ)
abla
abla\cdot u_t + \hatμΔu + (\hatλ+\hatμ)
abla
abla\cdot u - B
ablaΘ, \ κΘ_t = DΔΘ+ μ|
abla u_t|^2 + (λ+μ)|\mathrm{div}\,u_t|^2 - BΘ\,\mathrm{div}\,u_t. \end{cases}$$ Recently, Winkler (arXiv:2602.05964) established global-in-time solvability for an initial value problem in smoothly bounded multi-dimensional domains $Ω$ under homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions for the displacement variable $u$, and homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions for the temperature $Θ$, allowing the heat capacity $κ$ to depend on $Θ$. Moreover, it was shown there that the corresponding temperature is positive a.e. in $Ω	imes(0,\infty)$. In the present work, we strengthen this positivity result by deriving a quantitative lower bound for $Θ$. Our analysis applies to heat capacities $κ$ with power-law scaling for small arguments, precisely: either $κ(ξ)\simξ^α$ for some $α\ge 0$, or $κ(ξ)\geξ$, in a suitable neighborhood of $ξ=0$. Under these structural assumptions on $κ$, we show that for every $τ>0$ and $T>τ$ there exists $c(τ,T)>0$ such that $Θ(x,t)\ge c(τ,T)$ for a.e. $(x,t)\inΩ	imes(τ,T)$.

items.title: On generalized covering radii of binary primitive double-error-correcting BCH codes
items.summary: The generalized covering radii (GCR) of linear codes are a fundamental higher-dimensional extension of the classical covering radius. While the second and third GCR of binary primitive double-error-correcting BCH codes, $\text{BCH}(2,m)$, were recently determined, their proofs relied on highly complex combinatorial arguments, and the behavior of the GCR hierarchy for larger orders $k$ has remained largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce the Generalized Supercode Lemma, which lower-bounds the GCR of a code using the generalized Hamming weights of an appropriate supercode. Applying this lemma, we significantly streamline and simplify the proofs for the known lower bounds of $ρ_2(\text{BCH}(2,m))$ and $ρ_3(\text{BCH}(2,m))$, and we establish a new lower bound for $ρ_4(\text{BCH}(2,m))$. Furthermore, by combining combinatorial arguments with Weil-type exponential sum estimates, we investigate the GCR hierarchy for general $k$, proving that $2k \le ρ_k(\text{BCH}(2,m)) \le 2k+1$ whenever $m$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$.

items.title: When Is Two-Stage Sample Robust Optimization Asymptotically Optimal? A Simple Perspective
items.summary: Two-stage sample robust optimization with linear decision rules is a standard data-driven approach to two-stage stochastic linear programs with unknown distributions. \cite{bertsimas2022two} established that this approach is asymptotically optimal under several conditions. Most conditions are mild, but one imposes a technical requirement on the recourse system. Whether this condition is implied by the others was left as an open question. We resolve this open question through a geometric feature of the support set: simpleness, the property that every vertex is incident to exactly as many edges as the dimension of the support. For simple support sets, the technical condition is automatic, and asymptotic optimality holds under the remaining standard assumptions. For every non-simple support, we construct a recourse system that is feasible everywhere in the support but violates the technical condition, and this construction resolves the open question. We further characterize the simpleness of one-sided and two-sided budgeted uncertainty sets and identify when budget perturbations can restore simpleness. We also develop a polynomial-time algorithm that certifies the technical condition at a given vertex using its incident edge directions. Numerical experiments on newsvendor and network lot-sizing problems illustrate the characterization and the effectiveness of the verification algorithm.

items.title: Mean-field limit of non-exchangeable multi-agent systems over hypergraphs with unbounded rank
items.summary: Interacting particle systems are known for their ability to generate large-scale self-organized structures from simple local interaction rules between each agent and its neighbors. In addition to studying their emergent behavior, a main focus of the mathematical community has been concentrated on deriving their large-population limit. In particular, the mean-field limit consists of describing the limit system by its population density in the product space of positions and labels. The strategy to derive such limits is often based on a careful combination of methods ranging from analysis of PDEs and stochastic analysis, to kinetic equations and graph theory. In this article, we focus on a generalization of multi-agent systems that includes higher-order interactions, which has largely captured the attention of the applied community in the last years. In such models, interactions between individuals are no longer assumed to be binary (i.e. between a pair of particles). Instead, individuals are allowed to interact by groups so that a full group jointly generates a non-linear force on any given individual. The underlying graph of connections is then replaced by a hypergraph, which we assume to be dense, but possibly non uniform and of unbounded rank. For the first time in the literature, we show that when the interaction kernels are regular enough, then the mean-field limit is determined by a limiting Vlasov-type equation, where the hypergraph limit is encoded by a so-called UR-hypergraphon (unbounded-rank hypergraphon), and where the resulting mean-field force admits infinitely-many orders of interactions.

items.title: Irrationality Exponents of Real CM Elliptic Periods and Powers of the Lemniscate Period
items.summary: We give a determinant proof that every nonzero real period of a nonsingular elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ with complex multiplication, measured with a specified nonzero rational invariant differential, has irrationality exponent two. The proof uses an integral origin chart, matched local lengths, an actual compactification and weighted packet map, and arithmetic and analytic estimates for the same selected minor on a rectangular sublattice of the full CM period lattice. For the integral-defined lemniscate period $Ω=2\int_0^1(1-t^4)^{-1/2}\,dt$, we also give the uniform bound $μ(Ω^n)=O(n\log(2n))$ for integers $n\geq1$. Its new arithmetic ingredient clears integration denominators prime by prime while retaining the coefficient order; a one-root norm argument and an analytic estimate at algebraic centers complete the power proof. The two arguments are presented with their different charts and exact dependencies. Lean verifies the new CM determinant argument and rational normalization relative to explicit classical uniformization, CM-lifting and theta inputs; the lemniscate-power endpoint is also verified. The formalization record states the exact classical boundary and theorem references.

items.title: On Modified Newton Methods for Unconstrained Optimization Based on Lanczos Tridiagonalization
items.summary: For a strongly convex unconstrained minimization problem, Newton's method with a line search offers rapid convergence to a minimizer by incorporating second-order information. However, for a general unconstrained problem the Hessian need not be positive definite, which can lead to the inability to find a search direction or to search directions that fail to produce descent. Modified Newton methods are designed to handle this situation. This paper considers modifications to a Newton-conjugate-gradient approach based on Lanczos tridiagonalization. Existing methods are extended using dynamic modification schemes that provide a descent direction while keeping the modification bounded. A Lanczos-based scheme and a conjugate-gradient (CG)-based scheme are formulated and analyzed. These methods are mathematically equivalent in exact arithmetic, but their practical behavior differs in finite precision. Finally, it is shown how the convergence and computational cost are affected by varying the amount of additional curvature introduced and by allowing the early termination of the inner iterations.

items.title: Optimal Network Dependence in Distributed Stochastic Optimization via Tree Routing
items.summary: Communication is a central bottleneck in distributed optimization, but its effect is often summarized by the spectral gap of a chosen mixing matrix. Since this gap depends on link weights as well as topology, it can obscure the intrinsic effect of the network. We clarify this distinction by relating graph diameter to the inverse spectral gap. We establish a universal one-sided bound that is tight up to constant factors, while constructions across several graph families show that no topology-only converse or universal two-sided scaling law exists. This motivates a class-based view of network optimality: diameter-dependent guarantees can be assessed uniformly over graph classes, whereas spectral-gap optimality requires both the graph--matrix pair class and the admissible algorithm class to be specified. Based on the resulting diameter-based minimax benchmark, we introduce Tree-Routed Gradient Tracking (Tree-RGT), a distributed method for stochastic nonconvex optimization. The method pipelines model dissemination and gradient aggregation over a rooted shortest-path spanning tree. Each iteration uses one round of one-hop communication and one stochastic-gradient evaluation per agent, without inner consensus or multi-gossip. Under smoothness and unbiased bounded-variance oracles, Tree-RGT achieves uniformly optimal network dependence over connected graphs of prescribed size and diameter. It recovers centralized stochastic scaling after $\mathcal{O}(nD_{\mathcal{G}}^2)$ transient iterations, where $n$ is the number of agents and $D_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the graph diameter. This network-dependent transient-iteration bound improves upon or matches those reported for representative distributed methods. Thus, topology-aware routing attains diameter-optimal guarantees without relying on a prescribed mixing matrix.

items.title: Zero Forcing, Support Varieties, and Boundary Complexes
items.summary: Let a finite simple graph be given. We study symmetric matrices with this graph pattern that admit a null vector with prescribed exact support. Such a vector exists precisely when its support is a fort, meaning that no vertex outside the support has exactly one neighbor inside it. Over the complex numbers, we prove that the Zariski closure of each exact-support coefficient locus is irreducible and compute its codimension in terms of boundary vertices and a labeled forest on the connected components of the support. The corresponding forest deficiency also determines the generic restricted nullity. An incidence parametrization yields a prime decomposition of the reduced zero-forcing failure locus. For a prescribed common kernel, we describe the coefficient space through equilibrium stresses, exterior affine dependencies, and free coefficients. We then construct boundary complexes recording local solution values and equation residuals. Their gluing maps are defined over the universal coefficient ring and commute with arbitrary base change. By retaining the complete collection of support signatures associated with each seed set, we obtain a composition formula for the minimum zero-forcing number and an algorithm for its computation.

items.title: Nonexistence of Constant Congruences for the Cumulative Partition Function
items.summary: Let $p(n)$ be the ordinary partition function and let $c(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}p(k)$, with $c(0)=0$. We prove that, for every $a\geq1$, $b\geq0$, and $m\geq2$, the sequence $c(an+b)$ is not eventually constant modulo $m$, thereby answering a question posed by Chen. The proof combines the algebraicity over $\mathbb C(j)$ of modular functions for finite-index subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ with Voloch's theorem on the transcendence of elliptic modular functions in positive characteristic.

items.title: Almost every Boolean function has central threshold degree
items.summary: The polynomial threshold degree (or threshold degree) of a Boolean function is the least degree of a real polynomial whose sign represents it. We prove that almost every Boolean function has polynomial threshold degree among the central one or two integers. More precisely, a uniformly chosen Boolean function on $n$ variables has threshold degree either $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ or $\lceil n/2\rceil$, except with probability at most $\exp(-c2^{n/2}/n)$, for an absolute constant $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$. The paper proves a 1991 conjecture of Aspnes, Beigel, Furst and Rudich. It also proves a 1991 conjecture of Wang and Williams for even $n$ and its main concentration assertion for odd $n$. A parity example gives a lower bound on the exceptional probability whose exponent differs from ours by a factor of order $n$. The proof relates polynomial sign representation to recovery of Reed--Muller codes from random erasures, and combines sharp-threshold estimates with bounds on generalized Hamming weights and minimum distance.

items.title: Sharp Variational estimates for Schrödinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
items.summary: For $p\geq2$ and $r\geq 1$, we prove the sharp strong $r$-variation estimate for solutions to the free Schrödinger equation $$ \bigl\|V^r_{[0,1]}\{e^{itΔ}f\}\bigr\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)} \lesssim \|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^2)}. $$ The estimate holds if $s> s(p,r)$ and fails if $s< s(p,r)$, where $$s(p,r)=\max\left\{ \frac{2}{r}+\frac{1}{p}-\frac12,\, \frac{2}{r}-\frac{2}{p},\, \frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{r},\, \frac{2}{p}-\frac13,\, 1-\frac{2}{p} \right\}.$$ In particular, $s(3,\infty)=1/3$.
