Thus our result yields a sharp variational extension of the two-dimensional Schrödinger maximal estimate of Du, Guth, and Li [{Ann. Math.}, 186, 607--640 (2017)]. The proof employs fractal restriction estimates to eliminate the regularity loss originating from the summation in the variation norm.

items.title: Homological subsets of Spec
items.summary: We recover some data of a module $M$ from the Ext-family $\{Ext^i_R(M,R)\}$. In this regard, we investigate homological subsets of $Spec(R)$, defined by the help of Ext-family. For example, we present a situation for which $\bigcup_{i=0}^\infty Ass(Ext^i_R(M,R))$ is infinite, thereby answering a question of Vasconcelos. We extend Grothendieck's calculation of $dim(Ext^g_R(M,R))$ and present some new situations to calculate $dim(Ext^\ast_R(M,R))$. Also, we compute support and the set of all associated prime ideals of the Ext-family in a serial of nontrivial cases.

items.title: Policy Evaluation and Policy Gradient for Continuous-Time Markov Regime-Switching Systems
items.summary: We study policy evaluation (PE) and policy gradient (PG) for continuous-time stochastic control with Markov regime-switching. The main challenges are the coexistence of diffusion and regime jumps, the coupling of regime-dependent value functions, and the construction of model-free learning rules from the coupled generators. We establish a martingale characterization of PE that incorporates both Brownian and switching martingales, and extend martingale loss and orthogonality methods to this setting. We further derive a coupled PG equation and a trajectory-based gradient representation that, under an action-independent switching generator, avoids explicit knowledge of the system coefficients and transition rates. These results lead to offline and online actor-critic algorithms. We also establish convergence and study the finite-grid approximation required for implementation. Numerical experiments for a regime-switching linear-quadratic problem illustrate the proposed methods.

items.title: Persistence of gaps in the spectrum of certain almost periodic operators
items.summary: It is shown that for any irrational rotation number and any admissible gap labelling number the almost Mathieu operator (also known as Harper's operator) has a gap in its spectrum with that labelling number. This answers the strong version of the so-called "Ten Martini Problem". When specialized to the particular case where the coupling constant is equal to one, it follows that the "Hofstadter butterfly" has for any quantum Hall conductance the exact number of components prescribed by the recursive scheme to build this fractal structure.

items.title: Sharp CR Beckner-Onofri inequalities under high-order holomorphic moment constraints
items.summary: We establish sharp Beckner--Onofri on the CR sphere $\mathbb{S}^{2N-1}\subset\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge2$, under vanishing holomorphic moments through degree $m\ge1$. The optimal coefficients are $\frac{1}{m+1}$. The function inequality admits a stronger form involving only the energy above degree $m$. We also prove a quantitative concentration estimate in the $1$-Wasserstein distance and show that every maximizing sequence has diverging energy and approaches the family of uniform measures on regular $(m+1)$-polygons. The proof combines subcritical minimization with rigidity of the constrained Euler--Lagrange equation, obtained from an exact radial energy identity and a Hardy space projection estimate. Finally, weighted ball automorphisms yield sharp inequalities without moment constraints, with scalar conformal, barycenter, and holomorphic Gram determinant corrections.

items.title: Finite Element Approximation of Rotating MHD-Boussinesq Flows with Nonlinear Power-Law Viscosity
items.summary: We propose and analyse a fully discrete finite element approximation of the three-dimensional incompressible rotating MHD-Boussinesq system with nonlinear power-law ($p$-Laplace) viscosity. Conforming elements are used for the velocity and temperature, $\mathbf H(\operatorname{curl})$-conforming Nédélec elements for the magnetic induction, and a semi-implicit backward Euler scheme in time. The discretisation preserves the principal energy structure: the Lorentz and induction terms cancel exactly, while the Coriolis force remains energy neutral. This yields well-posedness and mesh-independent energy stability. The nonlinear power-law diffusion creates two main analytical difficulties. Since a uniform time-derivative estimate for the discrete velocity is unavailable, strong compactness is obtained through a time-translate argument and Simon's compactness criterion. The weak limit of the nonlinear diffusion is then identified by a Minty argument based on a discrete energy $\limsup$ inequality. Compactness and passage to the limit hold throughout the shear-thickening regime, while identification of a genuine weak solution is obtained in the Newtonian case and, in three dimensions, above an explicit threshold dictated by the Lorentz force rather than by convection. We further establish a priori error estimates without any mesh-time coupling condition. Three-dimensional numerical experiments confirm the stability and convergence behaviour predicted by the analysis.

items.title: A sharp isoperimetric bound for the ratio of the fifth and fourth eigenvalues of Dirichlet Laplacian
items.summary: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with $n\geq2$. The well-known Payne-Pólya-Weinberger conjecture for consecutive eigenvalue ratios asserts that $$ \frac{λ_{m+1}(Ω)}{λ_m(Ω)}\leq\left(\frac{j_{n / 2,1}}{j_{n / 2-1,1}}\right)^2,\quad m=1,2,3,\cdots. $$ Here, $j_{p,k}$ denotes the $k$-th positive zero of the Bessel function $J_p$, and $λ_j(Ω)$ are the Dirichlet eigenvalues of $Ω$, counted with multiplicity and ordered as $$ 0<λ_1(Ω)<λ_2(Ω)\leqλ_3(Ω)\leq\cdots. $$ The cases $m=1,2,3$ were established by Ashbaugh and Benguria in their seminal works. In this paper, we give an affirmative answer to the Payne-Pólya-Weinberger conjecture for $m=4$ by combining a quadratic-form identity with a Brouwer degree argument. We also extend the corresponding spectral inequality to arbitrary bounded open sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

items.title: Ledrappier-Young entropy formula for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms with dominated splitting Part 3: full formula with arbitrary multiplicities
items.summary: We establish the full Ledrappier-Young entropy formula for ergodic invariant measures of $C^1$ diffeomorphisms when the positive Oseledets bundles and their nonpositive complement form a dominated splitting. We prove transverse formulas under three-block domination and equality of metric and unstable entropy under positive-nonpositive domination. To complete the proof, we develop a new mechanism for estimating partial entropy through comparisons of conditional information along orbits. Applications characterize vanishing transverse dimension, give upper pointwise dimension bounds and exact dimensionality of hyperbolic measures. In the quasi-isometric-center setting, this implies a $C^1$ invariance principle for measures with nonpositive center Lyapunov exponents.

items.title: Euler characteristic and flat cohomology of convex projective $4$-manifolds
items.summary: Let $M=Ω/Γ$ be a closed properly convex real projective $4$-manifold. We prove the Chern-Hopf-Thurston conjecture for this class of manifolds, i.e. $χ(M)\geq0$. The argument transfers Akagawa's double-form identity on the Cheng--Yau cone over $Ω$ to a Bochner identity on $M$, from which we deduce that $H^q(M;Λ^pE^*)=0$ whenever $q<p(n+1-p)/(n+1)$, in arbitrary dimension $n$, for some flat bundle $E$ naturally attached to $M$. In dimension four, this implies that the cohomology with coefficients in $Λ^2E^*$ concentrates in degree two.

items.title: Connected irregular cospectral graphs with distinct Lovász numbers
items.summary: For every integer $n \geq 11$, we construct connected, irregular, nonisomorphic graphs on $n$ vertices with equal adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, normalized Laplacian, and Seidel spectra and equal independence, clique, chromatic, complement chromatic, and maximum-cut numbers, but distinct Lovász $\vartheta$-numbers. We join each graph in a fixed cospectral, nonisomorphic regular pair on ten vertices, due to van Dam and Haemers (2003), with $K_{n-10}$. We prove that these joins preserve equality of the five spectra and stated integer-valued invariants, and leave the respective Lovász numbers unchanged. We derive exact expressions for these numbers and prove that they are distinct. We also determine the cardinality-constrained maximum-cut profiles of both base graphs and their complements, yielding exact formulas and equality of maximum-cut numbers for the joins of either the base graphs or their complements with $K_{n-10}$. For $n=10$, we present a regular pair satisfying all stated properties except irregularity, followed by a connected, irregular, nonisomorphic pair satisfying all properties. An exhaustive computer search finds no connected, irregular, nonisomorphic pair on at most nine vertices sharing the first four spectra and all stated integer-valued invariants. Thus, ten is the smallest possible order, and such pairs exist for every $n \geq 10$. This extends and strengthens Sason's (2024) result for \emph{even} $n \geq 14$, which used the neighbors splitting join operation and did not address Seidel matrices, complement chromatic numbers, or maximum-cut numbers of the graphs or joins of their complements. Thus, the Lovász number efficiently certifies nonisomorphism even when all five spectra and stated integer-valued invariants coincide.

items.title: Potential estimates and improved Sobolev regularity for nonlocal fully nonlinear elliptic equations
items.summary: This paper investigates pointwise and oscillatory potential estimates for viscosity solutions and their gradients to a class of nonlocal fully nonlinear elliptic equations. The key ingredient of our argument is to establish precise pointwise bounds for a novel fractional sharp maximal function defined in terms of affine functions. As an immediate consequence, we prove higher order Sobolev regularity results of Calderón-Zygmund type for such equations without imposing any global boundedness assumptions on viscosity solutions. The potential theory developed herein extends the work of Daskalopoulos-Kuusi-Mingione (Commun. Partial Differ. Equ. 39: 574-590, 2014) for fully nonlinear second order elliptic equations to the fractional fully nonlinear setting.

items.title: The taming of 3-fold flops
items.summary: This article overviews recent progress in understanding and classifying one of the most elementary of birational surgeries within algebraic geometry, namely 3-fold flops, through the development of a noncommutative version of singularity theory.

items.title: New upper bounds for the period of a negative orientable sequence
items.summary: Negative orientable sequences, i.e. periodic sequences with elements from a finite alphabet of size at least three in which an n-tuple or the negative of its reverse appears at most once in a period of the sequence, were introduced by Alhakim et al. in 2024. The main goal in defining them was as a means of generating orientable sequences, which have automatic position location applications, although they are potentially of interest in their own right. In this paper we develop new upper bounds on the period of negative orientable sequences which, for n>2, are significantly sharper than the previous known bound. The approach used to develop the new bounds involves examining the nodes in the subgraph of the de Bruijn graph corresponding to a negative orientable sequence, and to consider the implications of the fact that the in-degree of every vertex in this subgraph must equal the out-degree. However, despite improving the bounds, a gap remains between the largest known period for a negative orientable sequence and the corresponding bounds for every n>2.

items.title: Semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf II: the Ran space version
items.summary: This paper is a sequel to arXiv:2310.0638. Let G be a split reductive group. We define the parabolic semi-infinite category on the Ran version of the affine Grassmanian Gr_{G,Ran}. We study the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf in this category. We provide several descriptions of this object, one as certain colimit, another as an intermediate extension in certain category. We relate the global and local semi-infinite categories of sheaves. We also relate the intersection cohomology sheaf of the Drinfeld compactification of Bun_P with the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf.

items.title: The classification of smooth 3-fold flops
items.summary: This paper establishes the analytic classification of smooth, simple, 3-fold flops, and in the process provides both an intrinsic characterisation and a classification of their contraction algebras.

items.title: On global Chern-Calabi flows on compact complex surfaces
items.summary: In this paper, we propose the Chern-Calabi Flow for extremal metrics in conformal Hermitian geometry. After the existence of extremal metric, we consider the existence of global flows to the Chern-Calabi flows for extremal metrics on compact complex surfaces with Gauduchon metrics. To achieve this goal, we use the Adams inequality and the Gronwall inequality method to obtain fourth order derivative norm estimates. We also study the convergence of the global solution to the Chern-Calabi flow and its limit is the solution of the Chern-Calabi extremal metric problem. We propose a fourth order elliptic problem and derive the Bochner formula relevant to the elliptic estimates for the Chern-Calabi heat flow.

items.title: A unified quantitative approach to Chiti and Kohler--Jobin inequalities
items.summary: We obtain two quantitative results related to classical rearrangement inequalities for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue. The first one is a quantitative version of Chiti's reverse Hölder inequality. More precisely, for every $1\le q<p<\infty$, we prove that the deficit controls, up to translations, the $L^q$ distance between a first eigenfunction of a bounded domain and the first eigenfunction of the ball having the same first eigenvalue. The second result concerns the Kohler--Jobin inequality and gives a quantitative estimate in terms of the $L^\infty\!\to L^2$ distance between the corresponding Dirichlet resolvents. In both cases, the main idea is to find a suitable superlevel set of the first eigenfunction which is almost optimal for the Faber-Krahn inequality.

items.title: Star operation, microscopic sets and porous sets
items.summary: This paper explores the interplay between star operations, microscopic sets, and porous sets. The study focuses on the Galvin-Mycielski-Solovay theorem, which characterizes strongly measure zero sets and their interactions with meager sets. Results include the investigation of the star operation $\mathcal{F}^*$ and its properties. The paper also examines the relationship between porous sets and microscopic sets. Additionally, the work presents constructions of families $\mathcal{F}$ in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Z}), \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Z}^ω),$ and $\mathcal{P}(2^ω)$ that satisfy $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F}^*$. Theorems and lemmas are provided to establish conditions under which $\mathcal{F}^{**} = \mathcal{F}$ and to analyze the implications of the Borel Conjecture and its dual. The paper concludes with a discussion of microscopic sets and their properties, including their interactions with porous sets and the non-equivalence of certain classes of sets.

items.title: Safety-constrained position tracking of a flexible transmission system
items.summary: We consider safety-constrained position tracking for a flexible transmission system consisting of a torsional shaft driven by a motor and connected to a gravitationally loaded inertia. The coupled PDE-ODE dynamics admit a semilinear formulation in which the linear input-output system is impedance passive and the gravitational torque enters as a bounded, globally Lipschitz perturbation. We establish an energy dissipation inequality for the nonlinear model and show that a position-funnel controller with supervised damping admits a unique global closed-loop trajectory. In particular, the motor-angle tracking error remains strictly inside a prescribed time-varying funnel, which can be chosen to enforce safety bounds on the motor angle.

items.title: Topological preservation under aggregation of quantale-valued metric spaces
items.summary: Aggregation functions provide a general mechanism for combining multiple inputs into a single output and constitute a fundamental tool in information fusion. Beyond the classical numerical setting, aggregation can also be considered at the level of mathematical structures, where the main question is to determine which properties of the original structures are preserved by the aggregation process. In this paper, we study the preservation of topology within a unified framework based on continuous quantales and quantale-enriched categories. We introduce strongly preserving functions, for which the natural topology induced by a $\mathscr V$-metric space coincides with that induced after aggregation. We decompose this property into its upper and lower versions and show that upper strong preservation is equivalent to Scott continuity at the unit of the domain quantale, whereas lower strong preservation is characterized in terms of the fibre of the unit and the Scott upper semicontinuity of the inverse multifunction. Combining these results, we obtain a complete characterization of strongly preserving functions, together with analogous results for separated, symmetric, and separated and symmetric $\mathscr V$-metric spaces. Finally, we specialize the general theory to functions from $\mathsf P_+^{\,I}$ to $\mathsf P_+$, obtaining characterizations of strongly extended quasi-pseudometric and pseudometric aggregation functions on Cartesian products and on common underlying sets, together with corresponding results for extended quasi-metric and metric aggregation functions on Cartesian products.

items.title: Complete conformal metrics of constant positive scalar curvature with prescribed isolated singularities
items.summary: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with positive Yamabe constant. For any prescribed finite set $Λ\subset M$ containing at least two points, we construct a complete metric on $M\setminusΛ$, conformal to $g$, with scalar curvature $n(n-1)$. At each singularity, the local geometric term in the reduced action comes from the first nonzero homogeneous metric term of degree at most $(n-2)/2$ in finite conformal normal coordinates, or from the mass of the Green function metric when all such terms vanish. We completely solve Schoen's conjecture about singular Yamabe problem.

items.title: Classification of Smooth Alignable Voss Surfaces
items.summary: Alignable nets are grid structures that can collapse to a planar strip. This property simplifies on-site assembly and enables compact transport and storage. These structures are then deployed by a scissor motion at vertices in a desired location. In this article, we classify all non-developable surfaces supporting an alignable net that additionally have the geodesic-conjugate net property, namely, the alignable Voss surfaces. Using the surface elements and adapted frames, we show that these surfaces arise as rotation fields of either helicoidal pseudospherical surfaces or Amsler surfaces, resulting in two distinct classes. The first class consists of helicoidal Voss surfaces. Exploiting this helicoidal structure, we combine a kinematic interpretation with the Bour family to derive explicit immersion formulas depending on the isometric deformation and alignability parameters. Furthermore, we examine several subclasses and an extension of this result in detail. In particular, we study the notable case of infinitely many geodesic-conjugate nets on a helicoid and provide a kinematic explanation for why this phenomenon appears in computations. For the second class, we obtain the classification at the level of the fundamental forms and show that they correspond to certain $3$-parameter families of non-helicoidal intrinsic surfaces of revolution. These families are governed by general Painleve III solutions including both regular and nonregular solutions. Finally, a surprising feature of this class is that its members support geodesic isothermal-conjugate nets absent from Eisenhart's classification of the aforementioned nets, thereby identifying a missing case in that classification.

items.title: Initial-boundary value problems for linear lattice differential equations
items.summary: We study initial-boundary value problems for linear lattice differential equations on the half-line. We first give a systematic account of fundamental solutions for equations with general finite-range interactions. We then develop complementary approaches based on reflection, the Laplace transform, and the unified transform method, obtaining contour integral and Bessel-function representations of solutions. For the semidiscrete diffusion equation, we justify these representations for continuous boundary data and initial data of polynomial growth, establish uniqueness in the corresponding growth class, and derive spatial estimates and long-time properties, including asymptotic periodicity. We also treat nonhomogeneous equations, Robin boundary conditions, nonsymmetric coefficients, and a class of time-dependent coefficients. Finally, higher-order examples illustrate how the unified transform approach extends beyond second-order equations.

items.title: Wandering exposed Julia components of rational maps
items.summary: We prove that every wandering exposed Julia component of a rational map is a point. Here a Julia component is exposed if it meets the boundary of a Fatou domain. The theorem extends the corresponding result for polynomials to rational maps, without any assumption on critical recurrence. The proof combines an enhanced nest with a covering estimate for multiply connected pullback domains.

items.title: There is no universal $F_σ$ equivalence relation
items.summary: Rosendal proved that any $K_σ$ equivalence relation is Borel reducible to $\ell_\infty$. We prove that for every $F_σ$ equivalence relation $F$ on a Polish space, there is an $F_σ$ real linear subspace $H$ of $\ell_2$ such that the coset relation $x\mathrel{E_H}y$ if and only if $x-y\in H$ has no Baire-measurable reduction to $F$. In particular, there is no $F_σ$ equivalence relation universal under Borel reducibility for all $F_σ$ equivalence relations. This answers a question of Rosendal.

items.title: The Keller-Segel Model for Chemotaxis on Metapopulation Graphs and Graphons
items.summary: Many models of spatial populations use directed motion towards environmental attractants as a mechanism for spatial pattern formation. While prior approaches typically focus on partial differential equation models for directed motion in continuous space, it is natural to consider the dynamics of biological and social systems on a metapopulation featuring well-mixed local patches and spatial motion between patches. In this paper, we formulate a version of the Keller-Segel model for chemotaxis on a graph metapopulation, modeling a chemoattractant that can diffuse across patches and a population of individuals who move through a biased random walk through comparing chemoattractant levels along edges of the metapopulation network. We also derive a continuum limit for our model describing chemotaxis in a population on patches connected by a graphon, showing that our resulting integro-differential equation model arises as the limit of our discrete patch model for families of large deterministic or random graphs. Through linear stability analysis, we derive conditions on the chemotactic sensitivity required to produce instability of a spatially uniform equilibrium for our Keller-Segel models in terms of the reaction parameters and the eigenvalues of the Laplacian operator for the metapopulation graph or graphon. Through a mix of weakly nonlinear stability analysis, numerical simulations, and analytical bounds on solutions, we can also characterize the form of pattern-forming instability in our graphon model and show how our choice of demographic dynamics for the population and the graphon adjacency function can impact the long-time total population size and chemoattractant concentration achieved in emergent spatial patterns.

items.title: Restricted variational principle for Lyapunov exponents of typical one-step cocycles
items.summary: In this paper, we study the multifractal formalism for Lyapunov exponents of typical one-step cocycles. We establish a variational relation between the Legendre transform of topological pressure of the generalized singular value function and measure-theoretic entropies. As a consequence, we show that the restricted variational principle of Lyapunov exponents holds for typical one-step cocycles. Furthermore, we prove a variational principle formula for the generalized singular value function.

items.title: Comparison of the Bergman and Szegő kernels on arbitrary bounded pseudoconvex domains with $C^2$ boundary
items.summary: On every bounded pseudoconvex domain $Ω\Subset\mathbb C^n$, $n\ge2$, with $C^2$ boundary, we prove $K_Ω/S_Ω\le C_{Ω,\varepsilon} δ_Ω^{-1}|\logδ_Ω|^{1+\varepsilon}$ near the boundary for every $\varepsilon>0$, where $δ_Ω$ denotes the boundary distance. For each positive nondecreasing $H(s)=o(s)$, a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex complete Reinhardt domain in $\mathbb C^2$ shows that the logarithmic factor cannot be replaced by $H(|\logδ_Ω|)$.

items.title: Sequential Monte Carlo Sampling of Feasible Regions Represented by R-Functions
items.summary: Feasible-region sampling and volume estimation become increasingly inefficient when constraints define only a small fraction of a convenient bounding domain. We combine R-functions, which encode compound feasibility as a continuous signed field, with sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) samplers. The proposed construction exploits not only the sign of the R-function, which determines exact feasibility, but also its continuous negative values outside the feasible set, which provide graded information on constraint violation. Logistic intermediate distributions use this information to guide particles progressively towards feasibility, while the final target distribution remains uniform on the feasible region. Experiments on intersections and unions, including disconnected cases of hyperballs, show substantial variance reductions relative to direct rejection sampling, with the statistical advantage generally increasing as the feasible fraction decreases. For sufficiently small feasible regions, these advantages persist even after accounting for computational cost. To isolate the benefit of continuous R-function information, we also compare the proposed method with an SMC sampler with a region-only (RO) construction that uses the same sequential particle machinery but retains only binary feasible/infeasible information. We demonstrate that the R-function-informed SMC method concentrates particles in the feasible region earlier and produces lower-variance volume estimates than RO.

items.title: Set-theoretic inevitability
items.summary: After defining the concept of inevitability for statements with the modal logic of forcing, we raise the question of which statements are inevitable under $\mathsf{ZFC}$ and under large cardinal hypotheses. We show that $\mathsf{SOA}$ (defined as $\mathsf{ZFC}^-$ + $\mathsf V=\mathsf{HC}$) plus the $\boldsymbolΣ^1_2$-perfect set property is $\mathsf{ZFC}$-inevitable, and that Projective Determinacy is inevitable in the theory of $\mathsf{ZFC}$ with a proper class of Woodin cardinals. We then discuss the possible conceptual significance of these results for the foundations of set theory.

items.title: Reflection symmetry in the equal-mass $1+N$ coorbital problem for $5\leq N\leq8$
items.summary: We study reflection symmetry in the equal-mass Newtonian \(1+N\) coorbital problem for \(N=5,6,7,8\). We prove that every collision-free solution of the angular central-configuration equations has a reflection axis. As a consequence, every non-coalescent limit of planar central configurations consisting of one dominant mass and \(N\) equal small masses is reflection-symmetric about a line through the dominant body. Our proof combines analytic arguments with rigorous computer-assisted verification. For each possible reflection, we introduce variables that measure the deviation from that reflection and vanish exactly when the configuration has that symmetry. The central-configuration equations yield a symmetric matrix equation in these variables. Concavity of the force derivative and estimates of the resulting quadratic forms reduce the symmetry problem to finitely many rigorously verified inequalities. Although the details depend on \(N\), the same general method applies in all four cases. We also obtain, as a separate result, the complete three-class classification for \(N=5\), up to the natural equivalences.

items.title: On nonnegative solutions of the differential inequality $Δ_pu+ Δ_q u+V(x)u^s\leq 0$ on Riemannian manifolds
items.summary: In this paper, we are concerned with differential inequalities with $(p,q)$-Laplacian operator on Riemannian manifolds. Using a test function argument, we establish Liouville-type theorems under the manifold's geometry and the potential's behavior at infinity. Finally, we give an example showing the sharpness when $V(x)$ is a positive constant.

items.title: Approximation algorithm for mixed volumes of a constant number of convex bodies
items.summary: We study the computation of mixed volumes of convex sets given as rational subspace sections of bodies described by membership oracles. The sets need not have nonempty interior. For positive multiplicities $α_1+\cdots+α_k=n$, we give a randomized algorithm that computes a relative $\varepsilon$-approximation with probability at least $1-δ$. Its running time is polynomial in Gurvits' factor $Γ_α=(n^n/n!)\prod_iα_i!/α_i^{α_i}$, the input presentation length, and $\varepsilon^{-1}$, and linear in $1+\logδ^{-1}$, with degree independent of $k$. The running-time bound holds for every choice of the random bits, and zero mixed volumes are detected exactly. We extend the capacity-scaling and sampling method of Narayanan--Roy by using rational projections and a smooth mixed Monge--Ampère representation. In particular, the algorithm runs in randomized polynomial time when the number of distinct convex sets is bounded above by a constant.

items.title: A paintbox characterization of labeled partitions
items.summary: We study pairs of labeled random partitions $(Π,τ)$ with a finite label set $E$, which can be thought of as a random mutation and coalescence mechanism of a countable number of blocks. Labeled exchangeable partition probability functions (LEPPFs) are defined via labeled analogues of Kingman's paintbox partitions. They satisfy normalization, symmetry and consistency in a multivariate sense. Under an equivariance condition, a representation for $(Π,τ)$ in terms of labeled paintbox partitions is derived, leading to a full characterization of LEPPFs by a unique probability measure $G$. This representation is extended to jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs using a product measure $F \otimes G$. These results yield a one-to-one correspondence between distributions of jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs and pairs of exchangeable distributions and LEPPFs.

items.title: Strong existence for SDEs with singular drifts driven by fractional Brownian motion
items.summary: Let $B^H$ be a $d$-dimensional fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1/2)$. We prove the existence of a strong solution to $$d X_t=b(t,X_t)d t+d B_t^H, X_0=x_0\in R^d,$$when $b\in L^q([0,T];L^p(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)),2\le p,q<\infty$ and the subcritical Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin condition $\frac1q+\frac{Hd}{p}<1-H$ is satisfied. Thus, within the finite-exponent range $p,q\ge2$, the strong-existence result covers the full subcritical region, including the regime $p<2Hd$, where a uniform strong Novikov condition may fail. The proof is based on a compactness criterion for Wiener functionals. Its main ingredients are an exponentially quantitative derivative estimate for the finite-dimensional densities of fractional Brownian motion, a conditional moment estimate obtained through a martingale representation of fractional Brownian motion, and a frequency-localized truncation of the Cameron--Martin shift. These estimates yield uniform Malliavin--Sobolev bounds for smooth approximations of the equation.

items.title: Data-dependent Compact Multinode Shepard Method
items.summary: We introduce a data-dependent compact multinode Shepard method for the approximation of scattered multivariate data. The proposed approach extends the compact multinode Shepard operator by incorporating nonlinear, data-dependent weights inspired by the weighted essentially non-oscillatory (WENO) methodology while preserving the partition of unity structure and the locality of the approximation. The construction is based on compactly supported multinode weight functions associated with local polynomial interpolants defined on unisolvent stencils. A smoothness indicator is employed to adapt the contribution of each stencil according to the local regularity of the underlying function, thereby reducing spurious oscillations near discontinuities while retaining the optimal approximation order in smooth regions. We establish the theoretical approximation properties of the proposed operator: it achieves the order of accuracy of its linear counterpart for sufficiently smooth functions and, under an explicit indicator-separation hypothesis, the same order is retained at every covered evaluation point near a jump discontinuity. Numerical experiments for local degrees up to four illustrate the performance of the method on both smooth and non-smooth data, on scattered as well as on gridded nodes.

items.title: On isoperimetric local-Bollobás-Thomason inequalities
items.summary: We prove the following isoperimetric-type inequality: for every convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and some $σ\subset[n]:=\{1,\dots,n\}$ there exists a suitable Hanner polytope $B_K$ with the same volume as $K$ and such that the volume of each of its orthogonal projections onto every subspace whose basis is formed by the canonical vectors $\{e_i:i\inτ\cup([n]\setminusσ)\}$, for every $τ\subseteqσ$, bounds from below the volume of the corresponding projections of $K$.

items.title: Unconditional Subexponential Arithmetic Circuits for Positive Factorial Multiples
items.summary: Let $τ(n)$ be the least number of binary additions, subtractions and multiplications required to construct $n$ from $1$ and $2$, with reuse of intermediate values. We show that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, some positive integer $m$ satisfies \[ τ(mk!)\leq \exp\!\left(O\!\left((\log k)^{2/3}(\log\log k)^{1/3}\right)\right). \] The proof combines unconditional results of Lenstra, Pila and Pomerance on smooth numbers in short intervals and on orders of genus-two Jacobians with a five-parameter family carrying a rational divisor class of infinite order. We encode rational divisor arithmetic, including the tests determining its branches, by a nonzero division-free integer circuit. A common finite sampling space yields circuits whose outputs collectively contain every prime at most $k$, and repeated squaring supplies the required factorial valuations. The circuit bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and GPT-6.1 Sol.

items.title: Approximation of structures:local and global
items.summary: We provide a mathematically rigorous definition of local approximation and demonstrate its applicability to some interesting classes of structures. In particular, we prove that any compact simple Lie group is locally approximated by finite groups. The definition and main examples are motivated by physics but the techniques are of model theory. Namely, we introduce the ultraproduct of emerging metric structures, which generalises the ultraproduct in metric model theory.

items.title: Exact Archimedean Flicker--Rallis Periods on Cohomological Minimal $K$-Types
items.summary: For the symmetric pair $(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C),\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb R))$, we compute the exact Flicker--Rallis period of a distinguished vector in a cohomological minimal $U(n)$-type, normalized by the Gel'fand--Tsetlin pairing of Hara--Miyazaki--Namikawa. Our main tool is a weight-independent identity between the Whittaker period and a compact $O(n)$-average. We determine the proportionality constant using the archimedean newform formula of Humphries--Jo, and evaluate the compact functional on the normalized distinguished vector. This yields an explicit formula for the Flicker--Rallis period for every cohomological weight.

items.title: A general quantified Wiener-Ikehara theorem
items.summary: Building on the technology developed in \cite{Deb-qik}, we establish a quantified Tauberian theorem under a flexible Wiener-Ikehara Tauberian condition and under several types of boundary behavior for the Laplace transform.

items.title: Asymptotics of the free path length in the periodic Lorentz gas in the Boltzmann-Grad limit
items.summary: We study the distribution of the free path length in the periodic Lorentz gas in the Boltzmann-Grad limit. For any unimodular Euclidean lattice and any smooth initial velocity distribution, we establish an asymptotic formula for the distribution function of the free path length with a polynomial rate of convergence. The proof combines the dynamical interpretation of the free path length in terms of expanding translates of horospherical orbits on the space of affine lattices, due to Marklof--Strömbergsson, with the effective equidistribution results of Kleinbock--Margulis and Kim. This extends the asymptotic formula of Boca--Zaharescu for the planar case to arbitrary dimension.

items.title: Triangulation of orbifolds with corners
items.summary: We prove that every compact orbifold with corners admits a triangulation in which the image of every codimension one face is a subcomplex. Faces need not be embedded, and the local groups may permute boundary components. The proof turns the boundary hyperplanes of linear charts into mirrors by means of the squaring map, which, unlike the folding $y\mapsto|y|$, is compatible with smooth changes of charts, and then applies the triangulation theorem for orbit spaces of proper Lie groupoids.

items.title: Landfall Geometry
items.summary: We study the negative gradient flow of analytic maps $f:X\to\R$ defined on compact analytic Riemannian manifolds without imposing any nondegeneracy or transversality assumptions. We construct tight isolating blocks around the connected components of the critical set $\Crit(f)$ and record only bounded-time contacts made after an orbit exits one block and before it makes landfall within the interior of another. These contacts assemble into a strict topological category $\cL$ -- called the landfall category -- whose classifying space $B\cL$ is shown to be simple homotopy equivalent to $X$ naturally over all down-sets of the flow partial order. The filtered homotopy type is independent of the isolating blocks. Passing to a finite subanalytic triangulation yields a flow-induced acyclic partial matching, and hence, an explicit finite chain complex generated by the non-exit simplices of the blocks which computes the homology of $X$. The finite model also computes the Morse--Conley spectral sequence over arbitrary coefficients; over a field, homological perturbation further produces a connection matrix whose entries are finite sums over descending contact itineraries.

items.title: Third-Order Weierstrass Points on Plane Quartics
items.summary: For a smooth plane quartic $C$, the $3$-Weierstrass points are the $300$ points (counted with weights) at which some plane cubic has contact order at least ten with $C$. Revisiting the work of Kamel and Elshareef, we write the third Veronese Wronskian as an $\text{SL}_3$-covariant form $Ω_3$ of degree $75$, given by a determinant of iterated Hamiltonian derivatives, and explain the special $3$-Weierstrass points through contact cubics and homologies preserving $C$. We determine $Ω_3$ for the Fermat, Komiya--Kuribayashi, Klein and Picard quartics; for the Klein quartic $Ω_3\equivΦ_6^2\,Φ_{21}\,(3Φ_{14}^3+21962\,Φ_6^7)$ modulo the curve, up to a non-zero scalar. Finally, the dectactic points of the Fermat quartic are not $4$-Weierstrass points, which disproves a conjecture of Kamel and Elshareef. All computations are supported by \texttt{SINGULAR} scripts.

items.title: On the transcendental Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture
items.summary: We prove the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture for transcendental Kähler classes in the case of trivial automorphisms. Indeed, we show the existence of Special Kähler Fujita Approximations of big cohomology classes associated to big test configurations, establishing the equivalence between the uniform $K$-stability and the strengthened version for models. More generally, we show that any big cohomology class on a compact Kähler manifold admits such Special Kähler Fujita Approximations: the volume and the analogue of the Riemann-Roch coefficient of the big class are both approximated by those of Kähler classes on higher compactifications.

items.title: Nonlocal Fisher--KPP propagation with heavy tails
items.summary: We study a nonlocal Fisher--KPP equation on the real line with compactly supported initial data. The reaction satisfies $f(s)\le f^{\prime}(0)s$ for $0\le s\le1$, with a power bound on $f^{\prime}(0)s-f(s)$ near zero. For continuous even probability kernels $J$ comparable to $|x|^{-γ}$, $γ>1$, we prove a global two-sided estimate and locate every fixed level set with a bounded error in $\log|x|$. The propagation scale is $\exp(f'(0)t/γ)$ for every $γ>1$. This differs sharply from the free-boundary propagation studied by Du and Ni \cite{DuNiJEMS}. For polynomial kernel tails, spreading in their model has linear, algebraic or $t\log t$ growth. We also obtain arrival-time and weighted-integral estimates and identify a spatial tail coefficient when $|x|^γJ(x)$ has a positive limit.

items.title: Uniformity of the minimal exponent on the GIT boundary of projective hypersurfaces
items.summary: Let $X$ be a non-stable (in the sense of GIT) hypersurface of degree $d \ge 3$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{n}$. S. G. Park proved that the global minimal exponent of $X$ satisfies the inequality $\widetildeα(X) \le \frac{n+1}{d}$. In this paper, we establish the uniform sharpness of this inequality: we prove that $\widetildeα(X) = \frac{n+1}{d}$ holds for a general member $X$ of every irreducible component of the strictly semistable locus. Moreover, a general point of each irreducible component of the GIT boundary $\partial M^{\mathrm{GIT}}$ admits a strictly semistable zero-weight representative with this minimal exponent. By the lower semicontinuity of the minimal exponent on the affine cone and a theorem of Mustaţă--Popa for general linear combinations of monomials, the problem is reduced to computing the log canonical thresholds, at the cone vertex, of the monomial ideals associated with the maximal strictly semistable supports with respect to a maximal torus and their weight-zero parts. Since the barycenter of the degree-$d$ simplex lies in the convex hull of each of these supports, Howald's formula forces these thresholds to be uniformly equal to $\frac{n+1}{d}$.

items.title: Extremal Lyapunov exponents in random and simultaneous dynamics
items.summary: In this manuscript, we consider finitely many maps, all of which are defined on a compact probability space, with at least one map in the collection having degree strictly bigger than 1. Working with two different, however related, dynamics generated by this setting, we obtain an expression for the extremal Lyapunov exponents, that characterise the instability of typical orbits, as the limit of the averages of the logarithm of the operator norm of linear cocycles of generic orbits. We obtain this as a consequence to the Kingman's ergodic theorem for a subadditive sequence of measurable functions, which naturally generalises the Birkhoff's ergodic theorem, in each of the cases.

items.title: Interior gradient estimates for mean curvature equations on Riemannian manifolds
items.summary:
In this paper, we study interior gradient estimates for solutions of \[ \operatorname{div}_{M}\left(  rac{
abla u}{\sqrt{1+|
abla u|_g^2}} ight) =f(x,
abla u) \] on a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge2$. Under a Ricci curvature lower bound and a Hessian comparison for the distance function, we derive polynomial and exponential gradient bounds under structural conditions on $f$ and its horizontal and vertical derivatives. The estimates quantify the dependence on the radius, the oscillation of the solution, and the geometric and analytic parameters. In the Euclidean case, we also improve the dependence on the radius in the gradient estimate of Xu~\cite[Theorem~1.1(d)]{Xu2026}. As applications, we obtain Liouville-type results for entire solutions under suitable curvature and growth assumptions.

items.title: A Unified Framework for Image-to-3D Part Generation via Variable Granularity
items.summary: Controllable 3D part generation is pivotal for digital asset creation, yet existing methods lack the flexibility to accommodate diverse user workflows requiring varying levels of control. In this paper, we introduce FlexPart, a unified image-to-3D part generation framework that supports variable-granularity geometric conditions within a single model. By seamlessly integrating heterogeneous inputs, ranging from sparse points to dense bounding boxes and masks, via gated adaptive modulation, FlexPart unlocks a powerful cross-modal synergy. We also propose an asymmetric geometric guidance mechanism that leverages strong spatial priors to align representations across granularities, improving geometric consistency and facilitating inter-task synergy. Under mask conditioning on PartVerseXL, FlexPart reduces Part CD by 16.6% relative to TripoSG + SAM3D and by 10.5% relative to OmniPart, while maintaining competitive whole-mesh quality. The code can be found at https://github.com/Gucci233/FlexPart

items.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
items.summary: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With $S^2$, we extend PRH to embodied models and make sensorimotor alignment empirically measurable, offering insight into why an embodied model succeeds beyond its closed-loop success rate.

items.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
items.summary: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. Despite their different objectives, both concern the relationship between video observations and an evolving world. This survey adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for examining these developments. Viewing an observed video as a partial, lossy, and temporally ordered projection of a latent temporal world, we organize the literature around four complementary operations: reading infers world properties from observed video; writing synthesizes video from specified or learned world conditions; sharing integrates understanding and generation through common modeling mechanisms; and interacting predicts and updates world states under actions and evolving observations. This perspective distinguishes temporal coherence in observed or generated sequences from consistency in the underlying world state. Across tasks, representations, models, datasets, and benchmarks, we trace a shift in emphasis from clip-level recognition and perceptual fidelity toward persistent state, controllable evolution, physical and causal validity, and evaluation grounded in interaction and downstream decisions, and we distill the open challenges that follow.

items.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
items.summary: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution. Running all candidate solutions to completion can be computationally demanding, so recent work prunes the candidate pool after generating only a short prefix, committing further computation only to the surviving candidates. Existing pruning strategies divide broadly into two categories: Quality-based methods assign a score to each partial solution and discard those predicted to ultimately lead to an incorrect final solution, while diversity-based methods select partial solutions that follow different reasoning trajectories and are therefore likely to cover different final solutions. The tension between these two objectives is an instance of exploration versus exploitation, yet little to no prior work on pruning exposes this trade-off directly, let alone optimizes it. In this paper, we introduce a pruning procedure that addresses this trade-off directly by optimizing pass@$k$ over the selected solution pool. In particular, it chooses the pool to maximize the probability that at least one of its partial solutions, when continued to completion, yields a correct answer. Because this objective simultaneously rewards high-quality partial solutions and penalizes redundancy among them, quality and diversity are naturally balanced by the criterion itself rather than through separate ad-hoc design choices. On eight open-weight reasoning models, our method outperforms existing quality-based and diversity-based pruning strategies. The gains are particularly pronounced when the pruning procedure keeps a moderate number of partial solutions for continued generation, highlighting the value of directly balancing quality and diversity during pruning.

items.title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
items.summary: We consider online monitoring of an AI system that produces a sequence of decisions. At each round, the system outputs a proposed decision together with a confidence score estimating the trustworthiness of the decision. The decision and confidence score need not be produced by the same model: for example, one agent may propose a decision, while a separate verifier agent evaluates it and outputs a correctness or safety score. Based on this information, we must decide whether to accept the AI decision automatically or consult an expert, such as a human auditor, who reviews the proposal and either accepts or corrects it. We formulate this task as an online constrained optimization problem in which the goal is to minimize the frequency of expert auditing while guaranteeing that the fraction of AI errors that go unaudited stays below a user-defined threshold. We derive a family of algorithms with provable error-control guarantees with no assumptions, including a method that is optimally efficient: it asymptotically attains the best achievable auditing rate for both adversarial and i.i.d. data streams. Experiments on screening harmful requests to large language models, qualitative text annotation, and data labeling show that our methods achieve valid error control in practice while substantially reducing the need for human auditing compared to baselines.

items.title: How Does RL Post-training Induce Skill Composition? A Case Study on Countdown
items.summary: While reinforcement learning (RL) successfully enhances reasoning in large language models, its role in fostering compositional generalization (the ability to synthesize novel skills from known components) is often conflated with mere length generalization. To this end, we study what RL post-training teaches about skill composition and how the composition structure affects the skill transfer. We focus on the Countdown task (given n numbers and a target, form an expression that evaluates to the target) and analyze model solutions as expression trees, where each subtree corresponds to a reusable subtask and thus can be viewed as a "skill." Tracking tree shapes and their success rates over training, we find: (i) out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization to larger n and to unseen tree shapes, indicating compositional reuse of subtasks; (ii) the order of skill acquisition depends upon the composition structure---models master shallow balanced trees (workload is balanced between subtasks) before deep unbalanced ones, with persistent fragility on right-heavy structures for a fixed composition depth. Our diagnostic reveals what is learned, in what order, and where generalization fails, clarifying how RL-only post-training induces OOD generalization beyond what standard metrics such as pass@k reveal. To study the implications of our findings for real-world tasks, we present a preliminary study on formal theorem proving.

items.title: SoundnessBench: Can Your AI Scientist Really Tell Good Research Ideas from Bad Ones?
items.summary: Autonomous AI research agents aim to speed up scientific discovery by automating the research pipeline from hypothesis generation to peer review. However, existing benchmarks rarely test a fundamental bottleneck whether LLMs can judge the methodological viability of a research idea $\textbf{before}$ investing time and computational resources. Without a reliable ``first-gate'' filter, autonomous agents risk scaling flawed methodology rather than accelerating meaningful science. We introduce $\textbf{SoundnessBench}$, a curated benchmark of 1,099 real research proposals, with source verified extraction, reviewer-derived proxy labels, and proposal-only expert judgments on a subset of 327 proposals. Across 12 frontier LLMs, our evaluation reveals a pervasive $\textbf{optimism bias}$: standard prompting yields a $74.0\%$ mean false-positive rate. Aggressive prompting reduces false approvals but substantially increases false rejections. Additional analyses show that optimism persists under controls for public corpus contamination, and surface features, as well as in literature-grounded agent evaluation. These results suggest a limitation in judging scientific soundness, indicating that current LLMs are not yet reliable as standalone gatekeepers for scientific rigor.

items.title: OpenTac: An Open Ecosystem for Customizable, Scalable, and Transferable 3D Tactile Sensing
items.summary: We present OpenTac, a novel sensor and a full-stack ecosystem for tactile skins that are highly customizable, scalable, and readily deployed in downstream robot control and learning applications. Our core contribution is twofold. First, we develop a scalable resistive tactile skin with a structured deformable overlay that converts tangential loading into spatially varying pressure. Differential responses across neighboring "taxels" support decoding of local shear vectors, and the common-mode response encodes normal force. Second, we provide a highly customizable sensor design tool that is able to automatically generate fabrication files for these tactile skins from 2D outlines and developable 3D surfaces, including from abstract descriptions such as text (e.g., "design a sensor for a size 9 shoe insole"). We develop an ecosystem around the OpenTac sensor, including the CAD design tool, a sensor simulator, cross-sensor transfer, and fast/adaptive data acquisition. We demonstrate the broad applicability of the OpenTac-CAD sensor design tool by designing and fabricating more than 30 sensors across a variety of robot embodiments. We characterize the three-dimensional tactile fields produced by OpenTac with a commercial, high-precision force/torque sensor. We demonstrate the broad applicability of 3D tactile sensing across contact-rich feedback control and manipulation policy learning on four real-world robot embodiments. Additionally, adaptive acquisition enables kilohertz-rate partial readouts, exceeding full-array raster scanning on the same sensor by 19.2X at 16 sampled taxels per update for a 1024-taxel skin. We provide all hardware, software, and result videos are at opentac.github.io

items.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
items.summary: Auditing whether a text-to-image (T2I) model was fine-tuned on a particular image collection is difficult: a model can absorb collection-level visual characteristics without reproducing training images. Proactive dataset-use auditing plants a shared signal in a dataset before release, then later checks whether that signal appears in a suspect model's generated outputs. Existing approaches often trade off verifiability, fidelity, robustness, and deployability. We introduce $\textbf{SpectralCanary}$, which uses a smooth low-pass mask to blend a fixed canary image into every collection image while leaving captions unchanged and requiring neither auxiliary generation nor per-image optimization. A lightweight verifier detects the transferred signal in suspect-model outputs. Across eight tests on the Pokemon dataset and three realistic data transformations, spanning two architectures families, SpectralCanary achieves the highest average per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR ($91.1\%$) and fixed threshold model-level accuracy using 30 generations ($94.8\%$) among the evaluated methods. Across five datasets spanning artistic, medical, satellite, and fashion domains with SD3.5, SpectralCanary averages $92.4\%$ per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR while preserving the released images (SSIM $0.989$, LPIPS $0.022$) with a near-zero mean change FID (mean $Δ$FID $0.05$) across datasets. Matched-energy ablations on Pokemon and ROCOv2 support our design choice, low-frequency placement transfers more reliably compared to mid/high-frequency placement. Under the evaluated adaptive attacks, the most effective removal requires aggressive modification and incurs more than $25$ $Δ$FID points. These results identify low-frequency visual signals as effective carriers for collection-level T2I audit traces.

items.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
items.summary: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage. We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting. Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis. The strongest prompted configuration reaches 0.477 accuracy on a stratified 1,000-ticket test subset, versus 0.879 for fine-tuned DistilBERT on the same tickets. Isotonic lowers expected calibration error without reliably improving discrimination: GPT-4o-mini few-shot has one confidence value before and after recalibration and correctness AUROC 0.500. We therefore report correctness AUROC and tie-aware risk-coverage area alongside ECE. At the analytically derived break-even probability 0.80, seven prompted configurations defer all tickets; Haiku few-shot routes only 19/1,000. An LLM-only agreement control and margin/entropy rejection baselines further separate calibration from discrimination. The findings are scoped to this dataset, prompt design, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; the work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or universal deployment certification.

items.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Meta-reinforcement learning aims to train agents that adapt quickly to unseen tasks from limited interaction, but this requires representing task evidence over long interaction histories. Classical recurrent agents compress experience into hidden states, while transformer-based agents retrieve from past trajectories at quadratic memory and computation cost. In this work, we propose Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation (METTA) for meta-reinforcement learning. It decomposes the fast adaptation phase into two temporal scales: a causal neural memory performs fine-grained within-episode adaptation with linear sequence complexity, while compact episode-level summaries support long-range cross-episode task inference without attending over the full interaction history. Moreover, equipping agents with neural memory provides sufficient expressive capacity and test-time training capability, enabling effective adaptation to unseen held-out tasks and task families at meta-test time. On unseen held-out Meta-World ML10/45 test environments, METTA achieves a success rate over $50\%$ while maintaining a low training budget and short wall-clock time. On long-context sparse-reward PointMaze tasks, it outperforms transformer-based baselines by exhibiting more structured exploration behavior. These results show that METTA provides an efficient path toward more adaptive and scalable long-context meta-RL.

items.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
items.summary: Frontier coding agents are becoming increasingly adept at 3D modeling. Yet, they still face challenges when building objects meant to be assembled in the physical world, often creating invalid assemblies with floating, colliding, or disconnected parts. We argue that providing agents with tools for assembling builds and verifying their physical feasibility is sufficient for them to produce physically valid assemblies that still adhere to input prompts. Focusing on the domain of LEGO brick builds, we present BrickWright, a framework for generating physically feasible brick builds from text or image prompts using pre-trained agents, where a build is physically feasible if it uses only real parts, has no colliding or floating parts, and forms a connected structure if possible. BrickWright guides agents to create builds by writing code with BrickLayer, a Python toolkit with two main components: an ergonomic brick assembly API that halves inference cost compared to working in raw LDraw, and a validator that provides feedback on physical feasibility. Whereas baseline agents achieve physical validity rates ranging from only 9% (GPT-6 Luna) to 69% (GPT-6 Astra), BrickWright-guided agents achieve 100% validity on a sample of 512 prompts, while improving prompt adherence for lightweight agents and maintaining it for stronger agents. Additionally, they outperform specialized models on the text-to-brick task. Code is available on our project page: https://avalovelace1.github.io/brickwright/

items.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
items.summary: Tool-using language model agents rely on environmental facts to decide whether an action is permitted. When a tool response omits a safety-relevant fact, an agent may carry out a prohibited action even though the user request is benign and every returned statement is true. We introduce \bench{}, an executable benchmark for evaluating unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery in LLM agents under missing evidence. It contains 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains. By systematically suppressing critical facts, the benchmark measures unsafe execution under critical evidence omission and determines the minimum observed failure cardinality, including failures with full evidence and cases with no observed failure after exhaustive testing. An independent audit tool tests whether agents seek missing facts and then withhold prohibited actions while completing permissible tasks. The benchmark reveals substantial variation across the ten models in omission robustness, evidence acquisition, and appropriate action. Resistance to missing evidence does not necessarily translate into useful recovery. Recovery access reduces unsafe execution for all ten models, but agents differ in whether they actively obtain the missing facts and use them to act appropriately in both worlds.

items.title: Gate3DGen: A Pre-processing Model that Selectively Purifies Real-World Images for 3D Generation
items.summary: Single-image 3D generation has achieved high fidelity on curated benchmarks, yet degrades sharply on real-world images with uneven illumination, blur, and occlusions. Purifying such inputs requires deciding when to intervene and preserving the visual cues needed for 3D generation, while leaving clean inputs unchanged. We introduce Gate3DGen, a selective pre-processing model that gates image inputs to existing 3D generators without retraining them. A degradation-aware router bypasses inputs classified as clean and extracts features to guide purification of the remaining inputs. Conditioned on these features, a 3D-oriented one-step purifier purifies degraded inputs with spatial losses that encourage preservation of object identity, contours, and textural cues. To provide paired supervision, we construct a synthetic data engine that renders clean views of 3D assets and synthesises composite degradations. On the synthetic benchmark, the purifier improves image fidelity and downstream 3D geometry in only 2.3s on average, reducing TRELLIS.2 mesh distance by 61.5% relative to degraded inputs. VLM evaluation and human preferences on real photographs further support identity preservation and degradation correction. More demos and code are available at https://supra-3d.github.io/gate3dgen.

items.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
items.summary: Many recent open-weight language models use n-gram embedding tables to improve performance. These tables store learned representations of short token sequences, such as pairs or triples of consecutive tokens, which the model retrieves during processing. However, they can require substantial memory: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, for example, allocates 196 billion parameters to its Engram n-gram memory. We therefore investigate whether this memory cost can be reduced while preserving the performance improvement that the tables provide. We propose storing n-gram embeddings at low precision and systematically investigate different quantization methods and bit allocations across tables. Across nanochat-, Llama-, and GPT-2-family models trained from scratch, four-bit tables save approximately 75% of table memory while preserving more than 99% of the validation-loss improvement from adding the tables. Using fewer bits leads to a larger drop in performance, although we find that a short fine-tuning phase recovers a significant part of this loss. In addition, reinvesting the saved memory in larger tables can improve performance beyond that of the original full-precision tables while still using less memory. These table memory savings also extend to large existing models: on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, low-bit tables save 47-55% of table memory, with perplexity increases of less than 1.2% and largely preserved downstream task performance. These findings establish low-bit precision as a practical way to reduce the memory requirements of n-gram embeddings and use the saved capacity to improve model performance.

items.title: Uncensored Is Not Unbiased: Abliteration Removes Refusals but Not Script-Dependent Bias About Taiwan
items.summary: "Abliterated" ("uncensored") builds of open-weight language models remove the activation direction that mediates refusal, and are popular partly on the assumption that a model that no longer refuses is free of political censorship. We test this on two matched pairs of 2-bit models: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, each against a community abliteration. Each model judged 22 statement pairs (on the Republic of China (Taiwan), 1989 Tiananmen, control countries) in Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese (a character-level conversion) and English, and answered 27 open questions per script. Script mattered far more than abliteration: the original Bolt scored +0.58 on Index S (-1: People's Republic of China (PRC) position; +1: ROC position) in Traditional Chinese, +0.57 in English and +0.05 in Simplified Chinese, and affirmed "Taiwan is part of the PRC" with probability 0.91 in Simplified but 0.06 in Traditional characters; abliteration changed its scores by at most 0.06, mostly by raising "yes" on both sides. In Qwen, abliteration removed every refusal on 1989 and raised scores by 0.21 to 0.34, yet the abliterated Qwen still affirmed that Taiwan is part of the PRC in all three scripts. Naming the state the Republic of China (Taiwan) raised every model's score by 0.10 to 0.33 but left the script gap. Control pairs showed no script gap; both edits changed only their declared tensors. In 740,000 web documents, Simplified text on Taiwan used PRC-framing terms 3.7 times as often as Traditional text. Steering the script gap away failed; a stance direction from the ROC wording raised scores on new statements by 0.04 to 0.06; negated, it lowered them more. A four-sentence system prompt raised the abliterated Qwen to +0.93 to +0.97. Keyword scoring rules failed the models closest to the ROC position mostly for attributing or denying the PRC claim. Uncensored is not unbiased.

items.title: OmniRay: Camera-Agnostic Monocular 3D Reconstruction with Composite Ray Fields
items.summary: Monocular models recover 3D geometry from a single image in one pass, but most assume a pinhole camera and produce distorted geometry on the wide-angle imagery produced by fisheye and panoramic lenses. Camera-aware models remove this assumption by predicting a per-pixel ray field. However, they represent different camera geometries using a single fixed basis to capture both the overall camera projection and its finer variations. We argue that camera geometry can be viewed as having a hierarchy of complexity for representing rays. We present OmniRay, a feed-forward model whose Ray Module is composed of three components: a monotone radial base that captures radially symmetric structure, a spherical-harmonic residual for smooth deviations from it, and a free-form residual for remaining local variation. These components are composed as successive rotations on the sphere, allowing the representation to accommodate diverse camera geometries. Given a single image, OmniRay predicts a ray direction and an up-to-scale radial distance for every pixel, from which a 3D point cloud is recovered without needing camera information at inference time. Extensive experiments across different camera configurations demonstrate that OmniRay establishes a new state-of-the-art in camera-agnostic monocular 3D reconstruction.

items.title: GigaBench: Benchmarking Learnable Representations for Gigapixel Image Compression and Super-Resolution
items.summary: Learnable Representations (LRs) can fit parametric families of functions to diverse kinds of signals. These emergent neural-native data formats are gathering interest in the scientific community due to their compactness, resolution-agnosticism and amenability to direct neural processing. On the other hand, gigapixel images are becoming increasingly widespread across a variety of scientific, cultural, and industrial domains. In this paper, we present GigaBench, the first benchmark and experimental evaluation focused on deploying LRs with gigapixel imagery. GigaBench includes images collected, acquired, and synthetically rendered across diverse domains, and addresses image compression and super-resolution. We adapt a representative set of LRs, spanning Implicit, Hybrid, and Explicit methods, so as to operate reliably at the gigapixel scale on consumer hardware. Through systematic evaluation across reconstruction quality, model size, compression and inference times, we identify consistent trends across methods and suggest actionable guidance for future investigation.

items.title: ATTUNE: Agentic Throughput Tuning for LLM Training
items.summary: The throughput of an LLM training job depends on its recipe: how the model is split across GPUs, how memory is traded for compute, and which kernels and communication overlaps it uses. The best recipe changes with every model, accelerator and framework version. Automated tuners search a fixed space of knobs and check only that a job runs, so they miss levers outside that space and can ship a configuration that silently changes training. ATTUNE is a coding agent that tunes any working recipe unattended within a GPU-hour budget. Guided by a skill of search rules, scripts and lessons from past tuning campaigns, it diagnoses each run and changes one lever at a time. A correctness gate outside the agent refuses any argument known to change the training objective. ATTUNE tunes Amazon's production post-training recipes on H100, H200 and B200 clusters, raising throughput by 1.7x on average. It beats the published throughput of four of NVIDIA's own benchmark recipes on NVIDIA's AutoModel framework by 6-17%. On models held out from its development, it improves the strongest public recipes most where they were written for another setting, by up to 2.6x on MiniMax-M2, and least where the vendor tuned them for the same hardware. Given the same GPU-hour budget, it outperforms existing automated tuners, including Bayesian optimization, random search and OptiCo, a recent LLM-agent tuner. Its gain on GLM-4.5 is more than four times the best alternative's. The same coding agent without ATTUNE's skill gains less and fails half its launches. We release ATTUNE at https://github.com/amazon-science/attune and OpenRecipes, a leaderboard of tuned and verified training recipes, at https://openrecipes.ai.

items.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
items.summary: Standard implementations of softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy have two numerical bugs. The first bug, Softmax Collapse, rounds the target logit's gradient to zero if that one logit is much larger than the others, resulting in gradients that no longer sum to zero. The second bug, Softmax Cancellation, occurs when student logits are close to teacher logits, and produces non-zero gradients even when the student and teacher logits are equal. We present simple implementations of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy that fix both bugs. Our fix eliminates the previously-observed "Slingshot" phenomenon, speeds up grokking with weight decay, prevents accuracy collapse without weight decay, stops student networks from drifting away from the teacher during distillation, and shows that after memorization, logit growth is bounded by an equilibrium between weight decay and Adam's $ε$ hyperparameter.

items.title: UniVOE: A Removal-Driven Framework for Interaction-Aware Universal Video Object Editing
items.summary: Video object removal and injection are reciprocal editing operations between object-present and object-absent video states, yet they differ substantially in training difficulty. Removal can be effectively bootstrapped from video inpainting and further adapted to erase object-related interaction effects. Injection, however, requires large-scale paired supervision to model object appearance, dynamics, and scene-dependent effects, while perfectly aligned real-world pairs are difficult to collect and synthetic data lacks sufficient realism and diversity. To address this challenge, we present UniVOE, a removal-driven framework for training both video object removal and injection models. We first train an effect-aware remover by transferring video inpainting priors and finetuning on object-present/object-absent pairs. The trained remover converts real object-present videos into object-absent counterparts, creating large-scale paired supervision for injection. An injection model is trained on these pairs in the reverse direction to recover objects together with their dynamics and interaction effects. Moreover, since pixel-level reconstruction alone cannot adequately capture perceptual realism, we introduce a reward-based post-training method that aligns injection results with human preferences using a proprietary reward model. Experiments against strong open-source and commercial systems demonstrate that UniVOE achieves state-of-the-art performance on both object removal and injection, particularly in challenging interaction-effect cases.

items.title: WorldForge V2: Eliciting Camera-Trajectory Alignment in Video Diffusion Models
items.summary: Video diffusion models have learned rich 3D/4D priors, making them promising for scene generation and video re-rendering. However, their use in spatial tasks is limited by imprecise camera control, spatial and temporal inconsistencies, and entangled camera motion with scene dynamics. Existing approaches, such as task-specific fine-tuning and post-process warping, often introduce visual artifacts, generalize poorly, or incur high computational costs. We propose WorldForge V2 to achieve accurate camera control while preserving the generative capabilities of pretrained video models. We first develop a training-free guidance framework using warped references to iteratively refine generation along a target camera path. Optical-flow analysis identifies motion-related latent channels for selective guidance, helping separate motion control from appearance. A dual-path strategy further compares guided and unguided predictions to correct artifacts from imperfect references.
