A constructive procedure with exact membership tests recovers all stabilizing intervals. A numerical example with an uncertain plant family containing non-minimum-phase members illustrates a disconnected admissible set.

items.title: Using Finite-Time Control to Synthesize Dynamic Backup Control Barrier Functions
items.summary: This paper presents a novel approach for the construction of control barrier functions (CBFs) for controllable linear systems subject to multiple state and input constraints. The approach is based on the Dynamic Backup CBF (DB-CBF) framework, where the control policy is parametrized using the equilibrium subspace of the system. By using a minimum-energy finite-time controller, we show that the terminal set constraint trivially reduces to having an admissible equilibrium point. The proposed DB-CBF is easy to tune (one parameter), fully takes advantage of the input range (by minimizing the control effort), and guarantees constraint enforcement (by tracking a backup equilibrium point that can be reached safely in finite time).

items.title: Damage detection in railway wheels from impact-induced ultrasonic ring-down using self-referenced decay features
items.summary: This study evaluates a non-contact screening method for stationary railroad wheelsets using air-coupled ultrasonic measurements excited by hammer impacts. Two decay features are considered. First, an effective damping ratio is obtained by normalizing the measured decay rate by the dominant response frequency. Second, strike-to-strike variations are measured to assess the quality of the energy-decay fit for the overall wheel. The method was evaluated using 22 wheelsets at two railroad facilities. The analysis indicates that a random forest trained on one dataset and tested on another performed poorly. This result motivated a simpler approach based on thresholds applied to the two decay features, which fixed the feature definitions and calibrated the thresholds on either dataset. This approach correctly classified every wheelset in the other dataset. A more stringent wheel-level validation repeated second-feature selection and threshold calibration while each test wheelset was withheld. This procedure correctly classifies 21 of 22 wheelsets. All defective wheelsets are identified, while one healthy wheelset yields a false positive. The results further show that the two-feature detector transferred between the tested datasets for stationary assessment of wheel damage. Further evaluation is required using worn but serviceable wheels, controlled support conditions, and additional independent datasets.

items.title: Beyond MSE: Rician Likelihood Denoising for Self-Supervised Cardiac $T2$ and $T1ρ$ MRI
items.summary: Magnetic resonance imaging involves an inherent trade-off among spatial resolution, acquisition time, and noise. This trade-off contributes to long scan times and high cost. Deep learning has improved image denoising, but cardiac MRI remains difficult because high-resolution, rapid acquisitions generally lack corresponding low-noise ground truth. Self-supervised denoising offers a potential solution by learning from noisy image pairs or even single noisy acquisitions. However, we show that Noise2Void-style blind-spot denoising, which uses a mean squared error (MSE) loss and assumes zero-mean, independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) noise, is poorly suited to MR magnitude images. When applied to short-axis $T2$-weighted and $T1ρ$-weighted cardiac MRI with synthetic Rician noise, it produces biased denoised images and biased parametric maps of $T2$ and $T1ρ$. To address this limitation, we formulate self-supervised denoising as maximum likelihood estimation under a known Rician noise model. This yields unbiased denoisers that are competitive with supervised baselines.

items.title: LLM2Cert: LLM Synthesis of Certificates with SMT/Lean Verification
items.summary: Lyapunov functions and barrier certificates give state-space guarantees of stability and safety, but synthesizing and verifying them---especially for nonlinear, high-dimensional systems---remains an open challenge. Existing pipelines verify candidates with numerical solvers (sum-of-squares programs), interval methods, or satisfiability-modulo-theories (SMT) solvers, which often require relaxations, are conservative, or scale poorly with model dimension and nonlinearity. These limitations have also shaped benchmark design: standard test suites are dominated by low-dimensional polynomial systems chosen to suit what solvers can handle rather than what engineering applications require. We address both sides of this challenge. First, we introduce DynaCertBench, a benchmark of 105 instances: 80 non-redundant systems curated from the literature, extended with high-dimensional and control-constrained variants and new nonlinearly coupled systems, comprehensively spanning stability, region-of-attraction, forward-invariance, and safety tasks. Second, we present LLM2Cert, an LLM-driven framework that synthesizes candidate certificates and verifies them against their proof obligations: each obligation is routed to an SMT solver or directly to the Lean Proof-Repair agent. On DynaCertBench, LLM2Cert verifies 81 of 105 instances ($77.1\%$), a $17.1$ percentage point improvement over one-shot proposal without feedback. On the 81 fixed certificates, LLM2Cert verifies 22 that All-SMT leaves unresolved. Code and data are available at https://github.com/FormalCert-AI/llm2cert.

items.title: Skew-Induced Insertion Loss Deviation (SILD) and FOM_SILD: Metrics for Quantifying P/N Skew Effects in High-Speed Channels
items.summary: The rise of AI workloads and growing data center demands have driven the need for ultra-high-speed interconnects exceeding 200 Gb/s. As unit intervals (UI) shrink, even a few picoseconds of P/N skew can degrade serializer-deserializer (SerDes) performance. Traditional methods for quantifying skew fall short in capturing its impact. We introduce two new metrics: 1) Skew-Induced Insertion Loss Deviation (SILD) and 2) its complementary Figure of Merit (FOM_SILD), analytically developed to assess P/N skew effects. Measured S-parameters confirm FOM_SILD reciprocity, while simulations of 224G PAM4 SerDes show strong correlation with bit error rate (BER) trends. This approach offers a robust framework for analyzing skew in next-generation ultra-high-speed interconnects.

items.title: Practical Approaches to Quantifying Intra-Pair Skew Impact via Insertion Loss Deviation
items.summary: The surge in AI workloads and escalating data center requirements have created demand for ultra-high-speed interconnects exceeding 200 Gb/s. As unit intervals (UI) shrink, even a few picoseconds of intra-pair skew can significantly degrade serializer-deserializer (SerDes) performance. To quantify the impact of intra-pair skew, conventional time-domain methods are often unreliable for coupled interconnects due to skew variations across voltage levels, while frequency-domain approaches frequently fail to address reciprocity and symmetry issues. This can result in channels that meet skew specifications in one direction but not the other, despite the inherently reciprocal nature of skew impact. To address these limitations, we introduce two new reciprocal parameters for quantifying intra-pair skew effects: Skew-Induced Insertion Loss Deviation (SILD) and its complementary Figure of Merit (FOM SILD). Measurements conducted using 224 Gb/s SerDes IP and a variety of channels with different intra-pair skews demonstrate a strong correlation between FOM SILD and bit error rate (BER). Results show that when FOM SILD is below 0.2-0.3 dB, BER remains stable, indicating minimal signal integrity degradation; however, BER increases noticeably as FOM SILD exceeds 0.3 dB. Statistical analysis across more than 3,000 high-speed twinax cables reveals that the majority exhibit FOM SILD values less than 0.1 dB, underscoring the practical relevance of the proposed metrics for high-speed interconnect assessment.

items.title: Principles of Robot Autonomy
items.summary: Autonomous robots are moving rapidly from research labs into everyday life - on roads, in the air, in warehouses, and in space. Robot autonomy is no longer solely an academic pursuit, but a collection of mature, field-tested methods and tools that practitioners rely on in real-world deployments. This book offers a clear, unified introduction to the methods that make this possible. Built on decades of teaching at Stanford, the text develops the core elements of modern autonomy stacks within a single conceptual framework, bridging classical robotics and modern physical AI. Every major topic is paired with hands-on Jupyter notebooks and implementation-driven exercises, so readers build practical intuition alongside theoretical understanding. The result is a principled, accessible, and deployment-aware foundation for anyone seeking to design, analyze, or contribute to the next generation of autonomous systems. This is a comprehensive resource for students, engineers, and researchers entering one of today's fastest-growing fields.

items.title: AVAtt: A Free-Viewing Eye-Tracking Dataset and Benchmark for Visual Attention on Paintings
items.summary:
Saliency and scanpath models are developed almost exclusively on natural photographs, yet paintings are composed by artists to guide the viewer's eye and differ from photographs in texture, colour and abstraction. We introduce \avatt, a free-viewing eye-tracking dataset on 
Images{} paintings spanning sixteen art movements and five centuries, with 
Scanpaths{} scanpaths and 
Fixations{} fixations from 
Participants{} participants (\spPerImageMin--\spPerImageMax{} observers per painting). For every painting we release individual scanpaths with fixation timing and eye--screen distance, fixation maps, saliency maps smoothed at one degree of visual angle, temporal saliency videos and rich art metadata. We benchmark classic and deep saliency models against human agreement, revealing substantial headroom for art-aware models, and rank 44 scanpath-similarity measures, including a new language-free family of image-encoder metrics built on ten CNN, ViT and self-supervised encoders. With controls that remove viewing biases, we show that faces are fixated  aceEnrich$	imes$ more than expected and within half a second, that local structure draws the eye, that composition rules fitted from image content predict where people look, and that art style shapes how much viewers agree. Dataset, code and a Python package are available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Amine-CV/AVAtt.

items.title: Learning to Incentivise: Using Reinforcement Learning for Sustainable Urban Mobility
items.summary: Traffic management has traditionally focused on toll-based and road pricing solutions. However, road pricing often raises concerns about accessibility and public dissatisfaction, leading to its prohibition in some places, such as Finland. This study optimises the dynamic allocation of incentives to drivers, encouraging them to reroute onto alternative (potentially longer) paths to achieve greater societal benefit, reduced total travel time (TTT) and total emissions in the transportation network, contributing to sustainable urban mobility. We employ a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach to dynamically assign incentives to drivers to reduce both TTT and emissions, with travel times estimated using traffic simulation software. We demonstrate that, with an unlimited budget and an objective of minimising travel time, the incentive scheme reduces TTT by 16%, compared to the dynamic User-Equilibrium (UE) with a budget equivalent to about 11% of the UE total time. When the goal is to minimise emissions, a 9% reduction in CO2 emissions is observed under an unlimited budget. We demonstrate a critical trade-off: minimising TTT leads to an increase in emissions, while prioritising emission reductions raises TTT. However, with the right combination of weights in the multi-objective function, both TTT and total emissions are improved beyond the baseline.

items.title: Equivariant Experience Replay for Continual Learning in Imaging Inverse Problems
items.summary: In this work, we propose Equivariant Experience Replay, a new paradigm for achieving continual learning of deep networks for solving ill-posed imaging inverse problems. Inspired by recent advances on unsupervised learning methods such as equivariant imaging/splitting, we find the exploitation of group-symmetry structure is particularly relevant and effective in continual learning setting for ill-posed inversion tasks. We therefore propose this new experience replay scheme, which is tailored for such inverse problems. Our numerical study demonstrates the superiority of our method compared to existing continual learning methods for inverse problems in medical imaging and image processing.

items.title: Strategic Arbitrage in Electricity Markets: A Multi-Agent Policy Optimization Framework
items.summary: Grid-scale storage and load aggregators are growing quickly in wholesale electricity markets. If highly consolidated, these new participants may distort the competitive market equilibrium through strategic withholding behavior. Traditional market power mitigation techniques are ill-suited to arbitrage-based participants. We provide a multi-agent policy optimization model to study game-theoretic equilibria for real-time markets with consolidated storage and/or aggregators. The model is designed to facilitate natural first-order equilibrium-seeking update rules. We analyze the theoretical properties of different supply functions and their implications on the convergence of the gradient dynamics. Finally, we train equilibrium policies for a modified version of the IEEE RTS-GMLC benchmark across different levels of storage fleet consolidation, to demonstrate the potential of the framework as a tool to characterize and quantify strategic arbitrage.

items.title: Integrated Longitudinal and Lateral Control for High-Speed Platooning of Articulated Vehicles
items.summary: This paper presents an integrated control framework for high-speed platooning of articulated vehicles, combining advanced longitudinal and lateral control strategies to address the challenges of safe and efficient autonomous driving. A novel proof of string stability for the proposed longitudinal control algorithm, based on a PID framework, ensures robust inter-vehicle distance regulation even under dynamic operating conditions. Additionally, an arc-length-based longitudinal error formulation enhances the applicability of the control system for curved roads, making it realistic for diverse driving scenarios. For lateral control, significant improvements to the clothoid-based path tracking algorithm are introduced to mitigate oscillations and enhance stability at high speeds. These enhancements include a tangential criterion for oscillation reduction, trajectory segment classification for adaptive lookahead distance tuning, a dual-adaptive mechanism for regulating the rate of lookahead distance adjustments based on both cross-track error (CTE) and anticipated road curvature, and extensions for articulated vehicle dynamics. The proposed integrated control framework is validated through simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in maintaining stability, minimizing tracking errors, and ensuring robust performance in high-speed and challenging platooning scenarios.

items.title: Secure Agentic AI and Multimodal Intelligence in 6G Communication Systems
items.summary: Sixth-generation (6G) communication systems are expected to support immersive, intent-driven, and latency-critical services through tight integration of multimodal intelligence, edge computing, and autonomous network control. In this setting, agentic AI systems can reason over heterogeneous inputs, use tools and network functions, coordinate across distributed entities, and adapt to dynamic environments. These capabilities make agentic multimodal intelligence promising for 6G applications such as semantic communications, digital twins, and zero-touch network management, but they also introduce security and privacy risks that extend beyond conventional AI and network security models. Vulnerabilities can propagate across multimodal data pipelines, memory, tools, communication interfaces, and inter-agent coordination loops. We survey multimodal intelligence and agentic AI for 6G cross-layered communication systems from the perspectives of privacy and security. We present a 6G-oriented system view spanning perception, memory, tool use, and multi-agent orchestration; analyze threat models and attack surfaces across sensing, cognition, action, memory, and communication layers; organize existing attacks into a structured taxonomy; and review mitigation strategies including prompt and memory defenses, inter-agent trust mechanisms, secure orchestration, and privacy-preserving learning. We conclude by outlining open research directions for trustworthy multimodal multi-agent 6G systems.

items.title: Plug-in Estimation Method for Topology and Admittance Estimation in Electric Grids
items.summary: This paper proposes a scalable method for topology and admittance estimation in electric power grids. Our proposed plug-in estimation method incorporates precise phasor measurement unit data to estimate planned or unplanned grid topology and admittance parameter changes. Our plug-in estimation method decouples the problem into two stages: (i) constructing and averaging voltage coefficient matrices and current vectors from phasor data, and (ii) estimating admittance parameters via a least-squares regression approach with thresholding to recover the network topology. Rigidity matrix theory underpins the design of our plug-in estimation method --- to determine the data requirements (e.g., necessary and sufficient conditions) for accurate estimation of the grid topology and admittance parameters. By means of numerical simulations on the IEEE 13-node, 123-node, and European low voltage test feeders, we demonstrate the scalability of our plug-in estimation method and benchmark the computational time against a structured total least squares method. Our simulation results highlight the practicality of the proposed method for topology and admittance estimation in large-scale electric networks, including electric grids with partial topology information.

items.title: BRISC: A Dataset of Channel Measurements at 5 GHz With a Reflective Intelligent Surface
items.summary: We introduce the broadband reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) channel (BRISC) dataset. The dataset comprises measurements of channel state information (CSI) collected at 5.530 GHz using a 256-element RIS with binary states. In the measurement campaign, the transmitter and receiver are two software-defined radios (SDRs), phase-synchronized via an OctoClock, where the transmitter (receiver) is equipped with one (two) antenna(s). To manage complexity, the RIS elements are grouped into blocks of different sizes, where all elements within a block share the same state. CSIs have been captured for multiple a) transmitter positions (and fixed receiver location), b) RIS element-grouping granularity, and c) RIS configurations. Furthermore, we calibrated the parameters of state-of-the-art RIS channel models to fit the measured CSI. With approximately 10 000 configurations explored per transmitting position, BRISC serves as a robust benchmark in communication applications.

items.title: Computationally Transparent Power Flexibility Aggregation via Directional Support Evaluation
items.summary: The growing penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) creates new opportunities for improving resource adequacy, operational flexibility, and power-system reliability. However, efficiently characterizing the aggregate flexibility of heterogeneous DER portfolios remains challenging because of high dimensionality, diverse operating dynamics, and spatio-temporal coupling constraints. This paper proposes a computationally transparent framework that formulates aggregate flexibility characterization as a sequence of linear programming (LP)-based directional support evaluations. The framework accommodates heterogeneous DER technologies and configurable device-, feeder-, and portfolio-level constraints. The convex hull of the resulting boundary trajectories provides a feasible inner approximation of the coupled aggregate power flexibility region. Theoretical analysis establishes feasibility and non-overestimation guarantees and characterizes the computational dependence on portfolio size, scheduling horizon, and direction budget. In the small-scale case, the proposed method produces tighter projected regions than box, zonotope, and Chebyshev inner-ball benchmarks and matches a dense directional reference within numerical tolerance using 16--64 construction directions. Large-scale simulations with up to 2000 DERs demonstrate approximately linear empirical runtime scaling with the portfolio size and direction budget over the tested ranges. The results establish a scalable and theoretically grounded approach for aggregate DER flexibility characterization.

items.title: Memory-Augmented Online Test-Time Adaptation for EEG Motor Imagery via Perturbation Consistency and Confidence Calibration
items.summary: Recently, electroencephalography (EEG)-based brain--computer interfaces (BCIs) have gained traction as portable neural measurement systems. However, the practical deployment of these instruments is often hindered by nonstationarity and cross-subject distribution shifts, which lead to significant intersubject inconsistency. Existing adaptation methods remain impractical for real-time measurement scenarios, as they typically require offline access to source or aggregated target data. To address these challenges, this article proposes memory-augmented online test-time adaptation (OTTA) with perturbation consistency and confidence calibration (MOPC), a source-free framework designed to enhance the reliability of BCI instrumentation. MOPC enables the measurement system to update its decoding parameters on the fly during the inference stage, facilitating single-pass adaptation without accessing sensitive source data. We introduce random-mask perturbations to enforce prediction consistency against inherent EEG signal noise and acquisition artifacts. Furthermore, a confidence-calibrated reweighting loss is designed to integrate feature-space similarity, effectively mitigating unreliable pseudolabels and class imbalance during continuous signal acquisition. To ensure system stability and prevent the catastrophic forgetting of established neural patterns, a lightweight memory module is incorporated to regularize parameter updates within a tight latency budget. Evaluated on the BCI IV IIb and OpenBMI datasets, MOPC achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming prior methods by 2.22~\% and 3.67~\%, respectively, while keeping the per-trial adaptation latency to approximately 40--60 ms. This study provides a robust, recalibration-free solution for real-time EEG decoding, marking a significant advancement in the precision and usability of practical BCI measurement instruments.

items.title: On the Gradient Domination of the LQG Problem
items.summary: We consider solutions to the linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) regulator problem via policy gradient (PG) methods. Although PG methods have demonstrated strong theoretical guarantees in solving the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem, despite its nonconvex landscape, their theoretical understanding in the LQG setting remains limited. Notably, the LQG problem lacks gradient dominance in the classical parameterization, i.e., with a dynamic controller, which hinders global convergence guarantees. In this work, we study a PG method for the LQG problem by adopting an alternative parameterization of the set of stabilizing controllers and employing a lifting argument. We refer to this parameterization as a history representation of the control input as it is parameterized by past input and output data from the previous p time-steps. Under this parameterization, the infinite-history LQG optimization reduces to an equivalent static state-feedback LQR problem, allowing us to recover gradient dominance and smoothness. For finite history length p, we establish model-based and model-free convergence guarantees up to a geometrically decaying history-truncation error.

items.title: On the Adversarial Vulnerability of Neural Receivers with Unrolled LDPC Decoders
items.summary: Neural receivers for 5G New Radio (NR) match classical model-based receivers in link-level performance, but their robustness to adversarial perturbations at the receiver input remains underexplored. We show that standard gradient-based attacks applied end-to-end through an unrolled low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoder fail to significantly outperform a matched-power Gaussian perturbation. We identify the failure as gradient masking caused by tanh saturation in the boxplus operation of the belief-propagation (BP) check-node update, with a per-iteration gradient norm decay of more than four orders of magnitude across ten unrolled BP iterations. Based on this finding, we propose two structurally independent loss functions that restore attack efficacy. L_BP routes the gradient through the unsaturated early iterations via per-iteration supervision, while L_LLR is a margin loss on pre-decoder log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) whose gradient bypasses the LDPC decoder entirely. Both loss functions increase the block-error rate (BLER) by one to four orders of magnitude at matched perturbation power, with the results reproduced on both the Sionna NeuralReceiver and DeepRx. At low PSR, L_LLR-optimized perturbations achieve up to three orders of magnitude higher BLER on unseen channel realizations than LBP-optimized perturbations.

items.title: Dynamic Active Fleet Sizing of Heterogeneous UAV Relays for Post-Disaster Communication Networks
items.summary: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems are increasingly used to provide temporary connectivity when ground communication infrastructure is damaged by disasters such as hurricanes and wildfires. However, the amount of aerial support required changes as ground networks recover and communication demand evolves. We focus on dynamically adjusting the number and allocation of actively deployed UAVs within a fixed available fleet. We develop a model predictive control (MPC) framework for dynamic fleet sizing of heterogeneous UAV relays during post-disaster communication recovery. The framework accounts for communication demand, ground network recovery, heterogeneous UAV operation, UAV energy availability, and backhaul capacity, which limits how much relayed traffic can be transmitted to the external communication network. The resulting formulation is a convex quadratic program that supports efficient online fleet sizing and deployment decisions. We evaluate the framework using seven historical disaster recovery case studies based on Federal Communications Commission reports, together with four backhaul scenarios and sensitivity analyses. Results show that required active UAV fleet size varies considerably throughout recovery, while backhaul capacity and fleet composition affect communication performance, highlighting the value of adapting active fleet size over time.

items.title: Bayesian Ambiguity Contraction-based Adaptive Robust Markov Decision Processes for Adversarial Surveillance Missions
items.summary: Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCAs) are envisioned to enable autonomous Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) missions in contested environments, where adversaries may act strategically to deceive or evade detection. These missions pose challenges due to model uncertainty and the need for safe, real-time decision-making. Robust Markov Decision Processes (RMDPs) provide worst-case guarantees but are limited by static ambiguity sets that capture initial uncertainty without adapting to new observations. This paper presents an adaptive RMDP framework tailored to ISR missions with CCAs. We introduce a mission-specific formulation in which the CCA alternates between movement and sensing states. Adversarial uncertainty is represented by finite threat prototypes defining observation, exposure, and state-action transition models. Our approach incrementally refines policies by eliminating inconsistent threat models, allowing the CCA to move from worst-case protection toward more efficient mission policies while maintaining robustness. We establish fixed point stability, agreement with nominal planning as credible sets identify the true node-specific threat prototypes, and a conservative expected value guarantee while those prototypes remain credible. Experiments under Gaussian and non-Gaussian threat models across diverse network topologies show higher mission rewards and fewer exposure events compared to nominal and static robust planners.

items.title: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Label-Efficient Gastric Cancer Detection and Intra-Tumour Progression Analysis
items.summary: Gastric Cancer is among the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The complexity and variability of histopathological images pose significant challenges for both pathologists and computer-based diagnostics, creating a growing need for machine learning approaches capable of capturing meaningful representations from limited labelled data. Selfsupervised Contrastive Learning (CL) has demonstrated promising results in natural image analysis; however, its application to gastric cancer histopathology remains underexplored. This paper proposes an integrated CL framework built on a ResNet50 encoder trained under the NT-Xent objective, without reliance on ImageNet pre-training, to learn discriminative and staining-invariant representations from H&E-stained tissue patches. The learned embeddings are transferred to a supervised downstream classifier for binary tumour/normal (TUM/NOR) detection, achieving a test accuracy of 83.13%, an AUC-ROC of 0.9087, and an Average Precision of 0.9063 - competitive with recent supervised and weakly-supervised approaches on comparable histopathology benchmarks. Beyond binary diagnosis, the framework applies K-Means clustering to tumour embeddings to identify four geometrically separable pseudo-stage clusters, confirmed by a Random Forest classifier achieving 97% accuracy and a mean Dice coefficient of 0.97, demonstrating the capacity of CL representations to encode progression-relevant morphological variation without stage-level annotations. Grad-CAM explainability is integrated throughout to ensure model transparency. The complete system is deployed via a Streamlit clinical interface. Compared to recent state-of-the-art methods the proposed framework operates with substantially fewer labelled samples while additionally providing unsupervised progression stratification and interpretable outputs, addressing a gap not covered by existing approaches.

items.title: Real-Time Disturbance-Aware Koopman Model Predictive Control for Quadrotors in Spatially Varying Winds
items.summary: Reliable quadrotor flight in disturbed environments requires predictive models that remain accurate as unmodeled aerodynamic effects change during deployment. We introduce a disturbance-aware Koopman Control Family (DA-KCF) framework that preserves an offline-identified nominal model while learning only a disturbance-induced correction online. A reference-dependent KCF is first learned from simulation data and calibrated using limited hardware data. During deployment, the nominal KCF remains fixed while a lightweight residual ensemble learns a low-dimensional disturbance correction from causal state-command-state transitions. The Adaptive DA-KCF model is incorporated into MPC, where disturbance corrections are evaluated along the prediction horizon to optimize position and yaw references sent to the onboard stabilizing controller. Hardware experiments on a nano-quadrotor under uniform wind and a spatially varying wake demonstrate that online adaptation improves multi-step prediction and trajectory tracking as disturbance-induced model mismatch increases, while satisfying real-time control requirements.

items.title: SciFusion: Physics-Guided Compositional Diffusion for Multimodal 3D Scientific Image Generation
items.summary: Existing 3D generative approaches are typically developed for individual imaging modalities, requiring substantial modality-specific data and limiting their ability to exploit shared structure across scientific imaging domains. We present SciFusion, a multimodal framework for unified 3D scientific image generation built on a latent diffusion backbone, with two key contributions. First, we introduce a compositional conditioning scheme that factorizes each modality into domain, object, and contrast representations. Sharing these factors across related modalities enables knowledge transfer across heterogeneous imaging domains and allows the factors to be recombined at inference time to synthesize unseen domain-object-contrast compositions in a zero-shot manner. Second, we incorporate domain-specific physics-informed objectives: Fourier spectral consistency for MRI, Radon projection consistency for CT, and multislice diffraction consistency for electron microscopy, to encourage generated samples to respect modality-dependent image formation processes. Extensive experiments across 15 medical and scientific imaging modalities demonstrate that SciFusion improves generation fidelity and cross-domain generalization over modality-specific and flattened multimodal conditioning strategies, while enabling zero-shot synthesis of unseen compositions without training on those target compositions. These results demonstrate that compositional, physics-guided conditioning provides a scalable framework for unified 3D scientific image generation, particularly for emerging modalities where large-scale training data are difficult to obtain.

items.title: Implementation of Dynamic Microsegmentation for a Multi-Robot Network
items.summary: This report describes a laboratory instantiation of a dynamic microsegmentation function for an Internet-of-Things network, specifically a multi-robot network, using a commercial software-defined microsegmentation tool. Fine-grained dynamic segmentation policies are defined, where segments are adapted based on asset functional and health tags. Automated implementation of the dynamic policies in software is also undertaken. The microsegmentation solution is shown to automatically isolate an indicated threat in real time, while maintaining unaffected operations. The demonstration indicates that microsegmentation can be implemented in IoT networks, in a way that allows for robust operation in the face of threats and disruptions.

items.title: Machine Learning-Enabled Wireless Power Transfer: A Task-Oriented Review of Structural Optimization, State and Parameter Estimation, and Adaptive Control
items.summary: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems must maintain efficient and safe energy delivery under variations in geometry, coupling, load, alignment, and operating conditions. Machine-learning methods are increasingly applied to accelerate structural design, estimate operating parameters and states, and support adaptive control and scheduling. This review develops a task-oriented framework organized around three interconnected domains: structural design and optimization, parameter and state estimation, and control and optimization. Supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and hybrid or physics-informed methods are compared in terms of data requirements, dependence on physical models, information sources, computational requirements, accuracy, online response, application scope, and optimization objectives. Supervised learning provides rapid surrogate modeling, regression, and classification when representative labeled data are available. Reinforcement learning addresses sequential control and scheduling but introduces challenges in reward design, safe exploration, and simulation-to-reality transfer. Hybrid methods integrate physical knowledge with data-driven models to improve data efficiency and physical consistency. The principal barriers to engineering deployment include limited and biased datasets, weak out-of-distribution generalization, insufficient physical consistency, unsafe online adaptation, embedded-resource constraints, and the absence of standardized benchmarks. Future research should prioritize uncertainty-aware and physics-informed learning, safe simulation-to-reality transfer, lightweight edge deployment, distributed coordination, reproducible evaluation, and digital-twin-assisted development.

items.title: Why the Swing Parameters Are Sloppy
items.summary: Evangelou, Stanković, Kevrekidis and Transtrum compared analytic and data-driven assessments of parameter identifiability for the infinite-bus synchronous generator. Fisher information with the manifold boundary approximation method (MBAM), and output diffusion maps with geometric harmonics, report the same six identifiable parameters on the late window $t \in [3, 5]\text{ s}$, and both place the inertia $H$ and the damping $D$ among the unidentifiable ones. We explain this result from the geometry of the dynamics rather than from that of the parameter-to-data map. The rotor swing is a fast fibre that has collapsed onto a two-dimensional normally attracting invariant manifold (NAIM) of the transient fluxes before the window opens. The zeroth-order NAIM is exactly independent of $H$, $D$, $T_{d0}''$ and $T_{q0}''$, four of the five MBAM limits. We prove, under stated smoothness and rank conditions, that each of the four limits is a boundary of the model manifold at a distance equal, to first order in the parameter, to its current profiled speed. The same analysis predicts how identifiability changes with the experiment: neither a larger initial speed deviation nor a load change restores $H$ or $D$ in the late window, whereas the early window $[0, 2]\text{ s}$ makes $H$ the best-determined parameter. Evaluated in a physical metric fixed by synchrophasor accuracy limits, the late window identifies five parameters rather than six and the early window nine. The spiked-covariance structure of the linearised trajectory map explains why the principal components of whitened, sampled trajectories reproduce the prior-scaled Fisher spectrum, and regression on those components attains the Fisher-predicted recovery error in 113 of 114 parameter--scenario pairs.

items.title: Fast Cascaded Recursive Filtering via a Block-Matrix Reformulation
items.summary: Recursive (IIR) filters realized as cascaded second-order sections (biquads) offer both design generality and robustness against coefficient quantization. However, their inherent sample-to-sample feedback dependency poses a fundamental obstacle to parallel computation. This paper reformulates the biquad difference equation as a banded block-Toeplitz linear system. It relies on a stride-$N$ permutation that maps a group of $NL$ samples into a block-tridiagonal structure whose entries are scalar multiples of identity and shift matrices. Within this framework, two data-parallel algorithms are developed which, to the best of our knowledge, are the fastest, single-core IIR filter implementations reported to date. A partial LU (PH) factorization preserves the sparse block structure and a cyclic reduction reduces the sequential dependency depth from $\mathcal{O}(N)$ to $\mathcal{O}(\log_2 N)$. For a cascade of $K$ biquads, the intermediate permutations between successive sections cancel exactly, so that only a single pair of permutations is required for the entire cascade. Exact block-level operation counts are derived for every algorithmic stage and validated against cycle-accurate measurements on three micro-architectures supporting AVX2 SIMD instructions. Experimental results for a 16th-order system show that the proposed multi-block algorithms reduce clock cycles per sample by up to $10\times$ compared to scalar filtering, with both algorithms scaling favorably on newer architectures. On a single Meteor Lake core, cyclic reduction achieves approximately 616 MS/s---four times the throughput of Intel's vendor-tuned IPP library.

items.title: Region of Attraction Estimation for Linear Quadratic Regulator, Linear and Robust Model Predictive Control on a Two-Wheeled Inverted Pendulum
items.summary: Nonlinear underactuated systems such as two-wheeled inverted pendulums (TWIPs) exhibit a limited region of attraction (RoA), which defines the set of initial conditions from which the closed-loop system converges to the equilibrium. The RoA of nonlinear and constrained systems is generally nonconvex and analytically intractable, requiring numerical or approximate estimation methods. This work investigates the estimation of the RoA for a TWIP stabilized under three model-based control strategies: saturated linear quadratic regulator (LQR), linear model predictive control (MPC), and constraint tightening MPC (CTMPC). We first derive a Lyapunov-based invariant set that provides a certified inner approximation of the RoA. Since this analytical bound is highly conservative, a Monte Carlo-based estimation procedure is then employed to obtain a more representative approximation of the RoA, capturing how the controllers behave beyond the analytically guaranteed region. The proposed methodology combines analytical guarantees with data-driven estimation, providing both a formally certified inner bound and an empirical characterization of the RoA, offering a practical way to evaluate controller performance without relying solely on conservative analytical bounds or purely empirical simulation.

items.title: NLOS-Aware TDOA-Based UAV Localization: Cramér-Rao Bounds, Measurement Modeling, and Experimental Validation
items.summary: Passive time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) localization is well suited for tracking non-cooperative unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) that do not report their positions. However, its accuracy degrades under the mixed line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) propagation that is typical of low-altitude flight. In this paper, we develop NLOS-aware Cramér--Rao lower bounds (CRLBs) and an empirically calibrated measurement model for TDOA-based UAV localization, and we evaluate both with measurements from five UAV flights on the Aerial Experimentation and Research Platform for Advanced Wireless (AERPAW). The analysis yields an identifiability condition that relates the number of sensors to the number of NLOS links, together with a bias-induced error floor that a wider bandwidth cannot remove. The model parameters are estimated by matching simulated and measured error distributions. Experimental results show that the error depends most strongly on the number of sensors in LOS, while a higher altitude and a wider bandwidth lower the median error. Relocating a sensor that is always in NLOS into the open flight area can lower the median horizontal bound by two orders of magnitude if the relocated sensor is in LOS. The fitted model reproduces the median errors of the 2.5 MHz and 5 MHz flights but underestimates the heaviest error tails. Finally, rejecting outlier fixes lowers the error far more than Kalman or particle filtering, because the remaining error is dominated by bias.

items.title: Dual Effect and Certainty Equivalence Revisited for a Linear-Gaussian Dual Control Problem
items.summary: This paper revisits the relation between dual effect and certainty equivalence (CE) through a scalar linear-Gaussian model. In dual control, the current input affects not only the immediate cost but also the information available for future decisions, and hence the future cost. Dynamic programming (DP) provides a natural framework for formulating dual control problems. At each step of the Bellman recursion, an optimal input minimizes the sum of the stage cost and the expected cost-to-go. We restrict attention to stage costs minimized by the CE input. However, CE may not minimize the Bellman objective because of the input-dependent expected cost-to-go. Classical no-dualeffect (NDE) conditions guarantee CE optimality in certain problem classes by requiring the conditional distribution of the estimation error to be independent of past controls. In the present model, we observe that CE can remain optimal at the level of a single Bellman recursion even when the classical NDE conditions fail, provided that the expected cost-to-go is independent of the current input. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a notion of NDE formulated directly at the level of the Bellman objective, which we call Bellman-side NDE. Under some mild regularity conditions, we show that Bellman-side NDE can be characterized by a heat equation. This characterization identifies the class of Bellman-side NDE functions, and further yields a decomposition of a generic cost-to-go function into a Bellman-side NDE component and a dual-effect component.

items.title: Enhancing IoT Network Reliability through Antenna Diversity in Real-World Scenarios
items.summary: Antenna diversity in Internet of Things (IoT) devices is explored to address challenges associated with fixed device orientation and interference from nearby metallic objects, which can degrade wireless network performance. Integrating multiple antennas with different polarizations can significantly enhance signal quality and network reliability. Experiments demonstrated significant improvements in link quality, with gains exceeding 30 dB in received signal strength for specific scenarios. Already the addition of a second PCB-based antenna alone, resulted in a 17 dB improvement. These findings suggest that the added complexity in hardware and software to incorporate antenna diversity could well be justified by the resulting enhancements in network stability for real-world applications.

items.title: Seeking Cost--Effective Incentive for Merchant MTDC Investment in an AC Grid: A Parametric MISOCP Model to VSC Siting and Sizing
items.summary: Deploying voltage source converter (VSC)-based multi-terminal DC (MTDC) networks in existing AC grids offers a promising solution for alleviating transmission congestion, enhancing power-transfer capability, and improving operational economy. However, constructing an MTDC network requires participation from merchant investors. Therefore, the transmission system operator (TSO) responsible for the AC grid must provide an adequate economic incentive that enables merchant investors not only to recover the MTDC investment cost but also to earn a reasonable return commensurate with their risk and expectations. An insufficient incentive may fail to attract merchant investment, whereas an excessive incentive may unnecessarily reduce the economic benefits retained by the TSO. Determining an appropriate incentive that balances these competing interests therefore becomes a critical issue. To address this issue, this paper formulates a sharing-rate-parameterized mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) model that jointly optimizes VSC siting and sizing while coordinating AC/DC system operation. A straightforward search procedure is then employed to identify the benefit-sharing rate that meets the investor's expectations while preserving sufficient benefits for the TSO. Case studies demonstrate the operating-cost benefits of MTDC integration and validate the proposed search strategy for seeking such a benefit-sharing rate.

items.title: Multiuser Channel Estimation in FIM Systems: A Structured Block Term Decomposition Approach
items.summary: Flexible intelligent metasurfaces (FIMs) create geometry-dependent array responses that provide spatial diversity but complicate multiuser channel estimation. This paper studies uplink estimation using pilot observations collected under multiple prescribed and calibrated morphing configurations. Each user contributes a matrix--vector block that couples its diagonal reference-array response with its morphing-dependent phases, while its third-mode vector is the known pilot scaled by the complex channel gain. We develop a pilot-constrained structured block term decomposition (BTD) estimator whose alternating least-squares updates exploit both the known pilot directions and the diagonal spatial factors. The undeformed configuration sets the columnwise scaling convention, and a unit first-entry normalization assigns the remaining block scale to the channel gain. Matching the recovered factors to the calibrated spatial--morphing manifold then yields the physical angles and configuration-dependent channels. We characterize the rank conditions for unique conditional least-squares updates, distinguish these conditions from global factor and physical-angle identifiability, and summarize the training, coherence-time, and computational requirements. Simulations show accurate two-dimensional angle and channel recovery in the tested settings, equal total pilot-symbol overhead in rigid-panel comparisons, improved steering-vector estimates as morphing diversity increases, and degradation as user loading or pilot correlation increases.

items.title: Constrained Koopman Control Parametrization: Convex Controller Synthesis for Tracking under Input Constraints
items.summary: Koopman operator theory represents nonlinear systems with linear and bilinear terms in the state and input observables, greatly simplifying control design. However, incorporating input constraints into Koopman-based controller synthesis remains challenging, limiting their applicability to constrained control tasks such as tracking. This paper develops a constrained Koopman Control Parametrization (cKoCoP) framework for synthesizing state-feedback controllers that satisfy prescribed input constraints with Lyapunov-certified stability of the identified lifted closed loop. The cKoCoP offers nonlinear state-feedback via linear-in-observables feedback, enabling linear controller design. The proposed controller is obtained through convex optimization: we incorporate ellipsoidal or polytopic input constraints with the S-procedure or Farkas-lemma-based conditions. We also introduce a Control Lyapunov Function (CLF) for trajectory tracking which incorporates input constraints. The approach is validated on two canonical nonlinear systems, a double pendulum and a unicycle, demonstrating data-driven tracking while respecting input constraints. Experiments validate the method's robustness to measurement noise, and runtime improvements over Koopman Model Predictive Control (KMPC) baselines. The results demonstrate that cKoCoP achieves competitive tracking performance with substantially reduced online computational cost, supporting its potential for real-time constrained tracking applications.

items.title: A Plantwide Simulation Library for Control-Oriented Design: Analytical and Data-driven Use Cases
items.summary: Control structures and operability indices for plantwide processes are developed and compared on fixed simulated flowsheets, and the configuration of a study is rarely reported in a form that another group can reproduce. In this contribution, plantbench, a library of plantwide process simulations in which the design, the controller tuning and the instrumentation of a plant are declared as hashed plain-data configurations, is presented. On a heat-integrated reactor--separator--recycle plant with an open-loop unstable reactor, a heuristic plantwide control design prices four heat-exchanger networks (HENs) by the least damping ratio of the linearized closed loop, and 2016 closed-loop runs over networks, tuning, analyzer deadtime and upsets test that ranking. Results show that the damping ratio orders the networks as the runs do with the network that recovers the most heat reaching 0.013 against 0.157 for the selected one and cycling under a throughput increase, but that it is a weak detector of which operation will oscillate. At the recall of a random forest on the first 100 min after an upset, 60 of 82 limit cycles, a damping-ratio threshold raises 173 false alarms against 5. The integral time of the temperature loop, to which the damping ratio is nearly insensitive, decides in part whether the plant holds an operating point.

items.title: Proposals and challenges for zero-knowledge verification of frontier AI training
items.summary: Proposals for Frontier AI rules often use cumulative training compute as the main criterion for identifying high-impact models. Recent governance analyses call zero-knowledge proofs promising but currently impractical at frontier scale [26, 4]. We argue this barrier reflects the current paradigm, not a fundamental limit. Our frontier dense-pre-training design combines a pre-committed specification, inter-node network observations, and live Merkle commitments to intermediate computation. Our reference zero-knowledge virtual machine (zkVM) provides a succinct proof layer with native BF16/FP32 precompiles. We qualitatively compare zkVMs, custom circuits, and direct interactive audits by transferability, soundness, and cost. Public randomness beacons are a separate audit-selection choice. At challenged positions, proofs check the committed computation against declared BF16/FP32 semantics bit-for-bit. A private training specification targets model-architecture confidentiality. Genesis proofs cover initialisation; then, in-training step proofs verify selected steps across the run. Ex-ante attestations enforce policy-relevant claims as running invariants on every proved step. Together they create a governance-auditable training record. Detection-probability formulas quantify sampling guarantees from the sampling budget and the share of computation altered. We give numerical examples and explain what sampling does not cover. We note, however, that weight smuggling could reuse or merge weights trained elsewhere without charging that work to the current run. We then argue that regimes with global training budgets are more robust than regimes with per-run FLOP caps. This advantage depends on counting all contributing training. We catalogue remaining research and engineering problems for external contributors.

items.title: Physics-Informed Koopman Learning for Data-Efficient System Identification of Automated Vehicle Dynamics
items.summary: Understanding how a particular automated vehicle reacts to nearby traffic can improve motion prediction, control development, traffic simulation, and safety evaluation. However, commercial automated driving systems are proprietary, and single encounters may provide only a few seconds of noisy data. Standard physical models are interpretable but inflexible, whereas neural models are often data-hungry. We propose a physics-informed Koopman framework that combines a calibrated car-following law with a correction learned from the observations. A weak-form estimator learns this correction from velocity measurements integrated over time, avoiding noise-sensitive numerical differentiation. The resulting continuous-time model predicts the follower's response and provides interpretable measures of driving behavior. Experiments on OpenACC and CATS-CF evaluate 5-, 7-, and 11-second histories. Averaged over these histories, the constant-time-headway branch reduces speed prediction error by 16.0% and 15.4% on OpenACC and CATS-CF, respectively, relative to the best neural baselines. The PI-Koopman branches achieve the lowest mean speed and gap errors among the physical and neural comparators. Weak-form estimation reduces acceleration-field reconstruction error by 74.5% in noisy known-law simulations and noise-induced field perturbation by 91.6% in paired real-vehicle measurements. The same PI-Koopman system identification supports following-mode recognition with an approximately eleven-fold difference in median residual variance between human drivers and automated vehicles, and a single residual threshold achieves 85.4% balanced accuracy. The branch informed by the intelligent driver model takes a median 17 to 26 ms for identification and forecasting on the tested central processing units, supporting frequent target adaptation.

items.title: A Learned Musical-Time Coordinate for Piano Audio-to-Score Transcription
items.summary: End-to-end piano audio-to-score (A2S) transcription is the task of reconstructing a notated score from an audio recording in a single system. Existing A2S approaches usually rely on pre-segmented excerpts, and few handle whole pieces without external segmentation. This raises the question of whether a musical-time coordinate can guide score transcription while also helping the system segment whole pieces. Previous work on jazz saxophone A2S uses an external beat tracker to obtain such a coordinate for score prediction. We introduce downbeat phase, a musical-time coordinate learned jointly with score transcription that represents each audio frame's relative position within a notated bar. With this coordinate, our system can not only condition its score decoder on downbeat phase but also self-segment at bar boundaries and stitch the segments into a whole piece. Evaluation suggests that the coordinate improves metrical structure and supports whole-piece transcription with comparable notation quality.

items.title: Initialization-Free LEO Doppler Positioning via Semidefinite Relaxation: A Cold-Start Approach
items.summary: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite Doppler measurements offer an alternative source of positioning information for Internet of Things devices when Global Navigation Satellite System signals are unavailable. Conventional local optimisation methods depend on an accurate initial position and can fail during a complete cold start. We propose an initialization-free LEO Doppler positioning framework based on semidefinite relaxation. The method reformulates the nonlinear positioning problem into a semidefinite programme to obtain a receiver position estimate without prior location knowledge. We analyse relaxation tightness under noiseless conditions and derive sufficient noise bounds under parameter disturbances. Simulations and field experiments using opportunistic Iridium-NEXT signals evaluate initialization sensitivity, positioning accuracy and computational cost. In the field experiment, the proposed method achieves a three-dimensional positioning error of 140 m without an initial position, whereas local solvers converge to poor solutions under large initial offsets. Using the semidefinite estimate to initialise Gauss-Newton or Dog-Leg reduces the positioning error to 130 m. The framework provides a cold-start initialization stage for subsequent local refinement in opportunistic LEO positioning. The implementation and datasets are publicly available to support reproducibility and further research.

items.title: Latency-Neutral Passive Cyber Monitoring for Grid-Edge Operational Technology Networks
items.summary: Deterministic industrial networks often present an operational trade-off between maintaining microsecond timing of primary control loops and capturing security telemetry. This work investigates the engineering feasibility of the Operational Technology Supervisor (OTSV), a three-tier passive monitoring framework designed to resolve this visibility challenge within timing-sensitive grid-edge infrastructure. By utilizing a Layer-3-unconfigured passive ingestion mode on bare-metal hardware via a physical switched port analyzer (SPAN) loop, the deep packet inspection engine is isolated from the production network, implementing a software-enforced unidirectional export policy. Performance validation conducted over a continuous audit comprising 32,927 active-monitoring round-trip time (RTT) samples yielded stable latency distributions across a laboratory power-monitoring loop running Modbus TCP and IEC 61850 MMS protocols. The measured latency delta between the unmonitored baseline and the active monitoring state was less than 0.12 milliseconds, supporting the feasibility of continuous high-fidelity security observation alongside stringent grid-edge metering timing bounds without measurably degrading the monitored reporting path.

items.title: Worst-Case Finite-Horizon Analysis of Perturbed LQR via Performance Estimation Problem
items.summary: We propose an exact formulation to quantify the finite-horizon robustness of a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) subject to norm-bounded Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) parametric uncertainties, using the Performance Estimation Problem (PEP) framework. Originally developed for optimization, this method allows us to reformulate the worst-case performance search as a rank-constrained Semidefinite Program (SDP). By applying operator interpolation, this formulation retains the sequence variables, allowing the worst-case to be explicitly reconstructed when a rank-one solution is found. This approach also opens new possibilities for the finite-horizon certification of broader system classes, such as data-driven models or nonlinear components. Using this framework, we observe that finite-horizon LTI perturbations do not simply follow asymptotic strategies. Instead, they align slowly decaying invariant manifolds with specific initial conditions to drive transient growth, causing a bifurcation in the worst-case behavior as the horizon length changes. Finally, we show numerically that our performance bounds sit between the upper bounds of Integral Quadratic Constraint (IQC) relaxations and a lower bound derived from a pseudospectral heuristic.

items.title: Pilot Decontamination via Data-aided Channel Tracking in Cell-free Massive MIMO
items.summary: As cell-free massive MIMO emerges as a promising technology for future wireless networks, robust channel estimation becomes increasingly important. Channel estimation relies on pilot transmissions, and with increasing number of users, pilot reuse inevitably introduces contamination that degrades channel estimation and symbol detection. This limitation is compounded by rapidly evolving channels, which render the estimates obsolete over time. To address both the problems, viz. pilot contamination and channel aging without additional pilot overhead, we propose a Kalman filter-based data-aided channel tracking strategy. By leveraging the symbol estimates as virtual pilots, the proposed approach successively refines the channel estimates over time. Unlike the conventional Kalman filter model, here, the observation model depends on symbol estimates, introducing symbol uncertainty that gets coupled with channel uncertainty. This requires a careful calculation of the innovation covariance matrices. Additionally, we discuss a stochastic-gradient-descent based tracking approach with low computational complexity. Extensive simulations are used to demonstrate that successive refinement progressively decontaminates the channel estimate, achieving lower channel estimation error and improved spectral efficiency.

items.title: Recovering Plausible Transmission Outage Scenarios
items.summary: Expansion planning for extreme weather needs outage scenarios that specify which transmission branches fail. However, public outage records often only report customers without power by county, making it unclear how to exploit this information to create outage scenarios. We propose a method to recover sets of outaged branches that most closely match regional load shed data. This gives us sets of plausible outages for a given hazard event. We formulate a bilevel problem with a load shedding DC optimal power flow in the lower level. We relax the binary branch states to differentiate the lower level problem, replace it with its sensitivity matrix, and use gradient descent to update the upper level. We treat the relaxed branch states as probabilities and perform randomized rounding to restore integrality. On three test systems with synthetic outages, the recovered sets reduce the load shed error to $0.02-4.5\%$. On the California Test System with storm data from December 2025, the error falls to $23\%$. These scenarios give expansion planning a reliable source of outage data tied to observed hazards.

items.title: The Cheap Hours Don't Stay Cheap: Price-Chasing Data Centers Reshape Grids and Markets
items.summary: Data centers unsettle the paradigm of location-bound electricity demand: computing workloads can migrate across sites and hours, whereas facilities and grid connections remain fixed. This mobility reduces electricity costs but reshapes the spatiotemporal structure of nodal prices. A model-driven framework couples US wholesale market signals with optimal fleet scheduling, showing how their interaction alters prices and other participants' responses. Greater flexibility enlarges savings yet can erode network benefits: in a Texas study, temporal shifting and cross-site allocation each relieve congestion, but their combination leaves total congestion nearly unchanged. At continental scale, computing demand gravitating toward cheaper electricity narrows price differences and compresses the low-price hours storage arbitrage relies on, threatening storage investment recovery. Cost-minimizing scheduling may therefore undermine grid-supporting resources. Comparing job-level and aggregate fleet representations reveals a trade-off between operational visibility and information disclosure, informing requirements and incentives that could turn workload mobility into a lever for system-wide efficiency.

items.title: NeuroCodec: EEG-Guided Latent-Domain Generative Model for High-Fidelity Target Speaker Extraction
items.summary: Driven by recent advancements in hearing assistive devices, target speaker extraction (TSE) in multi-talker environments has drawn significant attention. To address this, hearing technologies identify attention using neural signals recorded via electroencephalography (EEG) to guide TSE, enabling neuro-steered auditory attention decoding. However, most existing techniques rely on time-frequency masking, which suffers from low fidelity in spectro-temporally overlapping regions and is often restricted to narrowband audio. In contrast, we introduce NeuroCodec, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first generative EEG-guided TSE framework operating in the latent space of a neural audio codec. Specifically, NeuroCodec models spatial EEG dependencies via graph convolutions and fuses cross-modal EEG and speech representations through attention mechanisms and Mamba-based temporal modeling. We further introduce a six-phase training curriculum that progressively incorporates latent reconstruction, multi-scale spectral, and adversarial objectives to ensure stable, high-fidelity speech generation. Experiments on the public Cocktail Party and KUL datasets show NeuroCodec outperforms baselines, across several perceptual metrics. A listening experiment with 20 participants validated that NeuroCodec offers greater perceptual accuracy, achieving a mean score of 82.24 compared with 49.63 for M3ANet. Additionally, the proposed method is seen to enable 44.1 kHz reconstruction with spectral content extending up to 20 kHz, further supporting the perceptual results. Finally, we extend NeuroCodec with a causal streaming formulation suited for real-time processing, providing a basis for hearing assistive devices.

items.title: Geometry-Conditioned Target Speaker Extraction based on spatial features incorporating acoustic propagation principles
items.summary: Recently, spatially selective non-linear filter (SSF) was proposed for target speaker extraction, utilizing the direction-of-arrival (DOA) of the target speaker as a spatial cue. To overcome its dependency on a fixed microphone array geometry, geometry-conditioned SSF (GCSSF) was proposed, which maps the target DOA and the microphone positions into abstract high-dimensional embeddings using positional encoding. As an alternative to these high-dimensional embeddings, in this paper we propose utilizing two spatial features incorporating acoustic propagation principles for geometry conditioning: 1) the steering vector of the target speaker, which captures inter-microphone phase differences, and 2) a spatial mask based on GCC-PHAT, which quantifies presence of the target speaker per time-frequency bin. These features are used as input to a geometry-conditioning encoder and integrated via a FiLM layer into the GCSSF system. Experimental results on circular and random arrays demonstrate that conditioning with spatial features improves target extraction performance compared to abstract high-dimensional embeddings, maintaining a clear performance advantage across a wide range of target DOA errors.

items.title: Information-Induced Conservatism Frontier of Distributed Stability Certificates
items.summary: Conservatism in distributed stability certification is often treated as a limitation of the certificate itself, motivating richer Lyapunov functions, tighter relaxations, or stronger optimization. But a more fundamental limitation may arise from the reporting interface: once information is compressed, physically different systems can become indistinguishable. If stable and unstable systems produce the same report, no sound method can separate them. This paper asks where this information limit lies and how much additional information is needed to move it. We model information as an information structure that partitions admissible systems into information fibers. The strongest sound certificate for a fiber is determined by its smallest stability margin, yielding a method-independent benchmark. This separates total conservatism into information-induced and method-induced parts and characterizes information order, task sufficiency, and the stability value of additional information. Three network-node studies show that network-spectrum, scalar/eigenvalue-only passivity, and independent-local reports respectively lose network--node alignment, local directional alignment, and cross-node relation. They show that critical missing information is often relational rather than dimensional. We then move from diagnosis to information design. An information-conservatism frontier gives the smallest irreducible conservatism achievable under a prescribed budget, while its inverse gives the minimum information required for a target conservatism. A witness-pair characterization turns this into a weighted covering problem. Besides, a local sensitivity law provides a computable approximation and identifies valuable unresolved quantities. The framework indicates whether conservatism should be reduced by improving the certificate or enriching the information.

items.title: Delay-Doppler Domain Aided OFDM (DD-a-OFDM): Pulsone Pilot and Cross-Domain Iterative Receiver Design
items.summary: In high-mobility channels, the widely adopted orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation waveform suffers from significant performance degradation due to channel variation and severe inter-carrier interference. Although delay-Doppler (DD) domain multicarrier (DDMC) modulation enjoys a higher channel estimation (CE) accuracy via exploiting the inherent DD-domain channel stability, sparsity, and separability, its high detection complexity limits its practical deployment, making OFDM still a promising waveform candidate for the sixth-generation (6G) cellular networks. To simultaneously harness the complementary strengths of DDMC and OFDM and mitigate their respective limitations, this paper proposes a DD-domain aided OFDM (DD-a-OFDM) framework, including a pulsone pilot (PP) design and a cross-domain iterative receiver design, to enhance the CE and detection performance of OFDM in high-mobility channels. Specifically, a pulsone pilot sequence is periodically inserted before the cyclic prefix (CP) for each OFDM symbol in the time-domain, which is equivalent to a single DD-domain pilot impulse and enables accurate DD-domain CE. Then, we propose a cross-domain iterative receiver in which the time-frequency (TF) domain detection results are transformed into the DD-domain for interference cancellation and CE; in turn, the DD-domain estimated channel is transformed into the TF-domain for channel reconstruction and symbol detection. The proposed cross-domain iterative receiver achieves a higher CE accuracy and detection performance with a much lower pilot overhead, compared to the conventional OFDM system. Simulation results validate the fast convergence and superior performance of the proposed DD-a-OFDM scheme and demonstrate that it maintains a robust CE and detection performance even in high-mobility channels.

items.title: Depth through recurrence: Looped transformers for flow-matching TTS
items.summary: We study how to organize Transformer depth through recurrence in flow-matching text-to-speech, varying the amount, order, and placement of weight reuse. Seven layouts perform 18 block calls per network evaluation under a common training objective and sampler. On Seed-TTS and LibriSpeech-PC, SEQUENCE applies each of nine blocks twice consecutively, retaining competitive intelligibility, speaker similarity, and predicted speech quality at 32 sampling steps with 47.1% fewer parameters than the unshared baseline. Cycling six blocks three times further reduces model size but raises 32-step word error rates relative to cycling nine blocks twice. At matched parameter counts and executed depth, reuse order and sharing position produce different quality trade-offs. These comparisons depend on sampling budget: Prefix and Suffix have similar 32-step word error rates, but Suffix is worse by 3.44 and 5.97 percentage points at four steps on the two datasets, respectively. Only Middle ranks first or second in mean word error rate at 32 and four steps on both datasets. These results show that the organization of recurrent computation affects synthesis quality, and that reuse layouts should be selected for both the sampling budget and the quality dimensions of interest.

items.title: S-PASS: Star-Topology Pinching-Antenna Systems with Pipelined Antenna Pre-Positioning
items.summary: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) flexibly reconfigure the wireless channel by positioning dielectric antennas along a waveguide near each user. Releasing and re-attaching an antenna, however, is a mechanical operation orders of magnitude slower than electronic switching, wasting much transmission time. Existing designs generally assume instant reconfiguration, neglect the mechanical latency, or keep the antenna fixed. This paper proposes S-PASS, a star architecture of waveguides sharing one radio-frequency chain through a switch, and pipelined antenna pre-positioning (PAP), a time-division protocol in which idle waveguides pre-position their antennas for their next users while one transmits. It derives in closed form the scheduling efficiency, the number of waveguides beyond which the latency costs no transmission time, and the latency up to which PAP outperforms fixed placement. Analytical and numerical results show that this latency grows with each added waveguide, and users at the outer ends of the waveguides gain most.

items.title: Wave Processing Unit: Closed-Form Matrix Synthesis for Wave Computing in Multiuser MIMO Communications
items.summary: Wave computing offers a compelling route to bypass the latency and energy bottlenecks of digital baseband processing. However, existing wave-domain processors rely on task-specific, non-convex iterative optimization, which incurs substantial configuration overhead and limits real-time applications. In this paper, we propose the wave processing unit (WPU), a programmable planar Mach--Zehnder interferometer (MZI) network that accelerates matrix--vector multiplications in MIMO communications. First, we model the tunable MZI element as a parameterized $2\times2$ unitary transformation, and establish a closed-form synthesis framework for the WPU that decomposes an arbitrary unitary matrix into a cascade of MZI elements arranged in a compact rectangular topology. To handle arbitrary complex-valued operators, we further extend the method through singular value decomposition (SVD) and a hardware-efficient semi-unitary synthesis, avoiding redundant hardware and reducing the compilation complexity. We then apply the WPU to multiuser downlink precoding by an efficient WPU synthesis method, and compare the proposed architecture with hybrid and wave-domain ones. Numerical results demonstrate machine-precision synthesis with negligible residuals for up to $64\times64$ operators, with approximately $380\times$ faster configuration than iterative wave computing baselines. For 64-antenna, 8-user downlink precoding, WPU requires 87.5% fewer RF chains than the fully digital architecture while achieving the same sum rate under ideal hardware. These results highlight the potential of the WPU for precise, hardware-efficient wave-domain processing with rapid configuration.

items.title: A Semi-spontaneous Dutch Speech Dataset for Speech Enhancement and Speech Recognition
items.summary: We present DRES: a 1.5-hour Dutch realistic elicited (semi-spontaneous) speech dataset from 80 speakers recorded in noisy, public indoor environments. DRES was designed as a test set for the evaluation of state-of-the-art (SotA) automatic speech recognition (ASR) and speech enhancement (SE) models in a real-world scenario: a person speaking in a public indoor space with background talkers and noise. The speech was recorded with a four-channel linear microphone array. In this work we evaluate the speech quality of five well-known single-channel SE algorithms and the recognition performance of eight SotA off-the-shelf ASR models before and after applying SE on the speech of DRES. We found that five out of the eight ASR models have WERs lower than 22\% on DRES, despite the challenging conditions. In contrast to recent work, we did not find a positive effect of modern single-channel SE on ASR performance, emphasizing the importance of evaluating in realistic conditions.

items.title: Training-Efficient Channel Estimation for the Multiuser Uplink Relying on Generalized Flexible Intelligent Metasurfaces
items.summary: We consider uplink multiuser channel estimation for a generalized flexible intelligent metasurface at the base station, under narrowband far-field propagation and a twin-time-scale mechanical protocol: on the slow time-scale the panel translates rigidly over a planar grid, while on the fast time-scale the surface morphs along its normal direction. From orthogonal multiuser pilots, we show that each user's channel admits a fourth-order canonical polyadic tensor structure. We develop two complementary estimators: alternating least squares factorization followed by paired rotational-invariance wavevector extraction, and a tensor spatial-smoothing multiple signal classification estimator that preserves the multilinear array manifold. Both share a minimum description length front-end for automatic tensor-rank detection. We derive Kruskal identifiability conditions that relate the numbers of elements, morphing states and grid positions to the maximum number of recoverable multipath components, and show that the tensor model reconstructs the channel at panel configurations beyond the training grid. This prediction capability drives a configuration-selective multiuser transmit precoder that searches the entire motion grid without additional pilot overhead.
